“先让人捧腹大笑，再让人掩卷深思” —— First make people laugh, and then make them think “First make people laugh, and then make them think” — Celebrating 36 Years of Improbable Science

本编年史严格依据搞笑诺贝尔奖官方网站（improbable.com/ig/winners/）历届真实获奖名单与原始学术文献编纂，完整收录 1991年至2026年共36届、357项大奖。每一年均撰写一篇约800字的风趣纪实文章介绍当年各项奇葩研究，并为每一年精选一项代表性成果绘制专属科学幽默配图。 Faithfully compiled from the official Improbable Research archives and primary peer-reviewed literature, this chronicle documents all 36 ceremonies and 357 real Ig Nobel Prizes awarded from 1991 to 2026. Each year features a witty narrative essay introducing every winning study alongside a bespoke editorial science cartoon illustration.

水能记住旧情，氢弹重新定义和平 Water With a Memory and H-Bombs Redefining Peace

1991年首届盛典：当《自然》水记忆奇文、诺奖精子库与垃圾债券之父同台加冕 The 1991 Inaugural Ceremony: Where Sentient H₂O, a Nobel Sperm Bank, and the Junk Bond King Took the Stage

📖 1991年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1991 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1991年金秋，科学幽默杂志《不可思议研究年刊》主编马克·亚伯拉罕斯在麻省理工学院博物馆点燃了第一把荒诞与理性交织的火炬——首届搞笑诺贝尔奖正式横空出世。在这场笑声震天动地的开山盛典上，组委会不仅颁出了七项载入史册的真实大奖，还在元年附赠了三项后来被官方坦承为虚构彩蛋并永久剔除出正统名录的戏仿奖项，由此一举奠定了“初看让人捧腹发笑，细想引人掩卷深思”的评奖圭臬。

在自然科学阵营里，法国免疫学家雅克·本维尼斯特凭一篇震碎《自然》杂志编辑部三观的奇文高票摘得化学奖：他执着地宣称普通的水竟是一种“高智商液体”，哪怕把抗体溶液反复稀释到连半个溶质分子都不复存在，纯水依然拥有刻骨铭心的“水记忆力”，能够记住昔日溶质留下的深情往事。生物学奖颁给了优生学狂热分子罗伯特·克拉克·格雷厄姆，这位自诩的繁衍先知创办了大名鼎鼎的“生殖选择库”，傲慢地规定只接收诺贝尔奖得主与奥运冠军的精子捐赠，妄图用冷冻试管批量孵化人类天才精英。相比之下，医学奖得主艾伦·克利格曼则堪称造福苍生的餐桌活菩萨，他潜心研发的防胀气滴剂“豆乐”能够精准分解豆类多糖，彻底消灭了消化道浊气，将亿万食客从社交场合响屁连天、腹胀如鼓的尴尬深渊中解救出来。

社会与人文领域的四大奖项更是把辛辣讽刺拉到了满格。经济学奖颁给了华尔街呼风唤雨的“垃圾债券之父”迈克尔·米尔肯，致敬这位凭高风险金融魔术让全世界都欠他一笔巨债的资本大鳄；文学奖授予畅销奇书《众神之车》作者埃里希·冯·丹尼肯，感谢这位故事大王脑洞大开地将金字塔等古代文明奇迹统统归功于远古外星宇航员的降临指点。时任美国副总统丹·奎尔因屡次闹出拼写与科学常识笑话，被评委会册封为“消耗时间与占据空间的人”并获颁教育奖，因为他用自身言行比任何人都更雄辩地证明了普及科学教育是何等迫在眉睫；而首届和平奖则颁给了“氢弹之父”兼“星球大战”天基武器系统头号推手爱德华·泰勒——毕竟纵观二十世纪，实在没人比他更卖力地用核威慑重新定义了人类对“和平”二字的理解。

In the autumn of 1991, science humor editor Marc Abrahams and his colleagues gathered at the MIT Museum in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to light a torch of rational absurdity: the inaugural Ig Nobel Prize ceremony had arrived. Conceived to celebrate unusual achievements that 'first make people laugh, and then make them think,' that historic opening night presented seven genuine awards—alongside three tongue-in-cheek prizes for apocryphal achievements that were later officially retired from the canonical archive. Together, they set the gold standard for honoring human endeavours where high ambition collides head-on with unintended comedy, launching a beloved annual academic tradition supported by genuine Nobel laureates that would soon captivate scientists, students, and skeptics around the globe.

Leading the natural sciences, French immunologist Jacques Benveniste—prolific proselytizer and dedicated correspondent of the prestigious journal Nature—captured the Chemistry Prize for his persistent discovery that ordinary water (H₂O) is in fact an 'intelligent liquid.' Through extreme serial dilutions, Benveniste demonstrated to his own complete satisfaction that water is able to remember biological events long after every last trace of the original dissolved antibody molecules has vanished from the test tube. In Biology, selector of seeds and prophet of propagation Robert Klark Graham was honored for his pioneering development of the Repository for Germinal Choice, an elite California sperm bank designed to breed super-geniuses by accepting genetic donations exclusively from Nobel laureates and Olympic champions. Bringing laboratory science back down to the dinner table, Alan Kligerman—celebrated as the deviser of digestive deliverance and vanquisher of vapor—won the Medicine Prize for inventing Beano, the pioneering enzymatic liquid that breaks down complex sugars to prevent bloat, gassiness, gastrointestinal discomfort, and acute social embarrassment after eating beans and legumes.

The social, political, and literary prizes delivered equally razor-sharp satire. Wall Street titan Michael Milken, revered and reviled as the father of the high-yield 'junk bond,' was awarded the Economics Prize as a financial wizard 'to whom the entire world is indebted' while serving time for securities violations. Visionary Swiss raconteur Erich von Däniken claimed the Literature Prize for his best-selling book Chariots of the Gods?, which breathlessly explained how ancient human civilization, pyramids, and monolithic monuments were shaped by visiting astronauts from outer space. In Education, then-U.S. Vice President J. Danforth Quayle—officially cited as a 'consumer of time and occupier of space'—was honored for demonstrating, better than anyone else in public life, the urgent need for science education through his unforgettable public gaffes. Finally, the first-ever Ig Nobel Peace Prize saluted physicist Edward Teller, father of the thermonuclear hydrogen bomb and chief champion of the 'Star Wars' Strategic Defense Initiative weapons system, for his lifelong efforts to permanently change the meaning of peace as we know it through thermonuclear deterrence.

For his persistent discovery that water (H₂O) is an intelligent liquid capable of remembering events long after all trace of those events has vanished.

For his pioneering development of the Repository for Germinal Choice, a sperm bank that accepts donations only from Nobellians and Olympians.

Titan of Wall Street and father of the junk bond, to whom the world is indebted.
#06文学奖Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：埃里希·冯·丹尼肯 (Erich von Däniken)🏅 Winners: Erich von Däniken
撰写《众神之车》，绘声绘色地解释人类古代文明是如何受外太空远古宇航员影响的。
Author of Chariots of the Gods, for explaining how human civilization was influenced by ancient astronauts from outer space.

觉得自己脚臭的人，果真有脚臭 If You Think Your Feet Stink, Science Says They Do

1992年第2届：从资生堂闻臭师、刷掉史前壁画的童子军到每四天发一篇论文的狂人 The 1992 Ceremony: From Shiseido's Foot-Odor Sleuths and Cave-Scrubbing Scouts to a Paper Every 3.9 Days

📖 1992年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1992 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1992年的第二届搞笑诺贝尔奖将聚光灯投向了实验室与日常生活交汇处的荒诞火花。日本横滨资生堂研究中心的神田不二宏、八木荣一郎、福田实、中岛敬介、太田忠男与中田兴亚六位学者勇夺医学奖，他们在《英国皮肤病学杂志》发表了硬核论文《脚臭化学成分的阐明》，动用精密仪器分析鞋袜里的低级脂肪酸后，得出了一个震古烁今的哲学结论：凡是觉得自己有脚臭的人确实有脚臭，觉得自己没有的人就真的没有！化学奖颁给了胶体化学家伊薇特·巴萨，表彰她合成出令小朋友欢呼雀跃的“亮蓝色果冻”，堪称二十世纪人工色素与胶体化学的巅峰结晶；而营养学奖则致敬了斯帕姆午餐肉的广大食客，感谢他们五十四年来不挑食的顽强消化能力。

有些得主靠脑洞封神，有些得主则凭“好心办坏事”与离谱造假载入史册。法国新教童子军组织“法国探路者”本想做件公益好事去清理岩洞里的现代涂鸦，结果少年们干劲太足，操起钢丝刷把布鲁尼凯勒附近梅里耶尔洞穴岩壁上拥有上万年历史的史前远古野牛壁画给刷得干干净净，含泪捧走考古学奖。英国的道格·鲍尔与大卫·乔利两位老汉则摘得物理学奖，他俩承认多年来趁夜潜入麦田用木板和绳子压出几何图案，以“麦田怪圈”为低能物理学界的“场论”做出了字面意义上的画圈贡献。更离谱的是生物学奖得主塞西尔·雅各布森医生，这位生殖诊所专家发明了“单手操作”的精子库质量控制法——偷偷用自己的精子让数十位不知情的女患者受孕，成了名副其实的“造人族长”。

学术圈与公共领域的奇观同样精彩绝伦。莫斯科元素有机化合物研究所的尤里·斯特鲁奇科夫在十年间署名发表了惊人的九百四十八篇科学论文，平均每三点九天就产出一篇，凭一己之力将学术灌水推向极致而斩获文学奖。艺术奖由吉姆·诺尔顿与美国国家艺术基金会共享，前者绘制了经典解剖海报《动物王国的阴茎》，后者竟慷慨拨款资助他将其改造成一本立体翻翻书。经济学奖颁给了拒绝为巨额亏损买单、试图“为灾难本身投保”的伦敦劳合社投资者；和平奖则授予前洛杉矶警察局长达里尔·盖茨，嘲讽他用引发全城大暴动的独特执法手腕，“极具说服力地把各族民众团结在了一起”。

The second Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1992 turned the spotlight on the delightful intersection of meticulous laboratory instrumentation and everyday human folly. Six researchers at the Shiseido Research Center in Yokohama—F. Kanda, E. Yagi, M. Fukuda, K. Nakajima, T. Ohta, and O. Nakata—captured the Medicine Prize for their landmark paper in the British Journal of Dermatology, 'Elucidation of Chemical Compounds Responsible for Foot Malodour.' After analyzing short-chain fatty acids and isovaleric acid from sweaty socks, the team arrived at an immortal philosophical truth: people who think they have foot odor actually do, and those who think they don't, don't. In Chemistry, constructor of colorful colloids Ivette Bassa was celebrated for her decisive role in the crowning achievement of twentieth-century food chemistry: the synthesis of bright blue Jell-O. Meanwhile, the Nutrition Prize saluted the courageous consumers of Spam—utilizers of canned comestibles—for fifty-four years of undiscriminating digestion.

While some laureates triumphed through curiosity, others achieved lasting fame through overzealous blunders or audacious misconduct. The Archaeology Prize was awarded to Éclaireurs de France, a fresh-scrubbed French Protestant youth group whose name translates to 'those who show the way.' Embarking on a well-intentioned mission to scrub modern graffiti off the walls of the Meyrières Cave near the village of Bruniquel, the energetic scouts inadvertently scoured away priceless prehistoric cave paintings of bison dating back more than ten thousand years. In Physics, Englishmen David Chorley and Doug Bower—hailed as lions of low-energy physics—won for their circular contributions to 'field theory' based on the geometrical destruction of English crops, confessing how they had flattened wheat fields at night with planks and ropes to create Britain's famous crop circles. Even more brazen was Biology laureate Dr. Cecil Jacobson, a relentlessly generous fertility specialist who devised a 'simple, single-handed method of quality control' by secretly using his own sperm to impregnate dozens of unsuspecting patients.

Academic hyper-productivity, anatomical art, and institutional hubris completed the 1992 roster. Moscow crystallographer Yuri Struchkov of the Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds won the Literature Prize as an unstoppable author credited with publishing 948 scientific papers between 1981 and 1990—averaging more than one peer-reviewed paper every 3.9 days. The Art Prize went jointly to modern Renaissance man Jim Knowlton for his classic comparative anatomy poster 'Penises of the Animal Kingdom,' and to the U.S. National Endowment for the Arts for encouraging him to extend his work in the form of a pop-up book. Finally, the Economics Prize cited the investors of Lloyd's of London—heirs to 300 years of dull, prudent management—for their bold attempt to insure disaster by refusing to pay for their company's catastrophic losses, while former Los Angeles Police Chief Daryl Gates received the Peace Prize for his 'uniquely compelling methods of bringing people together.'

1992年的第二届搞笑诺贝尔奖将聚光灯投向了实验室与日常生活交汇处的荒诞火花。日本横滨资生堂研究中心的神田不二宏、八木荣一郎、福田实、中岛敬介、太田忠男与中田兴亚六位学者勇夺医学奖，他们在《英国皮肤病学杂志》发表了硬核论文《脚臭化学成分的阐明》，动用精密仪器分析鞋袜里的低级脂肪酸后，得出了一个震古烁今的哲学结论：凡是觉得自己有脚臭的人确实有脚臭，觉得自己没有的人就真的没有！化学奖颁给了胶体化学家伊薇特·巴萨，表彰她合成出令小朋友欢呼雀跃的“亮蓝色果冻”，堪称二十世纪人工色素与胶体化学的巅峰结晶；而营养学奖则致敬了斯帕姆午餐肉的广大食客，感谢他们五十四年来不挑食的顽强消化能力。

The second Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1992 turned the spotlight on the delightful intersection of meticulous laboratory instrumentation and everyday human folly. Six researchers at the Shiseido Research Center in Yokohama—F. Kanda, E. Yagi, M. Fukuda, K. Nakajima, T. Ohta, and O. Nakata—captured the Medicine Prize for their landmark paper in the British Journal of Dermatology, 'Elucidation of Chemical Compounds Responsible for Foot Malodour.' After analyzing short-chain fatty acids and isovaleric acid from sweaty socks, the team arrived at an immortal philosophical truth: people who think they have foot odor actually do, and those who think they don't, don't. In Chemistry, constructor of colorful colloids Ivette Bassa was celebrated for her decisive role in the crowning achievement of twentieth-century food chemistry: the synthesis of bright blue Jell-O. Meanwhile, the Nutrition Prize saluted the courageous consumers of Spam—utilizers of canned comestibles—for fifty-four years of undiscriminating digestion.

有些得主靠脑洞封神，有些得主则凭“好心办坏事”与离谱造假载入史册。法国新教童子军组织“法国探路者”本想做件公益好事去清理岩洞里的现代涂鸦，结果少年们干劲太足，操起钢丝刷把布鲁尼凯勒附近梅里耶尔洞穴岩壁上拥有上万年历史的史前远古野牛壁画给刷得干干净净，含泪捧走考古学奖。英国的道格·鲍尔与大卫·乔利两位老汉则摘得物理学奖，他俩承认多年来趁夜潜入麦田用木板和绳子压出几何图案，以“麦田怪圈”为低能物理学界的“场论”做出了字面意义上的画圈贡献。更离谱的是生物学奖得主塞西尔·雅各布森医生，这位生殖诊所专家发明了“单手操作”的精子库质量控制法——偷偷用自己的精子让数十位不知情的女患者受孕，成了名副其实的“造人族长”。

While some laureates triumphed through curiosity, others achieved lasting fame through overzealous blunders or audacious misconduct. The Archaeology Prize was awarded to Éclaireurs de France, a fresh-scrubbed French Protestant youth group whose name translates to 'those who show the way.' Embarking on a well-intentioned mission to scrub modern graffiti off the walls of the Meyrières Cave near the village of Bruniquel, the energetic scouts inadvertently scoured away priceless prehistoric cave paintings of bison dating back more than ten thousand years. In Physics, Englishmen David Chorley and Doug Bower—hailed as lions of low-energy physics—won for their circular contributions to 'field theory' based on the geometrical destruction of English crops, confessing how they had flattened wheat fields at night with planks and ropes to create Britain's famous crop circles. Even more brazen was Biology laureate Dr. Cecil Jacobson, a relentlessly generous fertility specialist who devised a 'simple, single-handed method of quality control' by secretly using his own sperm to impregnate dozens of unsuspecting patients.

学术圈与公共领域的奇观同样精彩绝伦。莫斯科元素有机化合物研究所的尤里·斯特鲁奇科夫在十年间署名发表了惊人的九百四十八篇科学论文，平均每三点九天就产出一篇，凭一己之力将学术灌水推向极致而斩获文学奖。艺术奖由吉姆·诺尔顿与美国国家艺术基金会共享，前者绘制了经典解剖海报《动物王国的阴茎》，后者竟慷慨拨款资助他将其改造成一本立体翻翻书。经济学奖颁给了拒绝为巨额亏损买单、试图“为灾难本身投保”的伦敦劳合社投资者；和平奖则授予前洛杉矶警察局长达里尔·盖茨，嘲讽他用引发全城大暴动的独特执法手腕，“极具说服力地把各族民众团结在了一起”。

Moscow crystallographer Yuri Struchkov of the Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds won the Literature Prize as an unstoppable author credited with publishing 948 scientific papers between 1981 and 1990—averaging more than one peer-reviewed paper every 3.9 days. The Art Prize went jointly to modern Renaissance man Jim Knowlton for his classic comparative anatomy poster 'Penises of the Animal Kingdom,' and to the U.S. National Endowment for the Arts for encouraging him to extend his work in the form of a pop-up book. Finally, the Economics Prize cited the investors of Lloyd's of London—heirs to 300 years of dull, prudent management—for their bold attempt to insure disaster by refusing to pay for their company's catastrophic losses, while former Los Angeles Police Chief Daryl Gates received the Peace Prize for his 'uniquely compelling methods of bringing people together.'

带猪飙车测排菌，千人合写十页文 Joy-Riding Pigs, Zipper Emergencies, and 976 Authors on Ten Pages

1993年第3届：从拉链卡住命根子的急救指南、母鸡冷聚变到戈尔巴乔夫的敌基督概率 The 1993 Ceremony: Chicken Cold Fusion, Dashboard TVs, and the Exact Odds That Gorbachev Is the Antichrist

📖 1993年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1993 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1993年的第三届搞笑诺贝尔奖一口气颁出十一项大奖，堪称奇葩学术研究的满汉全席。生物学奖得主保罗·威廉姆斯与肯尼思·纽厄尔化身为追踪猪粪的生物侦探，发表了妙趣横生的《兜风生猪的沙门氏菌排泄情况》，严肃论证生猪坐车兜风时的旅途颠簸与紧张兴奋如何显著促进沙门氏菌排泄。医学奖则让天下男士闻之双腿一紧：詹姆斯·诺兰、托马斯·斯蒂尔韦尔与约翰·桑兹三位急诊科好人凭借《拉链卡住阴茎的急性处理》获奖，为这一火烧眉毛的男科惨剧提供了用骨剪剪断拉链滑块横梁的无痛解救方案。而文学奖则颁给了埃里克·托波尔等四位领衔学者及其多达九百七十二名共同作者——他们在《新英格兰医学杂志》发表了一篇仅十页的心肌梗死溶栓论文，作者人数竟是页数的整整一百倍！

在科学与伪科学的跨界地带，各路奇人异士更是大显神通。哈佛医学院的约翰·麦克与天普大学的大卫·雅各布斯共享心理学奖，他们经过深度访谈后跳跃性地断言：那些相信自己被外星人绑架的人八成真被绑架过，而且“外星人绑架地球人的核心目的是为了繁衍后代”。法国学者路易·凯尔夫兰凭一腔炼金术热情摘得物理学奖，他信誓旦旦地宣称母鸡能在体内通过“生物冷聚变”过程，把吃进去的钾和硅凭空转化为鸡蛋壳里的钙质。南卡罗来纳州的罗伯特·费德则将统计学用到了神学极致，他精确算出苏联前领导人戈尔巴乔夫是“敌基督”的概率高达七十一亿亿分之一，一举斩获数学奖。

商业与技术发明同样令人拍案叫绝。深夜电视购物大王罗恩·波佩尔凭切菜神器、口袋钓鱼竿、麦克风先生以及“蛋壳内搅蛋器”重新定义了工业革命，荣膺消费工程学奖；发明家杰伊·希夫曼因造出让司机边开车边看电视的投影设备，与居然投票立法批准该设备的密歇根州议会共享前瞻技术奖；田纳西州的坎贝尔兄弟则因发明夹在杂志书页间、熏得读者直打喷嚏的“香水试纸条”拿到化学奖。此外，经济学家拉维·巴特拉靠狂销畅销书《1990年大萧条》“凭一己之力阻止了全球经济崩溃”而获经济学奖；菲律宾百事可乐公司则因瓶盖抽奖报错中奖号码，瞬间激怒并团结了八十万名持盖民众，让原本敌对的各路派系首次同仇敌忾，荒诞摘得和平奖。

Expanding to eleven eclectic categories, the third Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1993 served up a grand banquet of unforgettable empirical inquiries. In Biology, bold biological detectives Paul Williams Jr. of the Oregon State Health Division and Kenneth W. Newell of the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine were honored for their pioneering public-health investigation, 'Salmonella Excretion in Joy-Riding Pigs,' which carefully tracked how taking swine out for a vehicular spin triggers bacterial shedding. The Medicine Prize made men everywhere wince in instant sympathy: medical men of mercy James F. Nolan, Thomas J. Stillwell, and John P. Sands Jr. won for their painstaking emergency-room report, 'Acute Management of the Zipper-Entrapped Penis,' detailing how to rescue patients by snipping the zipper's median bar. Meanwhile, the Literature Prize went to Eric Topol, R. Califf, F. Van de Werf, P. W. Armstrong, and their 972 co-authors from fifteen countries for publishing a ten-page cardiology paper in The New England Journal of Medicine that featured one hundred times as many authors as pages.

On the wild frontier between bold speculation, alchemy, and apocalyptic statistics, three prizes stood out. Harvard Medical School psychiatrist John Mack and Temple University historian David Jacobs shared the Psychology Prize as mental visionaries for their leaping conclusion that people who believe they were kidnapped by aliens from outer space probably were—and especially for their clinical deduction that 'the focus of the abduction is the production of children.' In Physics, French alchemical admirer Louis Kervran was cited for his conclusion that the calcium in chickens' eggshells is created inside the hen by a biological process of cold fusion. Not to be outdone in mathematical rigor, farsighted statistical seer Robert Faid of Greenville, South Carolina, captured the Mathematics Prize for calculating the exact odds—710,609,175,188,282,000 to 1—that former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev is the Antichrist.

Commercial ingenuity, legislative madness, and corporate blunders provided the final fireworks of 1993. Incessant inventor and late-night television pitchman Ron Popeil won the Consumer Engineering Prize for redefining the industrial revolution with devices such as the Veg-O-Matic, the Pocket Fisherman, Mr. Microphone, and the Inside-the-Shell Egg Scrambler. The Visionary Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Michigan inventor Jay Schiffman for creating AutoVision—a head-up projection device that makes it possible to drive a car and watch television at the same time—and to the Michigan state legislature for making it legal to do so. Brothers James and Gaines Campbell of Lookout Mountain, Tennessee, took Chemistry for inventing magazine perfume scent strips, while Southern Methodist University economist Ravi Batra won Economics for selling enough copies of his best-sellers The Great Depression of 1990 ($17.95) and Surviving the Great Depression of 1990 ($18.95) to single-handedly prevent worldwide economic collapse. Finally, Pepsi-Cola of the Philippines won the Peace Prize for announcing the wrong winning number in a millionaire contest, inciting and uniting 800,000 riotously expectant winners and bringing warring factions together for the first time in their nation's history.

1993年的第三届搞笑诺贝尔奖一口气颁出十一项大奖，堪称奇葩学术研究的满汉全席。生物学奖得主保罗·威廉姆斯与肯尼思·纽厄尔化身为追踪猪粪的生物侦探，发表了妙趣横生的《兜风生猪的沙门氏菌排泄情况》，严肃论证生猪坐车兜风时的旅途颠簸与紧张兴奋如何显著促进沙门氏菌排泄。医学奖则让天下男士闻之双腿一紧：詹姆斯·诺兰、托马斯·斯蒂尔韦尔与约翰·桑兹三位急诊科好人凭借《拉链卡住阴茎的急性处理》获奖，为这一火烧眉毛的男科惨剧提供了用骨剪剪断拉链滑块横梁的无痛解救方案。而文学奖则颁给了埃里克·托波尔等四位领衔学者及其多达九百七十二名共同作者——他们在《新英格兰医学杂志》发表了一篇仅十页的心肌梗死溶栓论文，作者人数竟是页数的整整一百倍！

商业与技术发明同样令人拍案叫绝。深夜电视购物大王罗恩·波佩尔凭切菜神器、口袋钓鱼竿、麦克风先生以及“蛋壳内搅蛋器”重新定义了工业革命，荣膺消费工程学奖；发明家杰伊·希夫曼因造出让司机边开车边看电视的投影设备，与居然投票立法批准该设备的密歇根州议会共享前瞻技术奖；田纳西州的坎贝尔兄弟则因发明夹在杂志书页间、熏得读者直打喷嚏的“香水试纸条”拿到化学奖。此外，经济学家拉维·巴特拉靠狂销畅销书《1990年大萧条》“凭一己之力阻止了全球经济崩溃”而获经济学奖；菲律宾百事可乐公司则因瓶盖抽奖报错中奖号码，瞬间激怒并团结了八十万名持盖民众，让原本敌对的各路派系首次同仇敌忾，荒诞摘得和平奖。

Commercial ingenuity, legislative madness, and corporate blunders provided the final fireworks of 1993. Incessant inventor and late-night television pitchman Ron Popeil won the Consumer Engineering Prize for redefining the industrial revolution with devices such as the Veg-O-Matic, the Pocket Fisherman, Mr. Microphone, and the Inside-the-Shell Egg Scrambler. The Visionary Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Michigan inventor Jay Schiffman for creating AutoVision—a head-up projection device that makes it possible to drive a car and watch television at the same time—and to the Michigan state legislature for making it legal to do so. Brothers James and Gaines Campbell of Lookout Mountain, Tennessee, took Chemistry for inventing magazine perfume scent strips, while Southern Methodist University economist Ravi Batra won Economics for selling enough copies of his best-sellers The Great Depression of 1990 ($17.95) and Surviving the Great Depression of 1990 ($18.95) to single-handedly prevent worldwide economic collapse. Finally, Pepsi-Cola of the Philippines won the Peace Prize for announcing the wrong winning number in a millionaire contest, inciting and uniting 800,000 riotously expectant winners and bringing warring factions together for the first time in their nation's history.

在百万富翁抽奖中报错中奖号码，激怒并团结了80万名准百万富翁，令该国敌对派系首次携手。
For announcing the wrong winning number in a millionaire contest, uniting 800,000 riotously expectant winners and bringing warring factions together.

🏅 获奖者：杰伊·希夫曼 (Jay Schiffman) 与密歇根州议会🏅 Winners: Jay Schiffman and the Michigan State Legislature
前者发明让司机边开车边看电视的投影设备AutoVision，后者投票通过法律使其合法化。

发明了把香水涂在杂志书页间、令读者避之不及的“香味试纸条”（scent strips）。
Dedicated deliverers of fragrance, for inventing scent strips, the odious method by which perfume is applied to magazine pages.
#08文学奖Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：埃里克·托波尔 (Eric Topol) 等四人及其972名共同作者🏅 Winners: Eric Topol, R. Califf, F. Van de Werf, P. W. Armstrong, and 972 Co-Authors
发表了一篇作者人数是论文页数整整一百倍的医学研究论文。
For publishing a medical research paper in NEJM that has one hundred times as many authors as pages.

精确计算出戈尔巴乔夫是“敌基督”的概率为 710,609,175,188,282,000 比 1。
Farsighted seer of statistics, for calculating the exact odds (710,609,175,188,282,000 to 1) that Mikhail Gorbachev is the Antichrist.

断言鸡蛋壳里的钙质是由母鸡体内的“生物冷聚变”过程转化生成的。
Ardent admirer of alchemy, for his conclusion that the calcium in chickens' eggshells is created by a process of cold fusion.

🏅 获奖者：詹姆斯·诺兰 (James F. Nolan)、托马斯·斯蒂尔韦尔与约翰·桑兹🏅 Winners: James F. Nolan, Thomas J. Stillwell, and John P. Sands Jr.
发表令人肉痛的急诊医学报告《拉链卡住阴茎的急性处理》。
Medical men of mercy, for their painstaking research report 'Acute Management of the Zipper-Entrapped Penis.'

火花塞电嘴治蛇咬，猫耳螨塞进自己耳 Sparkplugs on a Snakebitten Lip and Cat Ear Mites in a Vet's Own Ear

1994年第4届：硬核自残实验、驻外美军便秘普查与一指头亏掉智利千分之五国力的交易员 The 1994 Ceremony: Self-Experimentation, Constipated Troops, and the Trader Who Botched 0.5% of Chile's GNP

📖 1994年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1994 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1994年的第四届搞笑诺贝尔奖堪称人类“硬核自残与迷之执着”的巅峰大赏（官方事后还严谨地剔除了一项源于失实媒体报道的乌龙奖项，保留九项真凭实据的传世杰作）。医学奖破天荒一分为二：前美国海军陆战队员“X患者”在被自家宠物响尾蛇咬伤嘴唇后，深信民间电击解毒偏方，执意让邻居把汽车火花塞电线夹在自己嘴唇上，将汽车引擎轰到每分钟三千转整整电击了五分钟；而理查德·达特与理查德·古斯塔夫森两位急诊专家则因将这一惨烈抢救写成论文《电击疗法治疗响尾蛇咬伤的失败》共同获奖。同样对自己下狠手的还有纽约兽医罗伯特·洛佩兹，他为了弄清猫耳螨会不会传染给人，亲自从猫耳朵里掏出耳螨塞进自己耳道，悉心体验并记录奇痒难耐的全过程，实至名归地捧走昆虫学奖。

军旅与政坛的入选者则展示了另类的数据控与管理术。布赖恩·斯威尼等四位美军军医凭《便秘的军人：驻外美军中的患病率》摘得生物学奖，他们深入战地对前线美军官兵的排便频率进行了极其详尽的统计学摸底。心理学奖颁给了新加坡前总理李光耀，表彰他长达三十年对三百万新加坡公民一旦吐痰、嚼口香糖或喂鸽子就予以重罚的“负强化心理学”大型社会实验。得克萨斯州参议员鲍勃·格拉斯哥则因在1989年推动一项奇葩禁毒法案荣膺化学奖——该法案规定公民未经官方许可购买烧杯、烧瓶或试管等实验室玻璃器皿统统违法，差点把全州中学化学老师送进警察局。

至于宗教、玄学与金融领域的跨界表现，更是让人啼笑皆非。玛赫西大学的物理学家约翰·哈格林宣称召集四千名受训冥想者集体发功，成功让华盛顿特区的暴力犯罪率下降了百分之十八，由此获颁和平奖；阿拉巴马州美南浸信会运用数学模型逐县估算全州有多少公民如果不悔改就会下地狱，摘得数学奖；山达基教创始人兼科幻作家罗恩·哈伯德则凭那本为自己赚得盆满钵满的畅销书《戴尼提》获追授文学奖。而经济学奖得主、智利国家铜业公司交易员胡安·巴勃罗·达维拉则上演了史诗级手滑：他在电脑上把“卖出”误敲成“买入”，随后为补窟窿疯狂加仓，最终亏掉智利国民生产总值的千分之五，还让智利人用他的名字造出了新动词“达维拉尔”（意为“把事情彻底搞砸”）。

The fourth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1994 stood as a monument to heroic self-experimentation and stubborn human persistence—comprising nine verified prizes after one award based on erroneous press accounts was officially removed. The Medicine Prize was presented in two unforgettable parts: first to 'Patient X,' a valiant former U.S. Marine who, after suffering a venomous bite on the lip from his pet rattlesnake, insisted on attaching automobile sparkplug wires to his lip while the car engine was revved to 3,000 rpm for five minutes; and second to Drs. Richard C. Dart of the Rocky Mountain Poison Center and Richard A. Gustafson of the University of Arizona for their well-grounded clinical report, 'Failure of Electric Shock Treatment for Rattlesnake Envenomation.' Matching that personal sacrifice, veterinarian Robert A. Lopez of Westport, New York—friend of all creatures great and small—won the Entomology Prize for extracting ear mites from cats, inserting them into his own ear canal, and carefully observing and analyzing the resulting torment in 'Of Mites and Man.'

Military logistics, behavioral conditioning, and legislative logic also earned top honors in 1994. Four military physicians—W. Brian Sweeney, Brian Krafte-Jacobs, Jeffrey W. Britton, and Wayne Hansen—won the Biology Prize for their breakthrough study in Military Medicine, 'The Constipated Serviceman: Prevalence Among Deployed US Troops,' featuring an exhaustive numerical analysis of bowel-movement frequency on the front lines. In Psychology, former Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew of Singapore was recognized as a master practitioner of the psychology of negative reinforcement for his thirty-year empirical study of the effects of punishing three million citizens whenever they spat, chewed gum, or fed pigeons. Meanwhile, Texas State Senator Bob Glasgow captured the Chemistry Prize as a wise writer of logical legislation for sponsoring a 1989 drug-control law that made it illegal to purchase beakers, flasks, test tubes, or other laboratory glassware without a permit.

Spiritual statistics, profitable prose, and financial catastrophe completed the 1994 chronicle. Physicist John Hagelin of Maharishi University and the Institute of Science, Technology and Public Policy received the Peace Prize as a promulgator of peaceful thoughts for his experimental conclusion that 4,000 trained meditators caused an 18 percent decrease in violent crime in Washington, D.C. The Mathematics Prize went to the Southern Baptist Church of Alabama—mathematical measurers of morality—for their county-by-county estimate of how many Alabama citizens will go to Hell if they do not repent, while science-fiction author and Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard won Literature for his crackling Good Book Dianetics, which proved highly profitable to mankind or to a portion thereof. Finally, tireless Chilean futures trader Juan Pablo Dávila of the state-owned Codelco company won Economics for instructing his computer to 'buy' when he meant 'sell,' and subsequently attempting to recoup his losses with increasingly unprofitable trades that lost 0.5 percent of Chile's gross national product—inspiring his countrymen to coin the verb 'davilar,' meaning 'to botch things up royally.'

把从猫耳朵里取出的耳螨塞进自己耳道里，亲自观察、记录并分析人感染猫耳螨的结果。
Valiant veterinarian, for obtaining ear mites from cats, inserting them into his own ear, and carefully observing and analyzing the results.

开展长达三十年的负强化心理学研究，对三百万新加坡公民每逢吐痰、嚼口香糖或喂鸽子即予以处罚。

科幻作家兼山达基教创始人，撰写出对人类（或其中一部分人）利润丰厚的畅销书《戴尼提》。
Author of science fiction and founding father of Scientology, for his crackling book Dianetics, which is highly profitable to mankind or a portion thereof.
#07化学奖Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：得克萨斯州参议员鲍勃·格拉斯哥 (Bob Glasgow)🏅 Winners: Texas State Senator Bob Glasgow
发起1989年禁毒法，规定未经许可购买烧杯、烧瓶、试管等实验室玻璃器皿均属违法。
For sponsoring the 1989 drug control law making it illegal to purchase beakers, flasks, test tubes, or other laboratory glassware without a permit.
#08经济学奖Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：胡安·巴勃罗·达维拉 (Juan Pablo Dávila)🏅 Winners: Juan Pablo Dávila (Codelco, Chile)
误把期货指令“卖出”输成“买入”，试图翻本却最终亏掉智利GNP的0.5%，催生新动词“davilar”（彻底搞砸）。
For instructing his computer to 'buy' when he meant 'sell' and losing 0.5% of Chile's GNP, inspiring the new verb 'davilar' ('to botch things up royally').
#09数学奖Mathematics Prize
🏅 获奖者：阿拉巴马州美南浸信会 (The Southern Baptist Church of Alabama)🏅 Winners: The Southern Baptist Church of Alabama
运用数学方法逐县精确估算：如果阿拉巴马州公民不悔改，全州究竟有多少人会下地狱。
Mathematical measurers of morality, for their county-by-county estimate of how many Alabama citizens will go to Hell if they do not repent.
1995 第5届搞笑诺贝尔奖 5th Ig Nobel Prize 1990s 📝 正文 856 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 485 words · 10 Prizes

鸽子鉴赏毕加索，湿内裤勇闯严寒 Art-Critic Pigeons, Soggy Cereal Physics, and Wet Underwear in the Cold

1995年第5届：猫屎咖啡端上餐桌、直肠异物百科全书与不含核酸的三螺旋香水 The 1995 Ceremony: Civet-Excreted Coffee, an Encyclopedia of Rectal Foreign Bodies, and DNA-Free Triple-Helix Perfume

📖 1995年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1995 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1995年10月，第五届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院首次实现全球网络直播，十项大奖将学术界的猎奇求知欲展现得淋漓尽致。日本庆应义塾大学的渡边茂、坂本淳子与胁田真纯团队荣膺心理学奖，他们通过麻籽投喂奖励，成功训练鸽子精准分辨莫奈的印象派风景与毕加索的立体派画作，证明鸟类的艺术鉴赏力绝不含糊。英国诺里奇食品研究所的乔治特、帕克与史密斯三位学者则将力学武器对准早餐碗，发表《含水量对早餐麦片压实行为影响的研究》，因严谨分析脆麦片泡软塌陷的物理过程而摘得物理学奖；亚特兰大商人约翰·马丁内斯则因向世界推广由印尼椰子猫吞食咖啡果并排泄出的昂贵“猫屎咖啡”获颁营养学奖。

人体奥秘与日常微末小事同样逃不过科学家们的法眼。威斯康星州的医学专家大卫·布什与詹姆斯·斯塔林凭借《直肠异物：病例报告与世界文献综合评述》勇夺文学奖，这篇旷世综述宛如一部人类菊部收纳百科全书，记录了七个灯泡、磨刀器、两把电筒、塞着土豆的油壶、珠宝锯、冰冻猪尾巴，甚至还有一位患者体内同时藏着眼镜、行李箱钥匙、烟草袋和一本杂志的惊人“四件套”收藏！挪威与丹麦学者玛莎·巴克维格和露丝·尼尔森因深入研究《寒冷环境下湿内裤对体温调节反应及热舒适度的影响》获颁公共卫生奖；玛西亚·比贝尔、大卫·尚纳霍夫与迈克尔·博伊尔三人凭研究堵住单侧鼻孔呼吸如何影响大脑认知摘得医学奖；牙医罗伯特·博蒙特则靠调查《患者对打蜡与未打蜡牙线的偏好》拿下牙医学奖。

在商业、金融与政坛领域，讽刺火力更是全开。比佛利山庄的设计师比扬·帕克扎德推出了大名鼎鼎的“基因古龙水”与“基因香水”——妙就妙在这款香水里既不含一丁点脱氧核糖核酸，瓶身还被设计成了违背双螺旋常识的“三螺旋”造型，毫无悬念地拿下化学奖。经济学奖由搞垮百年巴林银行的魔鬼交易员尼克·里森及其上司，与令加州奥兰治县破产的罗伯特·西特龙共享，感谢他们用金融衍生品微积分证明了“任何金融机构都是有极限的”。而和平奖则颁给了台湾立法院，表彰议员们用拳打脚踢、飞身锁喉的议场全武行向世界证明：政客互殴比对外发动战争划算多了。

Broadcast live over the internet from Harvard's Sanders Theatre for the very first time on October 6, 1995, the fifth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony showcased ten triumphs of unbridled scholarly curiosity. In Psychology, Shigeru Watanabe, Junko Sakamoto, and Masumi Wakita of Keio University in Tokyo won for training pigeons to peck keys that discriminated between the impressionist paintings of Claude Monet and the cubist canvases of Pablo Picasso—demonstrating that birds rewarded with hemp seeds can master modern art history. In Physics, D.M.R. Georget, R. Parker, and A.C. Smith of the Institute of Food Research in Norwich, England, were honored for their rigorous mechanical analysis of soggy breakfast cereal, published in Powder Technology as 'A Study of the Effects of Water Content on the Compaction Behaviour of Breakfast Cereal Flakes.' Meanwhile, Atlanta coffee merchant John Martinez claimed the Nutrition Prize for educating the world about Luak Coffee—the world's most expensive brew, made from coffee beans ingested and excreted by the Indonesian palm civet (the luak).

Anatomical audacity and everyday bodily discomfort dominated the medical and health categories. Surgeons David B. Busch and James R. Starling of Madison, Wisconsin, captured the Literature Prize for their deeply penetrating review in the journal Surgery, 'Rectal Foreign Bodies: Case Reports and a Comprehensive Review of the World's Literature.' Their scholarly citations cataloged an unforgettable inventory of extracted items: seven light bulbs, a knife sharpener, two flashlights, a wire spring, a snuff box, an oil can with a potato stopper, eleven forms of fruits and vegetables, a jeweler's saw, a frozen pig's tail, a tin cup, a beer glass, and one patient's remarkable ensemble collection consisting of spectacles, a suitcase key, a tobacco pouch, and a magazine. In Public Health, Martha Kold Bakkevig of Sintef Unimed in Norway and Ruth Nielsen of the Technical University of Denmark won for their exhaustive study, 'Impact of Wet Underwear on Thermoregulatory Responses and Thermal Comfort in the Cold.' Medicine honored Marcia E. Buebel, David S. Shannahoff-Khalsa, and Michael R. Boyle for 'The Effects of Unilateral Forced Nostril Breathing on Cognition,' while Minnesota dentist Robert H. Beaumont took Dentistry for his incisive study, 'Patient Preference for Waxed or Unwaxed Dental Floss.'

Commercial chemistry, high-stakes finance, and parliamentary brawling closed out the 1995 celebration. Beverly Hills fashion designer Bijan Pakzad won the Chemistry Prize for creating DNA Cologne and DNA Perfume—neither of which contains a single trace of deoxyribonucleic acid, and both of which come packaged in a biologically impossible triple-helix bottle. The Economics Prize was awarded jointly to rogue trader Nick Leeson and his superiors at Barings Bank, and to Orange County, California treasurer Robert Citron, for using the calculus of financial derivatives to demonstrate that every financial institution has its limits. Finally, the Taiwan National Parliament received the Peace Prize for demonstrating that politicians gain far more by punching, kicking, and gouging each other inside the legislature than by waging war against other nations.

For his incisive clinical study 'Patient Preference for Waxed or Unwaxed Dental Floss.'

For creating DNA Cologne and DNA Perfume, neither of which contains deoxyribonucleic acid, and both of which come in a triple-helix bottle.
1996 第6届搞笑诺贝尔奖 6th Ig Nobel Prize 1990s 📝 正文 853 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 493 words · 10 Prizes

黄油吐司必朝下，液氧三秒炸烤架 Butter-Side-Down Toast and a Three-Second Liquid-Oxygen Barbecue

1996年第6届：宇宙常数决定的墨菲定律、喝啤酒吃大蒜的水蛭与索卡尔学术恶搞事件 The 1996 Ceremony: Cosmic Murphy's Law, Beer-Loving Leeches, Mini-Princess Fossils, and the Sokal Hoax

📖 1996年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1996 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1996年的第六届搞笑诺贝尔奖将科学实验的狂野与冷幽默推上了新高度。英国阿斯顿大学物理学家罗伯特·马修斯凭《翻滚的吐司、墨菲定律与基本常数》摘得物理学奖：他严密推导出，受地球引力与宇宙基本常数决定的人类身高及餐桌高度所限，吐司从桌边滑落时刚好只来得及在空中翻转半圈，因此涂黄油的那一面总是宿命般地朝下拍在地毯上！如果说马修斯揭示了餐桌上的宿命，普渡大学的乔治·戈布尔则用暴力化学重塑了后院烧烤：他把液态氧直接浇在木炭上，创下三秒钟点燃烧烤架（顺便把烤架炸飞）的世界纪录，火热捧走化学奖。挪威卑尔根大学的安德斯·巴海姆与霍格纳·桑德维克则因测试《麦芽酒、大蒜与酸奶油对水蛭食欲的影响》获颁生物学奖。

医学、公卫与生物多样性奖项则充满了荒诞剧色彩。格陵兰与挪威医生埃伦·克莱斯特和哈拉尔·莫伊发表了令人瞠目的医学报告《通过充气娃娃传播的淋病》，追踪了一起在远洋渔船船员间因共用充气娃娃而引发的离奇感染，斩获公共卫生奖；布法罗大学的罗伯特·真科医生则因发现“缺钱带来的财务压力是破坏性牙周病的高危指标”而拿到经济学奖。日本名古屋的冈村长之助更是脑洞清奇，他在石灰岩薄片里看图说话，宣称发现了长度不足百分之一英寸的微型恐龙、微型马、微型飞龙乃至“微型公主”等上千种远古微缩化石，独揽生物多样性奖；而马萨诸塞州的唐·费瑟斯通则因发明风靡全美草坪的“粉红塑料火烈鸟”荣膺艺术奖。

年度最辛辣的三记耳光分别扇向了学界、商界与政界。文化研究名刊《社会文本》的编辑们获颁文学奖，因为他们兴高采烈地发表了物理学家艾伦·索卡尔蓄意杜撰的恶搞论文《超越界限：迈向引力量子力学的变革性诠释学》——编辑们自己根本看不懂，作者事后坦言全文胡扯，文中甚至宣称“客观现实并不存在”。医学奖颁给了雷诺、菲利普·莫里斯等七大烟草公司的总裁高管，嘲讽他们在美国国会听证会上集体发誓作证的“伟大医学发现”：尼古丁绝对不会让人上瘾！和平奖则授予法国总统雅克·希拉克，表彰他在广岛原子弹爆炸五十周年之际，居然选择在太平洋引爆一连串核试验来“隆重纪念”和平。

The sixth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre in October 1996 elevated deadpan theoretical physics and explosive backyard chemistry to new heights. British physicist Robert Matthews of Aston University captured the Physics Prize for his European Journal of Physics paper, 'Tumbling Toast, Murphy's Law and the Fundamental Constants.' Matthews rigorously demonstrated that because the height of a dining table is governed by human stature—which is itself constrained by chemical bonds and the fundamental constants of the universe—a slice of toast sliding over the table's edge only has time to complete half a somersault before hitting the carpet, dooming the buttered side to land face-down! If Matthews explained breakfast tragedy, Purdue University engineer George Goble perfected backyard pyrotechnics: he won the Chemistry Prize for igniting a charcoal barbecue grill in a blistering world-record time of three seconds using liquid oxygen. Meanwhile, Norwegian researchers Anders Bærheim and Hogne Sandvik of the University of Bergen took the Biology Prize for their tasty and tasteful report in the British Medical Journal, 'Effect of Ale, Garlic, and Soured Cream on the Appetite of Leeches.'

Medical caution, dental economics, and microscopic pareidolia defined the middle slate of awards. Physicians Ellen Kleist of Nuuk, Greenland, and Harald Moi of Oslo, Norway, received the Public Health Prize for their cautionary medical case report in Genitourinary Medicine, 'Transmission of Gonorrhea Through an Inflatable Doll,' tracing a bizarre venereal infection aboard a fishing vessel. At the University at Buffalo, Dr. Robert J. Genco won the Economics Prize for his discovery that 'financial strain is a risk indicator for destructive periodontal disease'—proving that money stress can literally cost you your gums and teeth. The Biodiversity Prize honored Chonosuke Okamura of the Okamura Fossil Laboratory in Nagoya, Japan, who peered into polished limestone and claimed to discover the fossils of dinosaurs, horses, dragons, princesses, and more than 1,000 other extinct 'mini-species,' each measuring less than one-hundredth of an inch in length. In Art, Don Featherstone of Fitchburg, Massachusetts, was celebrated for his ornamentally evolutionary invention: the plastic pink flamingo.

The sharpest satirical barbs of 1996 were reserved for postmodern academia, Big Tobacco, and nuclear diplomacy. The editors of the journal Social Text won the Literature Prize for eagerly publishing physicist Alan Sokal's deliberate parody paper, 'Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity'—research that the editors could not understand, that the author said was meaningless, and which claimed that physical reality does not exist. The Medicine Prize was presented to seven tobacco executives—James Johnston of R.J. Reynolds, Joseph Taddeo of U.S. Tobacco, Andrew Tisch of Lorillard, William Campbell of Philip Morris, Edward A. Horrigan of Liggett Group, Donald S. Johnston of American Tobacco, and the late Thomas E. Sandefur Jr. of Brown & Williamson—for their unshakable discovery, as testified to the U.S. Congress, that nicotine is not addictive. Finally, French President Jacques Chirac received the Peace Prize for commemorating the fiftieth anniversary of Hiroshima with atomic bomb tests in the Pacific.

For their tasty and tasteful report 'Effect of Ale, Garlic, and Soured Cream on the Appetite of Leeches.'

表彰他们在美国国会听证会上坚定不移地宣誓作证：“尼古丁不会让人上瘾”。

对墨菲定律进行物理学研究，从宇宙基本常数出发证明烤吐司掉下桌子时黄油面往往朝下。
For his studies of Murphy's Law, and especially for demonstrating that toast often falls on the buttered side.

🏅 获奖者：法国总统雅克·希拉克 (Jacques Chirac)🏅 Winners: Jacques Chirac (President of France)
为了“纪念”广岛原子弹爆炸五十周年，在南太平洋恢复并引爆了一系列核试验。
For commemorating the fiftieth anniversary of Hiroshima with atomic bomb tests in the Pacific.
#05公共卫生奖Public Health Prize

发表极具警示意义的医学案例报告《通过充气娃娃传播的淋病》。
For their cautionary medical report 'Transmission of Gonorrhea Through an Inflatable Doll.'
#06化学奖Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：乔治·戈布尔 (George Goble，普渡大学)🏅 Winners: George Goble (Purdue University)
利用木炭加液态氧，创下3秒钟极速点燃烧烤架的世界纪录。
For his blistering world record time for igniting a barbecue grill—three seconds, using charcoal and liquid oxygen.
#07生物多样性奖Biodiversity Prize
🏅 获奖者：冈村长之助 (Chonosuke Okamura，冈村化石研究所)🏅 Winners: Chonosuke Okamura (Okamura Fossil Laboratory)
宣称在岩石中发现了恐龙、马、飞龙、公主等上千种体长不足百分之一英寸的远古“微型物种”化石。
For discovering the fossils of dinosaurs, horses, dragons, princesses, and over 1,000 other extinct 'mini-species' less than 1/100 of an inch in length.
#08文学奖Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：《社会文本》(Social Text) 期刊的编辑们🏅 Winners: The Editors of the Journal Social Text
热切发表了物理学家艾伦·索卡尔撰写的、编辑自己看不懂、作者坦言毫无意义且声称“现实不存在”的恶搞论文。
For eagerly publishing Alan Sokal's hoax paper that they could not understand, that the author said was meaningless, and which claimed reality does not exist.
#09经济学奖Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：罗伯特·真科医生 (Dr. Robert J. Genco，布法罗大学)🏅 Winners: Dr. Robert J. Genco (University at Buffalo)
发现财务拮据与经济压力是导致破坏性牙周病的重要风险指标。
For his discovery that financial strain is a risk indicator for destructive periodontal disease.

发明了极具装饰性的美国草坪流行文化图腾——粉红塑料火烈鸟。
For his ornamentally evolutionary invention, the plastic pink flamingo.
1997 第7届搞笑诺贝尔奖 7th Ig Nobel Prize 1990s 📝 正文 829 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 453 words · 10 Prizes

电子宠物的摸鱼帝国与龙卷风拔鸡毛测速法 Tamagotchi Time-Sinks & Tornado Chicken-Plucking Physics

从风挡玻璃上的虫尸图鉴、圣经密码到电梯音乐防感冒，1997年的科学怪才们把脑洞开到了外太空与垃圾邮件箱。 From windshield bug-splat field guides and Bible codes to cold-preventing elevator Muzak, the 1997 laureates stretched curiosity from outer space to spam folders.

📖 1997年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1997 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1997年第七届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院首次实现全球网络直播，这一年的科学视野堪称上天入地、无所不包。天文学奖颁给了新泽西州的理查德·霍格兰，他信誓旦旦地在月球背面“发现”了十英里高的摩天大楼，还宣称火星上那块著名的岩石阴影是一张外星人雕琢的人脸。相比之下，气象学奖得主、著名作家库尔特·冯内古特的亲哥哥伯纳德·冯内古特则脚踏实地得多：他深入探究了《以拔鸡毛作为龙卷风风速的测量标准》，指出龙卷风过后活鸡之所以会全身赤裸，并非单纯被狂风硬生生拔毛，而是极度惊吓引发了家禽的心理性“羽落反应”，导致毛囊瞬间松弛脱落。

如果开车穿过风暴区，挡风玻璃上免不了啪啪作响，佛罗里达大学的马克·霍斯泰特勒便凭专著《你车上的那团黏糊物》斩获昆虫学奖，手把手教车主通过玻璃上的虫尸爆浆形状与颜色来鉴定昆虫种类。物理学奖得主、德克萨斯农工大学的约翰·博克里斯更是当代炼金术士，他在冷聚变、将贱金属点化成真金以及电化学焚烧生活垃圾三大领域同时发力。而以色列学者多伦·维茨图姆、伊利亚胡·里普斯、约阿夫·罗森伯格与美国作家迈克尔·德罗斯宁则凭吹毛求疵的统计法斩获文学奖，他们宣称用等距字母序列破译了隐藏在《圣经》里的预言密码。

在人体与心智研究上，瑞士苏黎世大学医院、日本大阪关西医科大学与捷克布拉格的柳生隆视、瓦克曼、木下、广田、河内、孔达科尔、柯尼希与莱曼跨国团队，因测量人们咀嚼不同口味口香糖时的脑电图复杂度而获生物学奖；威尔克斯大学的查内茨基、布伦南与西雅图穆扎克公司的哈里森则获医学奖，他们证明在电梯里听单调的背景音乐能刺激免疫球蛋白分泌，从而预防普通感冒。英国萨里大学的哈罗德·希尔曼凭饱含人文关怀的报告《不同死刑执行方式可能带来的痛苦》捧走和平奖。而在数字时代黎明，日本万代公司的真板亚纪与横井昭裕因发明电子宠物“拓麻歌子”，让全球打工人耗费数百万工时给虚拟小鸡铲屎而获经济学奖；费城的桑福德·华莱士则因风雨无阻地向全世界狂发电子垃圾邮件，毫无悬念地摘得通信奖。

Webcast live to the world for the very first time from Harvard’s Sanders Theatre, the 1997 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony spanned the heavens above and the highway asphalt below. The Astronomy Prize went to Richard Hoagland of New Jersey for identifying supposed artificial monuments across the solar system, including a sculpted human face on Mars and ten-mile-high skyscrapers rising from the far side of the Moon in his book 'The Monuments of Mars.' Back in Earth’s turbulent atmosphere, Meteorology laureate Bernard Vonnegut—distinguished atmospheric physicist and older brother of novelist Kurt Vonnegut—tackled a classic rural legend in his paper 'Chicken Plucking as Measure of Tornado Wind Speed.' Vonnegut demonstrated that birds found naked after a twister are not stripped purely by supersonic gale forces; rather, sheer terror triggers a physiological 'flight-molt' response that loosens their feather follicles.

For motorists driving through calmer weather, University of Florida entomologist Mark Hostetler earned the Entomology Prize for his indispensable field guide 'That Gunk on Your Car,' which teaches drivers how to identify insect species solely from the color, texture, and geometry of the bug splats smeared across their windshields. In the laboratory, Physics laureate John Bockris of Texas A&M University was honored for his audaciously wide-ranging pursuits in cold fusion, the alchemical transmutation of base elements into gold, and the electrochemical incineration of domestic garbage. Meanwhile, the Literature Prize recognized Israeli researchers Doron Witztum, Eliyahu Rips, and Yoav Rosenberg, alongside American journalist Michael Drosnin, for their hairsplitting statistical claim that equidistant letter sequences in the Book of Genesis conceal a prophetic 'Bible Code.'

Human physiology and everyday obsessions rounded out a memorable roster. An international neuroscience team—T. Yagyu, J. Wackermann, T. Kinoshita, T. Hirota, K. Kochi, I. Kondakor, Thomas König, and Dietrich Lehmann from Zurich, Osaka, and Prague—captured the Biology Prize by wiring volunteers to multichannel EEG caps to measure how different chewing gum flavors alter brainwave complexity. Medicine laureates Carl J. Charnetski and Francis X. Brennan, Jr. of Wilkes University, together with James F. Harrison of Muzak Ltd., cheered office workers everywhere by discovering that listening to soft elevator Muzak boosts secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) levels and may help ward off the common cold. On a far grimmer clinical note, Harold Hillman of the University of Surrey received the Peace Prize for his lovingly rendered study 'The Possible Pain Experienced During Execution by Different Methods.' Finally, the dawn of digital distraction claimed two prizes: Akihiro Yokoi of Wiz Company and Aki Maita of Bandai won in Economics for inventing the Tamagotchi virtual pet and diverting millions of productive work-hours into digital poultry husbandry, while self-appointed spam king Sanford Wallace of Cyber Promotions took home the Communications Prize for tirelessly blanketing the globe with electronic junk mail.

1997年第七届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院首次实现全球网络直播，这一年的科学视野堪称上天入地、无所不包。天文学奖颁给了新泽西州的理查德·霍格兰，他信誓旦旦地在月球背面“发现”了十英里高的摩天大楼，还宣称火星上那块著名的岩石阴影是一张外星人雕琢的人脸。相比之下，气象学奖得主、著名作家库尔特·冯内古特的亲哥哥伯纳德·冯内古特则脚踏实地得多：他深入探究了《以拔鸡毛作为龙卷风风速的测量标准》，指出龙卷风过后活鸡之所以会全身赤裸，并非单纯被狂风硬生生拔毛，而是极度惊吓引发了家禽的心理性“羽落反应”，导致毛囊瞬间松弛脱落。

Webcast live to the world for the very first time from Harvard’s Sanders Theatre, the 1997 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony spanned the heavens above and the highway asphalt below. The Astronomy Prize went to Richard Hoagland of New Jersey for identifying supposed artificial monuments across the solar system, including a sculpted human face on Mars and ten-mile-high skyscrapers rising from the far side of the Moon in his book 'The Monuments of Mars.' Back in Earth’s turbulent atmosphere, Meteorology laureate Bernard Vonnegut—distinguished atmospheric physicist and older brother of novelist Kurt Vonnegut—tackled a classic rural legend in his paper 'Chicken Plucking as Measure of Tornado Wind Speed.' Vonnegut demonstrated that birds found naked after a twister are not stripped purely by supersonic gale forces; rather, sheer terror triggers a physiological 'flight-molt' response that loosens their feather follicles.

如果开车穿过风暴区，挡风玻璃上免不了啪啪作响，佛罗里达大学的马克·霍斯泰特勒便凭专著《你车上的那团黏糊物》斩获昆虫学奖，手把手教车主通过玻璃上的虫尸爆浆形状与颜色来鉴定昆虫种类。物理学奖得主、德克萨斯农工大学的约翰·博克里斯更是当代炼金术士，他在冷聚变、将贱金属点化成真金以及电化学焚烧生活垃圾三大领域同时发力。而以色列学者多伦·维茨图姆、伊利亚胡·里普斯、约阿夫·罗森伯格与美国作家迈克尔·德罗斯宁则凭吹毛求疵的统计法斩获文学奖，他们宣称用等距字母序列破译了隐藏在《圣经》里的预言密码。

For motorists driving through calmer weather, University of Florida entomologist Mark Hostetler earned the Entomology Prize for his indispensable field guide 'That Gunk on Your Car,' which teaches drivers how to identify insect species solely from the color, texture, and geometry of the bug splats smeared across their windshields. In the laboratory, Physics laureate John Bockris of Texas A&M University was honored for his audaciously wide-ranging pursuits in cold fusion, the alchemical transmutation of base elements into gold, and the electrochemical incineration of domestic garbage. Meanwhile, the Literature Prize recognized Israeli researchers Doron Witztum, Eliyahu Rips, and Yoav Rosenberg, alongside American journalist Michael Drosnin, for their hairsplitting statistical claim that equidistant letter sequences in the Book of Genesis conceal a prophetic 'Bible Code.'

在人体与心智研究上，瑞士苏黎世大学医院、日本大阪关西医科大学与捷克布拉格的柳生隆视、瓦克曼、木下、广田、河内、孔达科尔、柯尼希与莱曼跨国团队，因测量人们咀嚼不同口味口香糖时的脑电图复杂度而获生物学奖；威尔克斯大学的查内茨基、布伦南与西雅图穆扎克公司的哈里森则获医学奖，他们证明在电梯里听单调的背景音乐能刺激免疫球蛋白分泌，从而预防普通感冒。英国萨里大学的哈罗德·希尔曼凭饱含人文关怀的报告《不同死刑执行方式可能带来的痛苦》捧走和平奖。而在数字时代黎明，日本万代公司的真板亚纪与横井昭裕因发明电子宠物“拓麻歌子”，让全球打工人耗费数百万工时给虚拟小鸡铲屎而获经济学奖；费城的桑福德·华莱士则因风雨无阻地向全世界狂发电子垃圾邮件，毫无悬念地摘得通信奖。

Human physiology and everyday obsessions rounded out a memorable roster. An international neuroscience team—T. Yagyu, J. Wackermann, T. Kinoshita, T. Hirota, K. Kochi, I. Kondakor, Thomas König, and Dietrich Lehmann from Zurich, Osaka, and Prague—captured the Biology Prize by wiring volunteers to multichannel EEG caps to measure how different chewing gum flavors alter brainwave complexity. Medicine laureates Carl J. Charnetski and Francis X. Brennan, Jr. of Wilkes University, together with James F. Harrison of Muzak Ltd., cheered office workers everywhere by discovering that listening to soft elevator Muzak boosts secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) levels and may help ward off the common cold. On a far grimmer clinical note, Harold Hillman of the University of Surrey received the Peace Prize for his lovingly rendered study 'The Possible Pain Experienced During Execution by Different Methods.' Finally, the dawn of digital distraction claimed two prizes: Akihiro Yokoi of Wiz Company and Aki Maita of Bandai won in Economics for inventing the Tamagotchi virtual pet and diverting millions of productive work-hours into digital poultry husbandry, while self-appointed spam king Sanford Wallace of Cyber Promotions took home the Communications Prize for tirelessly blanketing the globe with electronic junk mail.

#01生物学奖Biology
🏅 获奖者：T. Yagyu、J. Wackermann、T. Kinoshita、T. Hirota、K. Kochi、I. Kondakor、Thomas König 与 Dietrich Lehmann（瑞士/日本/捷克）🏅 Winners: T. Yagyu, J. Wackermann, T. Kinoshita, T. Hirota, K. Kochi, I. Kondakor, Thomas König, and Dietrich Lehmann (Switzerland / Japan / Czech Republic)
测量人们在咀嚼不同口味口香糖时的脑电波模式与全局复杂度变化。
For measuring people's multichannel EEG brainwave patterns while chewing different flavors of gum.
#02昆虫学奖Entomology
🏅 获奖者：Mark Hostetler（美国佛罗里达大学）🏅 Winners: Mark Hostetler (University of Florida)
撰写学术著作《你车上的那团黏糊物》，通过汽车挡风玻璃上的虫尸碎屑鉴别昆虫种类。
For his scholarly book 'That Gunk on Your Car,' which identifies the insect splats that appear on automobile windows.
#03天文学奖Astronomy
🏅 获奖者：Richard Hoagland（美国新泽西州）🏅 Winners: Richard Hoagland (New Jersey, USA)
“识别”出月球和火星上的人造建筑特征，包括火星人脸和月球背面十英里高的高楼。
For identifying artificial features on the Moon and Mars, including a human face on Mars and ten-mile-high lunar buildings.
#04通信奖Communications
🏅 获奖者：Sanford Wallace（美国费城 Cyber Promotions 公司总裁）🏅 Winners: Sanford Wallace (President of Cyber Promotions, Philadelphia)
风雨无阻、不分昼夜地向全世界发送铺天盖地的电子垃圾邮件。
For tirelessly delivering unstoppable floods of electronic junk mail (spam) to all the world.
#05物理学奖Physics
🏅 获奖者：John Bockris（美国德克萨斯农工大学）🏅 Winners: John Bockris (Texas A&M University)
表彰其在冷聚变、将贱金属转化为黄金以及生活垃圾电化学焚烧领域的“广泛成就”。
For his wide-ranging achievements in cold fusion, transmuting base elements into gold, and electrochemically incinerating domestic rubbish.
#06文学奖Literature
🏅 获奖者：Doron Witztum、Eliyahu Rips、Yoav Rosenberg（以色列）及 Michael Drosnin（美国）🏅 Winners: Doron Witztum, Eliyahu Rips, Yoav Rosenberg (Israel), and Michael Drosnin (USA)
通过吹毛求疵的统计学计算，宣称发现《圣经》中隐藏着等距字母序列的神秘密码。
For their hairsplitting statistical discovery that the Bible contains a secret hidden code via equidistant letter sequences.
#07医学奖Medicine
🏅 获奖者：Carl J. Charnetski、Francis X. Brennan, Jr. 及 James F. Harrison（美国）🏅 Winners: Carl J. Charnetski, Francis X. Brennan, Jr. (Wilkes University), and James F. Harrison (Muzak Ltd.)
发现聆听电梯背景音乐（Muzak）能刺激免疫球蛋白A（IgA）产生，从而有助于预防感冒。
For discovering that listening to elevator Muzak stimulates immunoglobulin A (IgA) production and may help prevent the common cold.
#08经济学奖Economics
🏅 获奖者：横井昭裕（Akihiro Yokoi）与真板亚纪（Aki Maita）（日本）🏅 Winners: Akihiro Yokoi (Wiz Company) and Aki Maita (Bandai Company, Japan)
发明电子宠物“拓麻歌子”（Tamagotchi），将全球数百万个工作工时转移到虚拟宠物饲养上。
The father and mother of Tamagotchi, for diverting millions of person-hours of work into the husbandry of virtual pets.
#09和平奖Peace
🏅 获奖者：Harold Hillman（英国萨里大学）🏅 Winners: Harold Hillman (University of Surrey, UK)
撰写充满关爱且终极平和的医学评估报告《不同死刑执行方式可能带来的痛苦》。
For his lovingly rendered and ultimately peaceful report 'The Possible Pain Experienced During Execution by Different Methods.'
#10气象学奖Meteorology
🏅 获奖者：Bernard Vonnegut（美国纽约州立大学奥尔巴尼分校）🏅 Winners: Bernard Vonnegut (State University of Albany)
发表极具启发性的报告《以拔鸡毛作为龙卷风风速的测量标准》。
For his revealing atmospheric report 'Chicken Plucking as Measure of Tornado Wind Speed.'
1998 第8届搞笑诺贝尔奖 8th Ig Nobel Prize 1990s 📝 正文 839 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 463 words · 10 Prizes

硬刚灰熊的钢铁侠与吃百忧解的快乐蛤蜊 The Grizzly-Proof Iron Man & Prozac-Popping Happy Clams

从顺势疗法的电话线传水记忆、五指山下的五年恶臭，到放屁对抗存在主义恐惧，1998年见证了人类最硬核的死磕精神。 From transatlantic water memory over telephone lines and a five-year putrid finger to farting away existential dread, 1998 celebrated fearless human persistence.

📖 1998年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1998 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1998年第八届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了人类挑战生理与物理极限的满腔热血与执着。安全工程奖得主、加拿大安大略省北湾的特洛伊·赫图比斯与灰熊邂逅幸存后，耗时七年倾家荡产研制出“防灰熊全身装甲”，并亲自穿上这套重型盔甲被大卡车猛撞、遭棒球棍围殴、滚下陡峭悬崖，拍成经典纪录片《灰熊计划》。同样关爱野生动物的还有葛底斯堡学院的彼得·方，他把抗抑郁药“百忧解”投喂给淡水蛤蜊，显著促进了蛤蜊排卵繁殖，凭“增进蛤蜊幸福感”斩获生物学奖。而印度总理瓦杰帕伊与巴基斯坦总理谢里夫则因在同年相继“极具侵略性又充满和平意味地”引爆原子弹，共同分享了极具讽刺意味的和平奖。

这一年还诞生了搞笑诺贝尔奖史上首位“梅开二度”的传奇得主：曾在1991年首届盛典因“水有记忆”获奖的法国学者雅克·本维尼斯特再夺化学奖，因为他进一步宣称水的顺势疗法记忆不仅真实存在，还能数字化后通过电话线和互联网跨大西洋远程传输！同样玄妙的还有物理学奖得主迪帕克·乔普拉，他将高深的量子物理学强行嫁接到生命、自由与追求经济幸福的畅销心灵鸡汤中；纽约大学荣休教授多洛雷斯·克里格则因推广“治疗性触摸”获科学教育奖——护士只要小心翼翼地避免触碰病人身体，隔空比划就能操控患者的“能量场”。芝加哥的理查德·锡德更放出豪言，企图通过克隆自己和其他人类来振兴世界经济，因而获颁经济学奖。

在直面人体尴尬的医学与心理学领域，多伦多西奈山医院的杰拉德·贝恩与阿尔伯塔大学的凯里·西米诺斯基经过严谨测量，发表《身高、阴茎长度与脚掌大小之间的关系》，用详实的统计数据击碎民间传言，荣获统计学奖。英国威尔士纽波特皇家格温特医院的米尔斯、卢埃林、凯利和霍尔特四位医生与“患者Y”共享医学奖，他们在《柳叶刀》上记录了这位男子拔鸡毛时扎破手指，导致感染罕见厌氧细菌并散发腐臭味长达五年的离奇病例。而华盛顿特区的精神分析学家玛拉·西多利博士则凭论文《放屁作为抵御难以言喻之恐惧的防御机制》摘得文学奖，证明一个适时的响屁正是幼童对抗存在主义焦虑的终极心理防御武器。

The 1998 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony saluted indomitable physical courage and eccentric compassion. Leading the charge in Safety Engineering was Troy Hurtubise of North Bay, Ontario, who survived a brush with a grizzly bear and spent the next seven years building the 'Ursus' series of bear-proof body armor. As chronicled in the National Film Board of Canada documentary 'Project Grizzly,' Hurtubise personally tested his suit by having biker gangs swing baseball bats at him, throwing himself down rocky cliffs, and getting rammed repeatedly by a three-ton pickup truck. Over in the Biology category, Peter Fong of Gettysburg College brightened the lives of mollusks by dosing fingernail clams with the antidepressant Prozac; his study proved that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors trigger vigorous clam spawning at ten times the normal rate. Meanwhile, the Peace Prize delivered biting geopolitical satire, honoring Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif for their 'aggressively peaceful' tit-for-tat explosions of atomic bombs.

History was also made in Chemistry when French immunologist Jacques Benveniste—already the 1991 Ig Nobel Chemistry laureate for claiming that water retains a homeopathic 'memory' of solutes long after they are diluted away—became the first two-time Ig Nobel winner. His 1998 follow-up asserted that water’s memory can be digitized and transmitted across the Atlantic Ocean via telephone lines and the Internet to imprint fresh water thousands of miles away. In Physics, wellness guru Deepak Chopra was cited for his creative appropriation of quantum mechanics to explain life, liberty, and the pursuit of economic happiness in books like 'Quantum Healing.' Science Education went to New York University Professor Emerita Dolores Krieger for championing 'Therapeutic Touch,' a nursing technique that manipulates patients' energy fields by carefully avoiding any physical contact with them whatsoever, while Chicago physicist Richard Seed won in Economics for his enterprising plan to jump-start the global economy by cloning himself and other human beings.

Finally, researchers fearless enough to confront human awkwardness claimed the remaining honors. Jerald Bain of Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto and Kerry Siminoski of the University of Alberta earned the Statistics Prize for their painstakingly measured clinical report 'The Relationships Among Height, Penile Length, and Foot Size,' which debunked locker-room folklore with hard regression data. The Medicine Prize was awarded jointly to 'Patient Y' and his physicians Caroline Mills, Meirion Llewelyn, David Kelly, and Peter Holt at Royal Gwent Hospital in Wales for their cautionary 'Lancet' case report 'A Man Who Pricked His Finger and Smelled Putrid for 5 Years' after puncturing his skin on a chicken bone. Rounding out the evening, Washington analytical psychologist Dr. Mara Sidoli received the Literature Prize for her illuminating psychoanalytic treatise 'Farting as a Defence Against Unspeakable Dread,' detailing how a troubled young boy used flatulence as an acoustic shield against existential terror.

#01安全工程奖Safety Engineering
🏅 获奖者：Troy Hurtubise（加拿大安大略省北湾）🏅 Winners: Troy Hurtubise (North Bay, Ontario, Canada)
研发并亲自测试了一套能够抵御灰熊攻击的全身装甲（《灰熊计划》）。
For developing and personally testing a suit of armor that is impervious to grizzly bears ('Project Grizzly').
#02生物学奖Biology
🏅 获奖者：Peter Fong（美国宾夕法尼亚州葛底斯堡学院）🏅 Winners: Peter Fong (Gettysburg College, Pennsylvania)
通过给蛤蜊喂食抗抑郁药百忧解（Prozac），为蛤蜊的幸福感与繁殖做出贡献。
For contributing to the happiness and reproductive spawning of fingernail clams by giving them Prozac.
#03和平奖Peace
🏅 获奖者：印度总理瓦杰帕伊（Atal Bihari Vajpayee）与巴基斯坦总理谢里夫（Nawaz Sharif）🏅 Winners: Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee (India) and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif (Pakistan)
表彰两国领导人为了“和平”而极具侵略性地相继引爆原子弹。
For their aggressively peaceful explosions of atomic bombs.
#04化学奖Chemistry
🏅 获奖者：Jacques Benveniste（法国，继1991年后二度获奖）🏅 Winners: Jacques Benveniste (France, two-time winner after 1991)
提出顺势疗法新发现：水不仅有记忆，而且这种信息还能通过电话线和互联网传输。
For his homeopathic discovery that not only does water have memory, but that the information can be transmitted over telephone lines and the Internet.
#05科学教育奖Science Education
🏅 获奖者：Dolores Krieger（美国纽约大学荣休教授）🏅 Winners: Dolores Krieger (Professor Emerita, New York University)
展示“治疗性触摸”的妙用——护士只需小心地避免触碰患者，就能隔空操控患者的能量场。
For demonstrating the merits of Therapeutic Touch, by which nurses manipulate patients' energy fields by carefully avoiding physical contact.
#06统计学奖Statistics
🏅 获奖者：Jerald Bain 与 Kerry Siminoski（加拿大多伦多西奈山医院/阿尔伯塔大学）🏅 Winners: Jerald Bain (Mt. Sinai Hospital, Toronto) and Kerry Siminoski (University of Alberta)
发表严谨测量的统计报告《身高、阴茎长度与脚掌大小之间的关系》。
For their carefully measured report 'The Relationships Among Height, Penile Length, and Foot Size.'
#07物理学奖Physics
🏅 获奖者：Deepak Chopra（美国加州乔普拉健康中心）🏅 Winners: Deepak Chopra (The Chopra Center for Well Being, California)
对量子物理学进行独特诠释，并将其应用于生命、自由和追求经济幸福的畅销书中。
For his unique interpretation of quantum physics as it applies to life, liberty, and the pursuit of economic happiness.
#08经济学奖Economics
🏅 获奖者：Richard Seed（美国芝加哥）🏅 Winners: Richard Seed (Chicago, Illinois)
表彰其企图通过克隆自己和其他人类来刺激世界经济的努力。
For his efforts to stoke up the world economy by cloning himself and other human beings.
#09医学奖Medicine
🏅 获奖者：患者Y及英国皇家格温特医院的 Caroline Mills、Meirion Llewelyn、David Kelly、Peter Holt🏅 Winners: Patient Y and Drs. Caroline Mills, Meirion Llewelyn, David Kelly, and Peter Holt (Royal Gwent Hospital, Wales)
在《柳叶刀》发表警示性医学报告《一个扎破手指后散发恶臭长达五年的男人》。
For their cautionary 'Lancet' medical report 'A Man Who Pricked His Finger and Smelled Putrid for 5 Years.'
#10文学奖Literature
🏅 获奖者：Mara Sidoli 博士（美国华盛顿特区）🏅 Winners: Dr. Mara Sidoli (Washington, DC)
撰写极具启发性的心理学报告《放屁作为抵御难以言喻之恐惧的防御机制》。
For her illuminating psychoanalytic report 'Farting as a Defence Against Unspeakable Dread.'
1999 第9届搞笑诺贝尔奖 9th Ig Nobel Prize 1990s 📝 正文 831 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 485 words · 10 Prizes

英式下午茶的流体力学与离心力甩娃分娩台 The Fluid Dynamics of Biscuit Dunking & Centrifugal Childbirth

从泡饼干方程、防出轨内裤喷雾、火焰喷射防盗车，到把产妇绑在转盘上高速旋转，世纪末的发明家们彻底放飞了自我。 From non-dripping teapots and infidelity-detecting underwear spray to a high-speed rotating birthing turntable, 1999 closed out the 1990s in spectacular style.

📖 1999年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 1999 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

1999年第九届搞笑诺贝尔奖洋溢着浓郁的英式下午茶气息与甜点风情。物理学奖一分为二：英国与澳大利亚物理学家伦·费舍尔利用毛细管流体力学方程，精确算出了将饼干浸入热茶而不至于泡软断落杯底的最佳倾角与浸泡秒数；英比学者让-马克·范登-布鲁克与美国数学家约瑟夫·凯勒则算出了如何消除液体表面张力的附壁效应，造出倒茶绝不滴漏的茶壶嘴。与之绝配的是文学奖得主英国标准协会，他们郑重其事地发布了长达六页的国家标准规范（BS-6008），对泡一杯正宗英式茶的水温、奶量和时间做出了严苛规定。而在大洋彼岸，多伦多约克大学的史蒂夫·彭福德则因撰写关于加拿大甜甜圈店社会史的博士论文，拿下了社会学奖。

饮食与日常生活的怪诞发明同样层出不穷。新墨西哥州立大学辣椒研究所所长保罗·博斯兰博士耗时多年培育出一种完全不辣的墨西哥辣椒，让怕辣人士也能体面吃椒，荣获生物学奖；挪威斯图尔的阿尔维德·瓦特勒医生则因长年仔细收集、分类并潜心思考患者提交尿液样本时选用的五花八门容器（从果酱玻璃罐到威士忌酒瓶），摘得医学奖。为了拯救社交体面与婚姻危机，韩国首尔科隆公司的权赫镐发明了摩擦面料即可自动散发香水的商务西装，获颁环境保护奖；日本大阪安全侦探社社长牧野武则因参与研发能让妻子喷在丈夫内裤上检测出轨痕迹的“S-Check”化学喷雾，抱走了化学奖。

本年度最令人瞠目结舌的莫过于三项硬核跨界大奖。美国堪萨斯州与科罗拉多州教育委员会因规定学生“不必相信达尔文的进化论，就像不必相信牛顿的万有引力定律、法拉第与麦克斯韦的电磁学理论或巴斯德的细菌致病论一样”，被授予科学教育奖；南非约翰内斯堡的查尔·富里与米歇尔·王发明了配备检测电路与车底火焰喷射器的汽车防盗报警器，凭“把劫匪烤成焦炭”的威慑力斩获和平奖；而已故的纽约与加州发明家乔治与夏洛特·布朗斯基夫妇则因一项疯狂专利获管理医疗保健奖——他们发明了一张高速旋转的圆形分娩转盘桌，把临产孕妇绑在上面飞速旋转，试图利用强大的离心力把婴儿直接“甩”出产道！

The 1999 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at Harvard’s Sanders Theatre was steeped in the refined rituals of British afternoon tea and North American comfort food. The Physics Prize was shared by two breakthroughs in everyday beverage mechanics: physicist Len Fisher of the UK and Australia applied Washburn’s capillary-flow equation to calculate the exact optimal angle and duration for dunking a digestive biscuit into hot tea without suffering catastrophic soggy collapse, while Jean-Marc Vanden-Broeck and Joseph Keller calculated how to contour a teapot spout lip so that surface tension no longer makes tea dribble down the porcelain. Fittingly, the Literature Prize went to the British Standards Institution for its deadpan six-page regulatory specification (BS-6008) prescribing the official, standardized method for brewing a proper cup of tea. Across the Atlantic, York University historian Steve Penfold earned the Sociology Prize for his doctoral dissertation examining the social life, commercial history, and working-class community role of Canadian donut shops.

Culinary curiosity and everyday domestic anxieties inspired several more winners. Dr. Paul Bosland, director of the Chile Pepper Institute at New Mexico State University in Las Cruces, received the Biology Prize for breeding the 'NuMex Primavera,' a completely spiceless jalapeño pepper that delivers all the verdant aroma of a jalapeño with zero capsaicin burn. In Norway, general practitioner Dr. Arvid Vatle of Stord won the Medicine Prize for meticulously collecting, classifying, and contemplating the eclectic array of household containers—ranging from jam jars and tomato-puree tins to miniature whiskey bottles—that his patients chose when submitting urine samples. Meanwhile, Hyuk-ho Kwon of South Korea’s Kolon Company took home the Environmental Protection Prize for inventing the self-perfuming business suit embedded with scent microcapsules that release fragrance whenever the wearer rubs his sleeves, and Takeshi Makino, president of the Safety Detective Agency in Osaka, won in Chemistry for developing 'S-Check,' an over-the-counter infidelity-detection spray that wives can apply to their husbands' underwear to reveal suspicious biological traces.

The final trio of prizes showcased unforgettable extremes in education, urban security, and obstetrics. The Kansas State Board of Education and the Colorado State Board of Education shared the Science Education Prize for mandating that schoolchildren should not be required to believe in Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution any more than they believe in Isaac Newton’s theory of gravitation, Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell’s theory of electromagnetism, or Louis Pasteur’s theory that germs cause disease. The Peace Prize honored Charl Fourie and Michelle Wong of Johannesburg, South Africa, for patenting the 'Blaster,' an anti-hijacking automobile burglar alarm consisting of a foot-pedal detection circuit and dual under-door liquefied-petroleum flamethrowers. Topping off the evening, the Managed Health Care Prize was awarded posthumously to George and Charlotte Blonsky of New York and San Jose for US Patent #3,216,423: an apparatus to aid women in giving birth by strapping the expectant mother onto a circular turntable and spinning it at high speed so centrifugal force gently flings the baby out.

#01社会学奖Sociology
🏅 获奖者：Steve Penfold（加拿大多伦多约克大学）🏅 Winners: Steve Penfold (York University, Toronto)
以加拿大甜甜圈店（Donut shops）的社会学史为主题撰写博士学位论文。
For writing his PhD thesis on the sociology and community history of Canadian donut shops.

🏅 获奖者：Len Fisher（英/澳）、Jean-Marc Vanden-Broeck（英/比）与 Joseph Keller（美国）🏅 Winners: Len Fisher (UK/Australia), Jean-Marc Vanden-Broeck (UK/Belgium), and Joseph Keller (USA)
分别计算出将饼干浸入热茶的最佳方式，以及如何设计倒茶不滴水的茶壶嘴。
For calculating the optimal way to dunk a biscuit, and how to make a teapot spout that does not drip.

颁布长达六页的英国国家标准规范（BS-6008），严格规定泡一杯茶的正确方法。
For its six-page official specification (BS-6008) of the proper way to make a cup of tea.

🏅 获奖者：美国堪萨斯州教育委员会与科罗拉多州教育委员会🏅 Winners: The Kansas State Board of Education and the Colorado State Board of Education (USA)
规定孩子们不必相信达尔文进化论，正如不必相信万有引力、电磁学或细菌致病理论。
For mandating that children should not believe in Darwin's theory of evolution any more than gravitation, electromagnetism, or germ theory.

🏅 获奖者：Arvid Vatle 医生（挪威斯图尔）🏅 Winners: Dr. Arvid Vatle (Stord, Norway)
仔细收集、分类并沉思患者在提交尿液样本时选用了哪些五花八门的瓶罐容器。
For carefully collecting, classifying, and contemplating which kinds of containers his patients chose when submitting urine samples.
#06化学奖Chemistry
🏅 获奖者：牧野武（Takeshi Makino，日本大阪安全侦探社社长）🏅 Winners: Takeshi Makino (President of The Safety Detective Agency, Osaka, Japan)
参与研发“S-Check”防出轨检测喷雾，供妻子喷洒在丈夫内裤上检测可疑痕迹。
For his involvement with S-Check, an infidelity detection spray that wives can apply to their husbands' underwear.
#07生物学奖Biology
🏅 获奖者：Paul Bosland 博士（美国新墨西哥州立大学辣椒研究所所长）🏅 Winners: Dr. Paul Bosland (Director of The Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University)
成功培育出一种完全不辣的墨西哥辣椒（spiceless jalapeño）。
For breeding a spiceless jalapeño chile pepper.
#08环境保护奖Environmental Protection
🏅 获奖者：权赫镐（Hyuk-ho Kwon，韩国首尔科隆公司）🏅 Winners: Hyuk-ho Kwon (Kolon Company, Seoul, South Korea)
发明能够自动散发香水的商务西装。
For inventing the self-perfuming business suit.

🏅 获奖者：Charl Fourie 与 Michelle Wong（南非约翰内斯堡）🏅 Winners: Charl Fourie and Michelle Wong (Johannesburg, South Africa)
发明由检测电路和车底火焰喷射器组成的汽车防盗报警器。
For inventing an automobile burglar alarm consisting of a detection circuit and a flamethrower.
#10管理医疗保健奖Managed Health Care
🏅 获奖者：已故的 George Blonsky 与 Charlotte Blonsky 夫妇（美国）🏅 Winners: The late George and Charlotte Blonsky (New York City and San Jose, California)
发明离心力分娩装置（美国专利#3,216,423）：将产妇绑在圆桌上高速旋转以辅助分娩。
For patenting a centrifugal birthing device (US Patent #3,216,423) that straps a woman onto a circular table and rotates her at high speed.
2000 第10届搞笑诺贝尔奖 10th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 858 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 463 words · 10 Prizes

飞翔的磁悬浮青蛙与“越无知越自信”的达克效应 The Levitating Frog & The Birth of the Dunning-Kruger Effect

千禧年盛典诞生了科学史上的双料传奇：从未来诺奖得主的悬浮活蛙、改变心理学史的达克效应，到核磁共振仪里的爱情。 The millennium ceremony produced two icons of modern science: a magnetically levitated live frog by a future Nobel laureate, and the psychology of inflated incompetence.

📖 2000年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2000 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2000年第十届搞笑诺贝尔奖堪称科学史上的传奇里程碑，诞生了多项真正写入教科书的经典研究。心理学奖颁给了康奈尔大学的大卫·邓宁与伊利诺伊大学的贾斯汀·克鲁格，他们那篇谦逊的论文《既不称职又不自知：难以认识自身无能如何导致膨胀的自我评估》，提出了如今家喻户晓的“达克效应”。物理学奖得主、荷兰奈梅亨大学的安德烈·海姆与英国布里斯托大学的迈克尔·贝里爵士则用强磁场利用抗磁性让一只活青蛙优雅地悬浮在半空中；十年后的2010年，海姆因石墨烯研究摘得真正的诺贝尔物理学奖，成为史上唯一同时囊括搞笑诺贝尔奖与诺贝尔奖的“双冠王”！

在探究爱情与身体奥秘方面，意大利比萨大学的玛拉齐蒂、罗西、卡萨诺与加州大学圣迭戈分校的阿基斯卡尔荣获化学奖，他们发现从血小板血清素转运体等生化指标来看，浪漫热恋与患有严重强迫症几乎毫无区别。荷兰格罗宁根的舒尔茨、范安德尔、穆亚特与阿姆斯特丹的萨贝利斯则更进一步，让志愿者情侣钻进狭窄的核磁共振仪里行房，凭发表在《英国医学杂志》上的《男女交合及女性性兴奋期间生殖器的磁共振成像》斩获医学奖。相比之下，文鲜明牧师则将婚姻做成了规模经济，从1960年的36对新人一路扩张到1997年的3600万对新人集体结婚，凭“集体婚礼产业的高效增长”获颁经济学奖。

千禧年的饮食与生活同样充满荒诞色彩。澳大利亚“食气主义”教母洁丝慕音出版《靠光生活》，宣称人类其实根本不需要吃饭，靠呼吸空气和阳光就能存活，因此获文学奖；达尔豪斯大学的理查德·瓦瑟苏格则亲口生嚼热带雨林蝌蚪，凭第一手味觉测评报告《哥斯达黎加旱季几种蝌蚪的适口性比较》获生物学奖。为拯救铲屎官的文档，亚利桑那州的克里斯·尼斯万德发明了能自动识别猫咪踩键盘并拦截乱码的软件“PawSense”，摘得计算机科学奖；苏格兰格拉斯哥的怀亚特、麦克诺顿与塔利特三位医生因记录多起市民如厕时老旧瓷马桶突然碎裂坍塌伤人的惨剧，荣获公共卫生奖；而英国皇家海军则因囊中羞涩，下令水兵在实弹演习中停止发射真炮弹，改由全员齐声大喊“砰！”来代替开炮，毫无争议地赢得了和平奖。

The 2000 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony—marking the tenth anniversary of the awards—stands as a landmark in scientific history, honoring two studies that became household touchstones around the world. The Psychology Prize went to David Dunning of Cornell University and Justin Kruger of the University of Illinois for their deceptively modest paper 'Unskilled and Unaware of It: How Difficulties in Recognizing One’s Own Incompetence Lead to Inflated Self-Assessments,' which introduced the world to the Dunning-Kruger Effect. Equally iconic was the Physics Prize, awarded to Andre Geim of the University of Nijmegen and Sir Michael Berry of Bristol University for using a powerful 16-Tesla electromagnet to levitate a live frog via diamagnetism. Exactly ten years later, in 2010, Geim won the Nobel Prize in Physics for isolating graphene, making him the first—and still only—person in history to win both an Ig Nobel Prize and a Nobel Prize individually.

Matters of the heart, passion, and matrimony were dissected with clinical precision. In Chemistry, Donatella Marazziti, Alessandra Rossi, and Giovanni B. Cassano of the University of Pisa, together with Hagop S. Akiskal of the University of California, San Diego, discovered that biochemically—specifically in blood platelet serotonin transporter levels—being head-over-heels in romantic love is virtually indistinguishable from suffering severe obsessive-compulsive disorder. Taking anatomical curiosity inside the scanner, Dutch researchers Willibrord Weijmar Schultz, Pek van Andel, Eduard Mooyaart, and Ida Sabelis won the Medicine Prize for their 'BMJ' paper 'Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Male and Female Genitals During Coitus and Female Sexual Arousal,' proving that volunteering couples could consummate love inside a cramped MRI tube. On a macroeconomic scale, the Reverend Sun Myung Moon received the Economics Prize for bringing steady exponential growth to the mass-marriage industry, expanding from a 36-couple wedding in 1960 to a reported 36,000,000-couple wedding in 1997.

The remaining laureates tackled quirky survival, culinary bravery, and domestic hazards. Australian 'Breatharian' guru Jasmuheen (formerly Ellen Greve) won the Literature Prize for her book 'Living on Light,' which insists that human beings never actually need to eat food if they nourish themselves on air and sunlight. In contrast, Dalhousie University biologist Richard Wassersug earned the Biology Prize for his first-hand gustatory report 'On the Comparative Palatability of Some Dry-Season Tadpoles from Costa Rica,' for which he personally chewed and graded tropical tadpoles. Computer Science honored Chris Niswander of Tucson, Arizona, for inventing 'PawSense,' software that detects when a cat is strolling across your computer keyboard and blocks feline gibberish. Public Health went to Glasgow emergency physicians Jonathan Wyatt, Gordon McNaughton, and William Tullett for their alarming report 'The Collapse of Toilets in Glasgow,' documenting injuries from crumbling Victorian porcelain commodes, while the Peace Prize saluted the British Royal Navy for ordering sailors to save money during gunnery drills by shouting 'Bang!' instead of firing live cannon shells.
