#01心理学奖Psychology
🏅 获奖者：David Dunning（康奈尔大学）与 Justin Kruger（伊利诺伊大学）🏅 Winners: David Dunning (Cornell University) and Justin Kruger (University of Illinois)
发表《既不称职又不自知》，发现能力欠缺者往往高估自身水平（即著名的“达克效应”）。
For their modest report 'Unskilled and Unaware of It,' establishing the Dunning-Kruger Effect.
#02文学奖Literature
🏅 获奖者：Jasmuheen（原名 Ellen Greve，澳大利亚）🏅 Winners: Jasmuheen (formerly Ellen Greve, Australia)
出版食气主义著作《靠光生活》，宣称人类虽然吃食物，但其实完全不需要进食。
First lady of Breatharianism, for her book 'Living on Light,' explaining that people don't ever really need to eat food.
#03生物学奖Biology
🏅 获奖者：Richard Wassersug（加拿大达尔豪斯大学）🏅 Winners: Richard Wassersug (Dalhousie University, Canada)
亲口品尝并撰写第一手报告《哥斯达黎加旱季几种蝌蚪的适口性比较》。
For his first-hand taste-testing report 'On the Comparative Palatability of Some Dry-Season Tadpoles from Costa Rica.'
#04物理学奖Physics
🏅 获奖者：Andre Geim（荷兰奈梅亨大学）与 Sir Michael Berry（英国布里斯托大学）🏅 Winners: Andre Geim (University of Nijmegen) and Sir Michael Berry (Bristol University)
利用强磁场抗磁性让一只活青蛙悬浮在半空中（海姆于2010年再获诺贝尔物理学奖）。
For using magnets to levitate a live frog (Geim later won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics).
#05化学奖Chemistry
🏅 获奖者：Donatella Marazziti、Alessandra Rossi、Giovanni B. Cassano（意大利）及 Hagop S. Akiskal（美国）🏅 Winners: Donatella Marazziti, Alessandra Rossi, Giovanni B. Cassano (Italy), and Hagop S. Akiskal (USA)
发现从生物化学指标来看，浪漫热恋与患有严重强迫症（OCD）几乎无法区分。
For discovering that, biochemically, romantic love may be indistinguishable from having severe obsessive-compulsive disorder.
#06经济学奖Economics
🏅 获奖者：文鲜明牧师（Reverend Sun Myung Moon）🏅 Winners: The Reverend Sun Myung Moon
为集体婚礼产业带来高效率与稳定增长，从36对新人婚礼一路扩张至3600万对。
For bringing efficiency and steady growth to the mass-marriage industry, from 36 couples in 1960 to 36 million couples in 1997.
#07医学奖Medicine
🏅 获奖者：Willibrord Weijmar Schultz、Pek van Andel、Eduard Mooyaart 与 Ida Sabelis（荷兰）🏅 Winners: Willibrord Weijmar Schultz, Pek van Andel, Eduard Mooyaart, and Ida Sabelis (The Netherlands)
发表《男女交合及女性性兴奋期间生殖器的磁共振成像（MRI）》。
For their illuminating BMJ study 'Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Male and Female Genitals During Coitus and Female Sexual Arousal.'
#08计算机科学奖Computer Science
🏅 获奖者：Chris Niswander（美国亚利桑那州图森市）🏅 Winners: Chris Niswander (Tucson, Arizona)
发明“PawSense”防猫踩键盘软件，能自动检测猫咪在电脑键盘上散步并锁定输入。
For inventing PawSense, software that detects when a cat is walking across your computer keyboard.
#09和平奖Peace
🏅 获奖者：英国皇家海军（British Royal Navy）🏅 Winners: The British Royal Navy
下令水兵在训练中停止使用昂贵的实弹炮弹，改由口头大喊“砰！（Bang!）”代替。
For ordering its sailors to stop using expensive live cannon shells during training and instead just shout 'Bang!'
#10公共卫生奖Public Health
🏅 获奖者：Jonathan Wyatt、Gordon McNaughton 与 William Tullett（苏格兰格拉斯哥）🏅 Winners: Jonathan Wyatt, Gordon McNaughton, and William Tullett (Glasgow, Scotland)
发表令人警醒的医学报告《格拉斯哥的马桶坍塌事件》。
For their alarming medical report 'The Collapse of Toilets in Glasgow.'
2001 第11届搞笑诺贝尔奖 11th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 859 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 465 words · 10 Prizes

公元2001年重新发明轮子与浴帘内吸之谜 Patenting the Wheel in 2001 & The Shower-Curtain Vortex

从黑洞即地狱的宇宙神学、为了省遗产税硬撑着不死，到高空坠落椰子与活性炭防臭屁内裤，21世纪初的脑洞无奇不有。 From black holes serving as biblical Hell and postponing death to cut estate taxes to falling coconuts and charcoal-filtered underwear, 2001 was pure ingenuity.

📖 2001年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2001 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

步入21世纪的2001年第十一届搞笑诺贝尔奖，首先用一项匪夷所思的专利震惊了世界：澳大利亚维多利亚州霍桑市的律师约翰·基奥在公元2001年郑重其事地将“轮子”包装成“一种促进移动的圆形装置”申请专利，而澳大利亚专利局竟不假思索地盖章签发了第2001100012号创新专利，双方因此携手共享技术奖！同样解开日常千古之谜的还有马萨诸塞大学的大卫·施密特，他利用流体力学计算机模拟证明花洒喷水会在浴室内形成水平低压涡旋，部分解答了“为什么洗澡时浴帘总是向内飘并贴在湿漉漉的人身上”，荣获物理学奖。麦吉尔大学的彼得·巴斯则奔赴热带岛屿，凭深入调查树上掉下沉重椰子砸伤头骨的医学报告《坠落椰子导致的创伤》摘得医学奖。

人体与生老病死的荒诞规律同样逃不过学者们的法眼。科罗拉多州普韦布洛的巴克·韦默为了造福肠胃胀气的伴侣，发明了配有可更换活性炭滤芯的气密防臭屁内裤“Under-Ease”，将难闻气体扼杀在逃逸之前，荣获生物学奖；印度班加罗尔国家精神卫生与神经科学研究所的安德拉德与斯里哈里则通过详尽的问卷普查，得出了“挖鼻孔在青少年群体中是一种极其普遍的行为”这一惊人医学发现，斩获公共卫生奖。而在金钱与死亡的终极博弈中，密歇根大学商学院的乔尔·斯莱姆罗德与不列颠哥伦比亚大学的沃伊切赫·科普楚克分析遗产税申报数据后获经济学奖：他们发现如果多活几天能适用更低的遗产税率，临终富人真的会想方设法推迟死亡时间！

精神世界与文化奇观更是百花齐放。密歇根州电视布道师杰克·范·伊姆佩博士与妻子雷克塞拉在节目中惊人宣布，宇宙中的黑洞在各项技术指标上完美符合《圣经》对“地狱”位置的所有要求，双双获颁天体物理学奖；俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的劳伦斯·舍曼因观察幼儿园孩童并发表《学龄前儿童小组中幸灾乐祸与狂喜的生态学研究》获心理学奖；英国波士顿的约翰·理查兹创立“撇号保护协会”，誓死捍卫英语中复数与所有格撇号的语法尊严，摘得文学奖；立陶宛格鲁塔斯的企业家维柳马斯·马利瑙斯卡斯则因收集前苏联废弃雕像、打造名为“斯大林世界”的主题游乐园，捧走了和平奖。

Entering the twenty-first century, the 2001 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony opened with a masterclass in bureaucratic absurdity. The Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Melbourne patent lawyer John Keogh, for successfully patenting the wheel in the year 2001—described in legalese as a 'circular transportation facilitation device'—and to the Australian Patent Office for dutifully granting him Innovation Patent #2001100012 without noticing that the Mesopotamians had beaten him to it by five millennia. Solving an equally enduring domestic mystery, University of Massachusetts mechanical engineer David Schmidt won the Physics Prize for using computational fluid dynamics to explain why shower curtains billow inward toward the bather: the spray creates a horizontal low-pressure vortex much like a miniature sideways cyclone. Meanwhile, McGill University physician Peter Barss received the Medicine Prize for his impactful tropical trauma paper 'Injuries Due to Falling Coconuts,' documenting the skull-crushing kinetic energy of ripe coconuts plummeting from tall palms.

Bodily habits and the economics of mortality yielded three more unforgettable laureates. In Biology, Buck Weimer of Pueblo, Colorado, was honored for inventing 'Under-Ease,' airtight polyurethane briefs equipped with a replaceable activated-charcoal filter that traps and deodorizes flatulence before it can escape into polite company. In Public Health, Chittaranjan Andrade and B.S. Srihari of India’s National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences in Bangalore won for their probing epidemiological survey 'A Preliminary Survey of Rhinotillexomania in an Adolescent Sample,' confirming empirically that teenagers across every socioeconomic stratum pick their noses nearly four times a day. And in Economics, Joel Slemrod of the University of Michigan and Wojciech Kopczuk of the University of British Columbia analyzed estate tax returns in 'Dying to Save Taxes,' concluding that wealthy individuals somehow manage to postpone their own deaths by several days if surviving past a statutory cutoff date qualifies their heirs for a lower inheritance tax rate.

The remaining awards celebrated cosmic theology, preschool pandemonium, grammar vigilance, and post-Soviet tourism. Television evangelists Dr. Jack and Rexella Van Impe of Jack Van Impe Ministries in Rochester Hills, Michigan, earned the Astrophysics Prize for announcing on their March 2001 broadcast that cosmic black holes fulfill every single technical requirement described in Scripture to serve as the literal physical location of Hell. Miami University psychologist Lawrence W. Sherman won in Psychology for his classic observational study 'An Ecological Study of Glee in Small Groups of Preschool Children,' charting how infectious shrieks of collective joy and mischief ripple through kindergarten classrooms. In Literature, retired British journalist John Richards of Boston, England—founder of the Apostrophe Protection Society—was saluted for his heroic one-man crusade defending the grammatical distinction between plural nouns and possessive apostrophes on shopkeepers' signs, while Lithuanian mushroom entrepreneur Viliumas Malinauskas of Grutas received the Peace Prize for rounding up discarded Soviet statues to build the satirical open-air theme park known as 'Stalin World.'

步入21世纪的2001年第十一届搞笑诺贝尔奖，首先用一项匪夷所思的专利震惊了世界：澳大利亚维多利亚州霍桑市的律师约翰·基奥在公元2001年郑重其事地将“轮子”包装成“一种促进移动的圆形装置”申请专利，而澳大利亚专利局竟不假思索地盖章签发了第2001100012号创新专利，双方因此携手共享技术奖！同样解开日常千古之谜的还有马萨诸塞大学的大卫·施密特，他利用流体力学计算机模拟证明花洒喷水会在浴室内形成水平低压涡旋，部分解答了“为什么洗澡时浴帘总是向内飘并贴在湿漉漉的人身上”，荣获物理学奖。麦吉尔大学的彼得·巴斯则奔赴热带岛屿，凭深入调查树上掉下沉重椰子砸伤头骨的医学报告《坠落椰子导致的创伤》摘得医学奖。

Entering the twenty-first century, the 2001 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony opened with a masterclass in bureaucratic absurdity. The Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Melbourne patent lawyer John Keogh, for successfully patenting the wheel in the year 2001—described in legalese as a 'circular transportation facilitation device'—and to the Australian Patent Office for dutifully granting him Innovation Patent #2001100012 without noticing that the Mesopotamians had beaten him to it by five millennia. Solving an equally enduring domestic mystery, University of Massachusetts mechanical engineer David Schmidt won the Physics Prize for using computational fluid dynamics to explain why shower curtains billow inward toward the bather: the spray creates a horizontal low-pressure vortex much like a miniature sideways cyclone. Meanwhile, McGill University physician Peter Barss received the Medicine Prize for his impactful tropical trauma paper 'Injuries Due to Falling Coconuts,' documenting the skull-crushing kinetic energy of ripe coconuts plummeting from tall palms.

人体与生老病死的荒诞规律同样逃不过学者们的法眼。科罗拉多州普韦布洛的巴克·韦默为了造福肠胃胀气的伴侣，发明了配有可更换活性炭滤芯的气密防臭屁内裤“Under-Ease”，将难闻气体扼杀在逃逸之前，荣获生物学奖；印度班加罗尔国家精神卫生与神经科学研究所的安德拉德与斯里哈里则通过详尽的问卷普查，得出了“挖鼻孔在青少年群体中是一种极其普遍的行为”这一惊人医学发现，斩获公共卫生奖。而在金钱与死亡的终极博弈中，密歇根大学商学院的乔尔·斯莱姆罗德与不列颠哥伦比亚大学的沃伊切赫·科普楚克分析遗产税申报数据后获经济学奖：他们发现如果多活几天能适用更低的遗产税率，临终富人真的会想方设法推迟死亡时间！

Bodily habits and the economics of mortality yielded three more unforgettable laureates. In Biology, Buck Weimer of Pueblo, Colorado, was honored for inventing 'Under-Ease,' airtight polyurethane briefs equipped with a replaceable activated-charcoal filter that traps and deodorizes flatulence before it can escape into polite company. In Public Health, Chittaranjan Andrade and B.S. Srihari of India’s National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences in Bangalore won for their probing epidemiological survey 'A Preliminary Survey of Rhinotillexomania in an Adolescent Sample,' confirming empirically that teenagers across every socioeconomic stratum pick their noses nearly four times a day. And in Economics, Joel Slemrod of the University of Michigan and Wojciech Kopczuk of the University of British Columbia analyzed estate tax returns in 'Dying to Save Taxes,' concluding that wealthy individuals somehow manage to postpone their own deaths by several days if surviving past a statutory cutoff date qualifies their heirs for a lower inheritance tax rate.

精神世界与文化奇观更是百花齐放。密歇根州电视布道师杰克·范·伊姆佩博士与妻子雷克塞拉在节目中惊人宣布，宇宙中的黑洞在各项技术指标上完美符合《圣经》对“地狱”位置的所有要求，双双获颁天体物理学奖；俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的劳伦斯·舍曼因观察幼儿园孩童并发表《学龄前儿童小组中幸灾乐祸与狂喜的生态学研究》获心理学奖；英国波士顿的约翰·理查兹创立“撇号保护协会”，誓死捍卫英语中复数与所有格撇号的语法尊严，摘得文学奖；立陶宛格鲁塔斯的企业家维柳马斯·马利瑙斯卡斯则因收集前苏联废弃雕像、打造名为“斯大林世界”的主题游乐园，捧走了和平奖。

The remaining awards celebrated cosmic theology, preschool pandemonium, grammar vigilance, and post-Soviet tourism. Television evangelists Dr. Jack and Rexella Van Impe of Jack Van Impe Ministries in Rochester Hills, Michigan, earned the Astrophysics Prize for announcing on their March 2001 broadcast that cosmic black holes fulfill every single technical requirement described in Scripture to serve as the literal physical location of Hell. Miami University psychologist Lawrence W. Sherman won in Psychology for his classic observational study 'An Ecological Study of Glee in Small Groups of Preschool Children,' charting how infectious shrieks of collective joy and mischief ripple through kindergarten classrooms. In Literature, retired British journalist John Richards of Boston, England—founder of the Apostrophe Protection Society—was saluted for his heroic one-man crusade defending the grammatical distinction between plural nouns and possessive apostrophes on shopkeepers' signs, while Lithuanian mushroom entrepreneur Viliumas Malinauskas of Grutas received the Peace Prize for rounding up discarded Soviet statues to build the satirical open-air theme park known as 'Stalin World.'

发表研究报告《学龄前儿童小组中幸灾乐祸与狂喜（Glee）的生态学研究》。

在电视布道中宣布发现宇宙黑洞完全符合《圣经》中关于“地狱”位置的所有技术要求。
For their discovery that cosmic black holes fulfill all the technical requirements to be the location of Hell.

收集前苏联时代的雕像与遗物，创建了名为“斯大林世界”的主题游乐园。
For creating the open-air Soviet statue amusement park known as 'Stalin World.'
#09技术奖Technology
🏅 获奖者：John Keogh 与澳大利亚专利局（澳大利亚）🏅 Winners: John Keogh (Hawthorn, Victoria) and the Australian Patent Office
分别因在公元2001年为“轮子”申请专利，以及居然批准了这项第2001100012号专利而获奖。
For patenting the wheel in the year 2001, and for granting Innovation Patent #2001100012.

🏅 获奖者：Chittaranjan Andrade 与 B.S. Srihari（印度班加罗尔国家精神卫生与神经科学研究所）🏅 Winners: Chittaranjan Andrade and B.S. Srihari (National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences, Bangalore, India)
通过深入调查得出医学发现：挖鼻孔在青少年群体中是一种普遍活动。
For their probing medical discovery that nose picking (rhinotillexomania) is a common activity among adolescents.
2002 第12届搞笑诺贝尔奖 12th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 861 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 462 words · 10 Prizes

给印度大象算表面积与啤酒泡沫的指数衰减 Surface Area of Indian Elephants & Exponential Beer Froth Decay

从向饲养员求偶的英国鸵鸟、四条腿的元素周期表真桌子、肚脐眼绒毛普查，到华尔街把“虚数”写进财报，2002年妙趣横生。 From ostriches flirting with British farmers and a four-legged Periodic Table Table to Wall Street's imaginary numbers, 2002 turned everyday oddities into quantitative science.

📖 2002年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2002 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2002年第十二届搞笑诺贝尔奖将数学与物理的严谨发挥到了极致。数学奖颁给了印度喀拉拉邦农业大学的斯里库马尔与已故的尼尔马兰，他们为了帮兽医计算给大象用药的精确剂量，拿着卷尺测量了24头亚洲象，最终推导出通过肩高与前脚周长估算《印度象总表面积》的数学公式。德国慕尼黑大学的阿恩德·莱克则把实验室搬进了啤酒馆，通过严谨记录不同种类啤酒泡沫高度随时间的变化，证明啤酒泡沫的消散完美服从数学上的“指数衰减定律”，斩获物理学奖。而横跨美瑞两国的西奥多·格雷则玩起了英文“Table”的一语双关，亲手收集多种真实化学元素样本并打造成一张长着四条腿的木制“元素周期表桌子”，抱走化学奖。

在人与动物的奇妙互动中，英国学者诺玛·布比尔、帕克斯顿、鲍尔斯与迪明荣获生物学奖，他们的论文《英国农场饲养条件下鸵鸟对人类的求偶行为》发现，养殖场里的鸵鸟见到人类饲养员走近时，竟会频频扇动翅膀、曲膝大跳求偶舞，对人的热情远胜同类。为了跨越物种障碍，日本玩具公司社长佐藤庆太、音响专家铃木松美与兽医小暮规夫联合发明了计算机狗语自动翻译机“汪语通”，因促进人狗和谐共处而获和平奖；西班牙塔拉戈纳的爱德华多·塞古拉则发明了全自动猫狗宠物洗衣机，让阿猫阿狗享受喷淋清洗、消毒除虱与水力按摩一条龙服务，摘得卫生学奖。

对人类自身的观察同样令人捧腹。悉尼大学的卡尔·克鲁泽尔尼茨基对人类肚脐眼绒毛展开了史上最全面的普查，查清了肚脐毛球的产生时间、颜色与重量，证明多毛微胖中年男性的腹毛最易把衣物纤维卷进肚脐，荣获跨学科研究奖；伦敦大学学院的克里斯·麦克马纳斯则在《自然》杂志发表《人类与古代雕塑中的阴囊不对称性》，细致考证了真人与古希腊雕塑中左右睾丸的高低与大小差异，获颁医学奖；中密苏里州立大学的吉尔与克赖纳因证实二手书上原有的乱划重点会严重干扰后人阅读理解而获文学奖。至于年度经济学奖，则一举颁给了安然、世通、安达信、施乐、美林、默克、泰科、俄罗斯天然气工业等二十八家陷入财务丑闻的跨国巨头与审计机构，讽刺他们创造性地将数学中的“虚数”概念引入了商业财务报表！

The 2002 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony celebrated the triumph of mathematical rigor and literal-minded ingenuity over the messiness of the natural world. The Mathematics Prize honored K.P. Sreekumar and the late G. Nirmalan of Kerala Agricultural University in India for their painstaking report 'Estimation of the Total Surface Area in Indian Elephants,' which measured 24 Asian elephants to derive an equation predicting total pachyderm surface area from shoulder height and forefoot circumference. In Physics, Arnd Leike of the University of Munich demonstrated that a freshly poured mug of beer is a legitimate physics laboratory, proving that disappearing beer froth strictly obeys the mathematical Law of Exponential Decay. Meanwhile, American-Swiss author Theodore Gray won the Chemistry Prize for taking the phrase 'Periodic Table' literally—constructing a handsome four-legged wooden conference table containing actual physical samples of the chemical elements embedded under each square.

Interspecies romance, communication, and hygiene dominated the animal sciences. British researchers Norma Bubier, Charles G.M. Paxton, Phil Bowers, and D. Charles Deeming earned the Biology Prize for their paper 'Courtship Behaviour of Ostriches Towards Humans Under Farming Conditions in Britain,' documenting how farmed ostriches frequently flutter their wings and perform amorous mating dances for their human caretakers rather than for fellow ostriches. Bridging the communication gap with man’s best friend, Takara Co. president Keita Sato, acoustic scientist Dr. Matsumi Suzuki, and veterinarian Dr. Norio Kogure won the Peace Prize for inventing 'Bow-Lingual,' a computerized collar-and-microphone gadget that translates dog barks into human sentences. And for pets in need of a scrub, Spanish inventor Eduardo Segura of Lavakan de Aste received the Hygiene Prize for patenting a fully automated, coin-operated washing and drying machine for cats and dogs.

Turning the magnifying glass back onto human anatomy and folly yielded the final four honors. University of Sydney science broadcaster Karl Kruszelnicki won the Interdisciplinary Research Prize for his exhaustive survey of human belly button lint—establishing once and for all that slightly overweight, hairy middle-aged men wearing blue cotton shirts are the primary producers of navel fluff because abdominal hair channels fibers inward. In Medicine, Chris McManus of University College London received the prize for his balanced 1976 'Nature' report 'Scrotal Asymmetry in Man and in Ancient Sculpture,' noting that classical Greek sculptors accurately depicted the right testicle as higher than the left, yet erroneously sculpted the lower left testicle as larger. Literature honored Vicki Silvers Gier and David S. Kreiner of Central Missouri State University for proving that pre-existing, inappropriate yellow highlighter marks in used textbooks actively sabotage reading comprehension. Finally, the Economics Prize was awarded collectively to the executives, directors, and auditors of Enron, WorldCom, Arthur Andersen, Xerox, Merrill Lynch, Tyco, Gazprom, and 21 other scandal-ridden corporations for creatively adapting the mathematical concept of 'imaginary numbers' for use in corporate balance sheets.

#01生物学奖Biology
🏅 获奖者：Norma Bubier、Charles G.M. Paxton、Phil Bowers 与 D. Charles Deeming（英国）🏅 Winners: Norma Bubier, Charles G.M. Paxton, Phil Bowers, and D. Charles Deeming (UK)
发表研究报告《英国农场饲养条件下鸵鸟对人类的求偶行为》。
For their report 'Courtship Behaviour of Ostriches Towards Humans Under Farming Conditions in Britain.'
#02物理学奖Physics
🏅 获奖者：Arnd Leike（德国慕尼黑大学）🏅 Winners: Arnd Leike (University of Munich, Germany)
通过实验与数学分析证明啤酒泡沫的消散遵循数学上的“指数衰减定律”。
For demonstrating that beer froth obeys the mathematical Law of Exponential Decay.
#03跨学科研究奖Interdisciplinary Research
🏅 获奖者：Karl Kruszelnicki（澳大利亚悉尼大学）🏅 Winners: Karl Kruszelnicki (University of Sydney, Australia)
对人类肚脐眼绒毛进行全面普查——查明谁会产生、何时产生、什么颜色以及有多少。
For performing a comprehensive survey of human belly button lint—who gets it, when, what color, and how much.
#04化学奖Chemistry
🏅 获奖者：Theodore Gray（美国/瑞士）🏅 Winners: Theodore Gray (USA and Switzerland)
收集元素周期表中的多种真实化学元素，并将其组装成一张长着四条腿的“元素周期表桌子”。
For gathering many elements of the periodic table and assembling them into the form of a four-legged wooden 'Periodic Table Table.'
#05数学奖Mathematics
🏅 获奖者：K.P. Sreekumar 与已故的 G. Nirmalan（印度喀拉拉邦农业大学）🏅 Winners: K.P. Sreekumar and the late G. Nirmalan (Kerala Agricultural University, India)
发表分析报告《印度象总表面积的估算》，推导出根据肩高和前脚周长计算大象表面积的公式。
For their analytical report 'Estimation of the Total Surface Area in Indian Elephants.'
#06文学奖Literature
🏅 获奖者：Vicki Silvers Gier 与 David S. Kreiner（美国中密苏里州立大学）🏅 Winners: Vicki Silvers Gier and David S. Kreiner (Central Missouri State University)
发表报告《二手书上原有的不当荧光笔划线对阅读理解的影响》。
For their colorful report 'The Effects of Pre-Existing Inappropriate Highlighting on Reading Comprehension.'
#07和平奖Peace
🏅 获奖者：佐藤庆太、铃木松美博士与小暮规夫博士（日本）🏅 Winners: Keita Sato, Dr. Matsumi Suzuki, and Dr. Norio Kogure (Japan)
发明计算机狗语自动翻译机“Bow-Lingual”（汪语通），促进物种间的和平与和谐。
For promoting peace between the species by inventing Bow-Lingual, a computer-based automatic dog-to-human language translation device.
#08卫生学奖Hygiene
🏅 获奖者：Eduardo Segura（西班牙塔拉戈纳 Lavakan de Aste 公司）🏅 Winners: Eduardo Segura (Lavakan de Aste, Tarragona, Spain)
发明全自动猫狗宠物洗衣机，提供清洗、消毒、除虱与水力按摩服务。
For inventing an automated washing, disinfecting, and hydromassaging machine for cats and dogs.
#09经济学奖Economics
🏅 获奖者：安然（Enron）、世通（WorldCom）、安达信（Arthur Andersen）等28家公司高管与审计师🏅 Winners: Executives, directors, and auditors of Enron, WorldCom, Arthur Andersen, and 25 other companies
表彰他们将数学中的“虚数”（Imaginary numbers）概念创造性地应用于商业财务世界。
For adapting the mathematical concept of imaginary numbers for use in the corporate business world.
#10医学奖Medicine
🏅 获奖者：Chris McManus（英国伦敦大学学院 UCL）🏅 Winners: Chris McManus (University College London, UK)
在《自然》发表极其讲究平衡的报告《人类与古代雕塑中的阴囊不对称性》。
For his excruciatingly balanced 'Nature' report 'Scrotal Asymmetry in Man and in Ancient Sculpture.'
2003 第13届搞笑诺贝尔奖 13th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 871 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 510 words · 10 Prizes

墨菲定律的诞生、拖羊力学与伦敦司机的超级大脑 Murphy's Law, Sheep-Dragging Physics, and London Cabbies' Super-Brains

从凡事必出错的工程铁律到不招鸽子的青铜像与“死人协会” From the Engineering Iron Law of Catastrophe to Pigeon-Repelling Statues and the Association of Dead People

📖 2003年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2003 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2003年第十三届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院热闹揭晓，把“墨菲定律”式的幽默推向了高潮。工程学奖追授给已故的约翰·保罗·斯塔普、爱德华·墨菲以及尚在人世的乔治·尼科尔斯，表彰他们在1949年火箭雪橇试验中共同催生了那条令全人类瑟瑟发抖的铁律：“凡是可能出错的事，就一定会出错。”而在南半球的剪羊毛棚里，澳大利亚学者杰克·哈维、约翰·卡尔弗诺、沃伦·佩恩、史蒂夫·考利、迈克尔·劳伦斯、大卫·斯图尔特与罗宾·威廉姆斯对绵羊展开了严谨的力学测量，凭借《在各种表面上拖拽绵羊所需力量的分析》斩获物理学奖，证明倾斜木板配特定纹理地面拖羊最省力。

自然界与城市雕像同样充满了意外惊喜。荷兰鹿特丹自然历史博物馆的塞斯·莫利克夺得生物学奖，他在博物馆玻璃幕墙外亲眼目睹并科学记录了绿头鸭中首例有据可查的“同性恋恋尸癖”行为；瑞典斯德哥尔摩大学的斯特凡诺·吉尔兰达、莉塞洛特·扬松与马格努斯·恩奎斯特捧走跨学科研究奖，其论文《鸡更喜欢漂亮的人类》证实鸡对人类面孔颜值的审美偏好竟与大学生高度一致。日本金泽大学的广濑幸雄则因潜心化验金泽市一尊从不招惹鸽子的日本武尊青铜雕像而摘得化学奖——原来铜合金里富含剧毒的砷与铅，连鸽子都懂得趋吉避凶。

回到人类社会，伦敦大学学院的埃莉诺·马圭尔、大卫·加迪安、英格丽·约翰斯鲁德、卡特里奥娜·古德、约翰·阿什伯纳、理查德·弗拉科维亚克与克里斯托弗·弗里斯荣膺医学奖，脑部核磁共振扫描证实伦敦出租车司机的海马体比普通市民更发达。罗马大学的吉安·维托里奥·卡普拉拉、克劳迪奥·巴巴拉内利与斯坦福大学的菲利普·津巴多在心理学奖研究中指出，《政客独特而简单的性格》只需“精力”与“诚实”两个维度即可概括。纽约巴鲁克学院的约翰·特林考斯凭八十多篇统计反戴棒球帽、穿白球鞋、浅水区游来回及超市快速通道超件等日常烦心事的报告拿下文学奖；卡尔·施瓦茨勒与列支敦士登公国因推出“整国出租”服务办年会与婚礼赢得经济学奖；印度北方邦的拉尔·比哈里在被官方宣告“合法死亡”后顽强生活、发起死后维权运动并创立“死人协会”，众望所归地捧走和平奖。

The 13th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre in 2003 elevated everyday catastrophe to high art by honoring the birth of Murphy's Law. The Engineering Prize was awarded to the late John Paul Stapp, the late Edward A. Murphy, Jr., and George Nichols, who in 1949 formulated the immortal principle during rocket-sled deceleration tests: 'If there are two or more ways to do something, and one of those ways can result in a catastrophe, someone will do it'—better known as 'If anything can go wrong, it will.' Meanwhile, down in the shearing sheds of Australia, Jack Harvey, John Culvenor, Warren Payne, Steve Cowley, Michael Lawrance, David Stuart, and Robyn Williams captured the Physics Prize for their irresistible ergonomic treatise, 'An Analysis of the Forces Required to Drag Sheep over Various Surfaces,' proving that a 1-in-10 sloped ramp with parallel wooden slats offers the least frictional resistance when hauling a stubborn fifty-kilogram ewe.

Nature and urban statues proved equally full of surprises. C.W. (Kees) Moeliker of the Natuurhistorisch Museum Rotterdam won the Biology Prize after a mallard duck crashed into his museum's glass facade and another male mallard promptly arrived to perform the first scientifically documented case of homosexual necrophilia in the species. Over at Stockholm University, Stefano Ghirlanda, Liselotte Jansson, and Magnus Enquist claimed the Interdisciplinary Research Prize for 'Chickens Prefer Beautiful Humans,' demonstrating that chickens peck preferentially at composite faces rated most attractive by university students. In Japan, Yukio Hirose of Kanazawa University took home the Chemistry Prize for investigating why a bronze statue of the mythological hero Yamato Takeru in Kanazawa never attracts pigeons—revealing that the alloy was laced with arsenic and lead, which kept the birds wisely at bay.

Back in human society, Eleanor Maguire, David Gadian, Ingrid Johnsrude, Catriona Good, John Ashburner, Richard Frackowiak, and Christopher Frith of University College London earned the Medicine Prize by showing via MRI brain scans that London taxi drivers possess significantly more developed posterior hippocampi than ordinary citizens after mastering 'The Knowledge.' Conversely, Gian Vittorio Caprara and Claudio Barbaranelli of the University of Rome, joined by Stanford's Philip Zimbardo, won the Psychology Prize for 'Politicians' Uniquely Simple Personalities,' proving voters reduce politicians' characters from the usual Big Five traits down to just two: energy and honesty. New York business professor John Trinkaus received the Literature Prize for publishing more than eighty meticulous statistical reports about things that annoyed him—from the percentage of youths wearing baseball caps backward to shoppers exceeding item limits in express checkout lanes, drivers rolling through stop signs, and students who despise Brussels sprouts. Rounding out the night, Karl Schwärzler and the nation of Liechtenstein won the Economics Prize for making it possible to rent the entire country by the night for corporate conventions, weddings, and bar mitzvahs, while Lal Bihari of Uttar Pradesh, India, won the Peace Prize for a triple triumph: leading an active life after being declared legally dead by bribed officials, waging a spirited posthumous campaign against bureaucratic inertia and greedy relatives, and founding the Association of Dead People.

#01工程学奖 (Engineering)Engineering Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Paul Stapp, Edward A. Murphy, Jr., George Nichols🏅 Winners: John Paul Stapp, Edward A. Murphy, Jr., George Nichols
在1949年共同催生了著名的“墨菲定律”——如果做一件事有两条或更多途径，而其中一条会导致灾难，就一定有人会选那条路（即“凡是可能出错的事，就一定会出错”）。
For jointly giving birth in 1949 to Murphy's Law: 'If there are two or more ways to do something, and one of those ways can result in a catastrophe, someone will do it' ('If anything can go wrong, it will').
#02物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Jack Harvey, John Culvenor, Warren Payne, Steve Cowley, Michael Lawrance, David Stuart, Robyn Williams🏅 Winners: Jack Harvey, John Culvenor, Warren Payne, Steve Cowley, Michael Lawrance, David Stuart, Robyn Williams
发表令人难以抗拒的人体工程学报告《在各种表面上拖拽绵羊所需力量的分析》。
For their irresistible ergonomic report 'An Analysis of the Forces Required to Drag Sheep over Various Surfaces.'
#03医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Eleanor Maguire, David Gadian, Ingrid Johnsrude, Catriona Good, John Ashburner, Richard Frackowiak, Christopher Frith🏅 Winners: Eleanor Maguire, David Gadian, Ingrid Johnsrude, Catriona Good, John Ashburner, Richard Frackowiak, Christopher Frith
提供确凿的脑成像证据，证明伦敦出租车司机的大脑海马体比普通市民更加发达。
For presenting neuroimaging evidence that the brains (specifically the hippocampi) of London taxi drivers are more highly developed than those of their fellow citizens.
#04心理学奖 (Psychology)Psychology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gian Vittorio Caprara, Claudio Barbaranelli, Philip Zimbardo🏅 Winners: Gian Vittorio Caprara, Claudio Barbaranelli, Philip Zimbardo
发表极具洞察力的心理学报告《政客独特而简单的性格》。
For their discerning report in Nature, 'Politicians' Uniquely Simple Personalities.'
#05化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：广濑幸雄 (Yukio Hirose)🏅 Winners: Yukio Hirose
对日本金泽市一尊从不吸引鸽子驻足的青铜雕像展开化学调查，发现其中含有砷和铅。
For his chemical investigation of a bronze statue in the city of Kanazawa that fails to attract pigeons due to its arsenic and lead content.
#06文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Trinkaus🏅 Winners: John Trinkaus
一丝不苟地收集数据并发表了80多篇关于日常烦心事的学术报告（如反戴棒球帽、穿白运动鞋、浅水区游泳、超市快速通道超件等比例）。
For meticulously collecting data and publishing more than 80 detailed academic reports about everyday things that annoyed him (such as backward baseball caps, white sport shoes, shallow-end lap swimmers, rolling stops, and express-lane violators).
#07经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Karl Schwärzler 与列支敦士登公国 (Nation of Liechtenstein)🏅 Winners: Karl Schwärzler and the Nation of Liechtenstein
使人们能够整租列支敦士登整个国家来举办企业年会、婚礼、成人礼及其他聚会。
For making it possible to rent the entire country of Liechtenstein for corporate conventions, weddings, bar mitzvahs, and other gatherings.
#08跨学科研究奖 (Interdisciplinary Research)Interdisciplinary Research Prize
🏅 获奖者：Stefano Ghirlanda, Liselotte Jansson, Magnus Enquist🏅 Winners: Stefano Ghirlanda, Liselotte Jansson, Magnus Enquist
发表实验研究报告《鸡更喜欢漂亮的人类》。
For their experimental report 'Chickens Prefer Beautiful Humans.'
#09和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Lal Bihari🏅 Winners: Lal Bihari
达成三重壮举：在被宣告“合法死亡”后依然积极生活；发起生机勃勃的死后运动对抗官僚惰性与贪婪亲戚；创立“死人协会”。
For a triple accomplishment: leading an active life despite being declared legally dead, waging a lively posthumous campaign against bureaucratic inertia and greedy relatives, and creating the Association of Dead People.
#10生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：C.W. Moeliker (Kees Moeliker)🏅 Winners: C.W. Moeliker (Kees Moeliker)
科学记录并发表了绿头鸭中首例有据可查的同性恋恋尸癖行为。
For documenting the first scientifically recorded case of homosexual necrophilia in the mallard duck (Anas platyrhynchos).

看不见的大猩猩、五秒规则与放屁交流的鲱鱼 Invisible Gorillas, the Five-Second Rule, and Farting Herrings

从卡拉OK和平奖到地方支援中央梳头法与外包祈祷 From the Karaoke Peace Prize to Patented Combovers and Outsourced Vatican Prayers

📖 2004年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2004 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2004年第十四届搞笑诺贝尔奖将聚光灯投向了人类视觉盲区与日常生活的奇思妙想。心理学奖颁给伊利诺伊大学的丹尼尔·西蒙斯与哈佛大学的克里斯托弗·查布里斯，他们用经典的“看不见的大猩猩”实验证明：当人们全神贯注于数传球次数时，哪怕一个穿大猩猩道具服的女人大摇大摆走过球场中央，也会被半数观察者彻底忽略。在物理学奖得主、渥太华大学的拉梅什·巴拉苏布拉马尼安与康涅狄格大学及哈斯金斯实验室的迈克尔·特维眼中，转呼啦圈则是复杂的多体节生物控制论课题。佛罗里达州奥兰多的唐纳德·史密斯及其已故父亲弗兰克·史密斯，则因给掩盖秃顶的“地方支援中央”式梳头法申请美国专利而摘下工程学奖。

声音与海洋同样暗藏玄机。日本兵库县的井上大佑因发明卡拉OK荣膺和平奖，评委会盛赞他为人类提供了一种全新的“学会互相容忍”的方式；而在大洋深处，加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚大学的本·威尔逊、西蒙菲莎大学的劳伦斯·迪尔、苏格兰海洋科学协会的罗伯特·巴蒂、丹麦奥胡斯大学的马格努斯·瓦尔伯格与瑞典国家渔业局的哈坎·韦斯特伯格共同夺得生物学奖，他们发现鲱鱼在黑暗中竟是通过肛门排出气泡、“放屁”发声来互通情报的。相比之下，美国韦恩州立大学的史蒂文·斯塔克与奥本大学的詹姆斯·冈德拉赫拿下略带忧伤的医学奖，其统计报告《乡村音乐对自杀的影响》指出广播里乡村音乐播放量越大的城市，白人自杀率往往越高。

饮食、信仰与文献领域同样妙趣横生。当时就读于芝加哥农业科学高中及霍华德大学的吉莉安·克拉克凭借检验“食物掉在地上五秒内捡起来还能不能吃”的“五秒规则”赢得公共卫生奖，证实地面一旦有细菌，食物接触瞬间即被污染。英国可口可乐公司则尴尬地领走化学奖，因为他们利用所谓“尖端技术”把普通自来水包装成透明瓶装水“达萨尼”，却因检出致癌物溴酸盐超标而不得不紧急召回、禁止向消费者供应。此外，梵蒂冈因将海量弥撒祈祷业务外包给印度神父而斩获经济学奖；位于佛罗里达州基西米的美国天体主义研究图书馆则因妥善保存裸体主义历史文献、“以便每个人都能一览无余”，幽默地捧走了文学奖。

The 14th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2004 shone a bright light on human blind spots and ingenious everyday inventions. The Psychology Prize went to Daniel Simons of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and Christopher Chabris of Harvard University for their legendary 'Gorillas in Our Midst' experiment, which proved that when people pay close attention to counting basketball passes, roughly half fail to notice a woman in a gorilla suit strolling right through the scene and beating her chest. Movement of a more circular kind captivated Physics Prize winners Ramesh Balasubramaniam of the University of Ottawa and Michael Turvey of the University of Connecticut and Haskins Laboratory, who modeled the multisegmental biomechanics and coordination modes required to keep a hula hoop spinning. Meanwhile, Donald J. Smith and his late father, Frank J. Smith of Orlando, Florida, earned the Engineering Prize for U.S. Patent #4,022,227: the strategic three-directional 'combover' designed to conceal baldness without a wig.

Soundwaves above and below water yielded equally memorable breakthroughs. Daisuke Inoue of Hyogo, Japan, won the Peace Prize for inventing karaoke, receiving a standing ovation at Sanders Theatre for 'providing an entirely new way for people to learn to tolerate each other.' Deep beneath the waves, an international team—Ben Wilson of the University of British Columbia, Lawrence Dill of Simon Fraser University, Robert Batty of the Scottish Association for Marine Science, Magnus Wahlberg of the University of Aarhus, and Håkan Westerberg of Sweden's National Board of Fisheries—shared the Biology Prize for discovering that Pacific and Atlantic herrings communicate in the dark by squeezing gas bubbles out of their anal ducts, producing high-frequency 'Fast Repetitive Tick' (FRT) farting sounds. On a more somber acoustic note, Steven Stack of Wayne State University and James Gundlach of Auburn University received the Medicine Prize for 'The Effect of Country Music on Suicide,' showing that metropolitan areas with greater country music radio airtime experience higher white suicide rates.

Public health, corporate chemistry, and globalized faith rounded out the 2004 roster. High school apprentice Jillian Clarke of the Chicago High School for Agricultural Sciences and Howard University won the Public Health Prize for putting the folkloric 'Five-Second Rule' to the laboratory test—discovering that E. coli bacteria transfer to dropped gummy bears and cookies almost instantaneously on smooth tiles, and also noting that women are more likely than men to eat dropped food. The Chemistry Prize was bestowed upon The Coca-Cola Company of Great Britain for using 'advanced technology' to convert ordinary Thames tap water into Dasani bottled water, only to pull the entire product line from British shelves after it was found contaminated with carcinogenic bromate. Finally, the Vatican won the Economics Prize for outsourcing excess Mass prayer requests to priests in India, while the American Nudist Research Library of Kissimmee, Florida, took home the Literature Prize for 'preserving nudist history so that everyone can see it.'

#01医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Steven Stack, James Gundlach🏅 Winners: Steven Stack, James Gundlach
发表社会学与医学统计报告《乡村音乐对自杀的影响》，探讨乡村音乐广播比例与城市自杀率的相关性。
For their published sociological and medical report 'The Effect of Country Music on Suicide.'
#02物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Ramesh Balasubramaniam, Michael Turvey🏅 Winners: Ramesh Balasubramaniam, Michael Turvey
从多体节生物控制论角度探索并解释了转呼啦圈的动力学原理。
For exploring and explaining the multisegmental dynamics and coordination modes of hula-hooping.
#03公共卫生奖 (Public Health)Public Health Prize
🏅 获奖者：Jillian Clarke🏅 Winners: Jillian Clarke
科学检验了关于“掉在地上的食物五秒钟内捡起来是否还能安全食用”的“五秒规则”（Five-Second Rule）。
For investigating the scientific validity of the 'Five-Second Rule' about whether it is safe to eat food that has been dropped on the floor.
#04化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：英国可口可乐公司 (The Coca-Cola Company of Great Britain)🏅 Winners: The Coca-Cola Company of Great Britain
利用“先进技术”将普通自来水转化为透明的达萨尼（Dasani）瓶装水，随后出于预防性安全原因不得不将其全面下架召回。
For using advanced technology to convert ordinary tap water into Dasani, a transparent form of water, which for precautionary reasons was then made unavailable to consumers.
#05工程学奖 (Engineering)Engineering Prize
🏅 获奖者：Donald J. Smith, Frank J. Smith🏅 Winners: Donald J. Smith, Frank J. Smith
为掩盖谢顶的“地方支援中央”式梳头法（Combover）申请并获得了美国专利（US Patent #4,022,227）。
For patenting the combover (U.S. Patent #4,022,227).
#06文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：美国天体主义研究图书馆 (The American Nudist Research Library)🏅 Winners: The American Nudist Research Library
妥善保存天体主义（裸体主义）历史文献，“以便每个人都能一览无余”。
For preserving nudist history in Kissimmee, Florida, so that everyone can see it.
#07心理学奖 (Psychology)Psychology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Daniel Simons, Christopher Chabris🏅 Winners: Daniel Simons, Christopher Chabris
通过著名的“看不见的大猩猩”实验证明，当人们高度专注于某件事时，极易忽略眼前的其他事物——哪怕是一个穿着大猩猩套装的人。
For demonstrating that when people pay close attention to something, it is all too easy to overlook anything else—even a woman in a gorilla suit.
#08经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：梵蒂冈 (The Vatican)🏅 Winners: The Vatican
将信徒的弥撒祈祷业务外包给印度的神父代为执行。
For outsourcing Mass prayers to priests in India.
#09和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：井上大佑 (Daisuke Inoue)🏅 Winners: Daisuke Inoue
发明了卡拉OK，从而为人类提供了一种全新的“学会互相容忍”的方式。
For inventing karaoke, thereby providing an entirely new way for people to learn to tolerate each other.
#10生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Ben Wilson, Lawrence Dill, Robert Batty, Magnus Wahlberg, Håkan Westerberg🏅 Winners: Ben Wilson, Lawrence Dill, Robert Batty, Magnus Wahlberg, Håkan Westerberg
共同发现太平洋与大西洋鲱鱼在黑暗中显然是通过“放屁”（肛门排出气泡发声）来进行群体交流的。
For showing that Pacific and Atlantic herrings apparently communicate by farting (releasing anal gas bubbles).
2005 第15届搞笑诺贝尔奖 15th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 846 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 487 words · 10 Prizes

企鹅排便压强、沥青滴漏与糖浆游泳赛 Penguin Poo Pressure, the 78-Year Pitch Drop, and Swimming in Syrup

从会逃跑的闹钟到新西兰爆炸裤子与看《星球大战》的蝗虫 From Runaway Alarm Clocks to Exploding New Zealand Trousers and Star Wars-Watching Locusts

📖 2005年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2005 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2005年第十五届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了跨越世纪的惊人耐心与脑洞大开的奇观。物理学奖授予澳大利亚昆士兰大学的约翰·梅恩斯通与已故的托马斯·帕内尔，表彰他们自1927年起苦苦守候的“沥青滴漏实验”——漏斗中凝固的黑色沥青平均每九年才缓慢滴落一滴。同样考验耐力的还有营养学奖得主、日本东京发明家中松义郎博士，他连续三十四年为自己吃下的每一顿饭拍照并进行回顾性分析。而在新西兰梅西大学，詹姆斯·沃森凭借学术论文《理查德·巴克利先生爆炸的裤子之重要意义》摘得农业史奖，生动还原了二十世纪三十年代新西兰奶农用氯酸钠除草剂喷洒杂草后，药液沾染裤子干燥遇火猛烈爆炸的历史。

流体与气味的研究更是令人捧腹。德国不来梅国际大学及芬兰奥卢大学的维克托·本诺·迈耶-罗乔与匈牙利罗兰大学的约瑟夫·加尔荣膺流体力学奖，他们运用基础物理学公式严谨计算了企鹅排便时体内积聚的惊人压强，发表了《企鹅排便时产生的压力——鸟类排便计算》。明尼苏达大学的爱德华·卡斯勒与威斯康星大学的布莱恩·格特尔芬格则往泳池里倒入瓜尔胶，通过实验解答“人在糖浆里游泳比在水里更快还是更慢”而拿下化学奖，证实二者速度几乎难分伯仲。生物学奖颁给本杰明·史密斯、克雷格·威廉姆斯、迈克尔·泰勒、布莱恩·威廉姆斯与早坂洋司，他们不辞辛劳地逐一嗅闻并分类记录了131种蛙类在感到压力时分泌的奇特气味。

动物福利、昆虫观影与现代科技也各显神通。密苏里州的格雷格·米勒因发明具有三种尺寸和三种软硬度的绝育公狗人造替代睾丸“Neuticles”赢得医学奖；英国纽卡斯尔大学的克莱尔·林德与彼得·西蒙斯在蝗虫观看电影《星球大战》精彩片段时，用电极监测其脑细胞活动，奇妙地捧走和平奖。麻省理工学院的高里·南达发明了会反复逃跑并躲藏起来的闹钟，因理论上能迫使人们准时下床、增加每日有效工作时长而斩获经济学奖；尼日利亚的“互联网创业者们”则因通过电子邮件向全球群发短篇故事，塑造阿巴查将军、阿巴查夫人与姆贝基大律师等急需一小笔手续费以解锁巨额财富的富豪角色，一举夺得文学奖。

The 15th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2005 celebrated monumental scientific patience alongside explosive historical curiosities. The Physics Prize went to John Mainstone and the late Thomas Parnell of the University of Queensland, Australia, who had patiently tended the famous Pitch Drop Experiment since 1927, watching a congealed glob of black tar ooze through a glass funnel at the glacial rate of roughly one drop every nine years. A rival feat of multi-decade dedication earned Dr. Yoshiro Nakamats of Tokyo the Nutrition Prize for photographing and retrospectively analyzing every single meal he had consumed over a period of thirty-four years (and counting). Meanwhile, James Watson of Massey University, New Zealand, captured the Agricultural History Prize for his scholarly paper 'The Significance of Mr. Richard Buckley's Exploding Trousers,' recounting how interwar New Zealand dairy farmers spraying ragwort weeds with sodium chlorate herbicide inadvertently turned their cotton pants into violently combustible garments.

Fluid mechanics and olfactory endurance took center stage in the middle rounds. Victor Benno Meyer-Rochow of International University Bremen and the University of Oulu, together with Jozsef Gal of Loránd Eötvös University in Hungary, won the Fluid Dynamics Prize for 'Pressures Produced When Penguins Pooh—Calculations on Avian Defaecation,' computing that penguins build up between 10 and 60 kilopascals of rectal pressure to fling guano forty centimeters clear of their nests. Over in Minnesota, chemical engineers Edward Cussler and Brian Gettelfinger thickened a twenty-five-meter swimming pool with guar gum to win the Chemistry Prize, settling a classic debate by proving that humans swim at virtually the same speed in syrup as they do in water. And an intrepid team led by Benjamin Smith, Craig Williams, Michael Tyler, Brian Williams, and Yoji Hayasaka earned the Biology Prize for painstakingly smelling and cataloging the stressed-out skin secretions of 131 different species of frogs—ranging from nutty and floral to rotten fish.

Canine dignity, cinephile insects, and digital storytelling rounded out the 2005 honors. Gregg A. Miller of Oak Grove, Missouri, received the Medicine Prize for inventing Neuticles—prosthetic replacement testicles for neutered dogs, offered in three sizes and three degrees of firmness so pets can retain their self-esteem. Newcastle University neurobiologists Claire Rind and Peter Simmons won the Peace Prize for wiring up a locust's brain to monitor its Descending Contralateral Movement Detector neuron while the insect watched action highlights from the movie 'Star Wars.' MIT graduate student Gauri Nanda claimed the Economics Prize for inventing Clocky, a wheeled alarm clock that leaps off the nightstand and hides repeatedly, forcing sleepers out of bed and theoretically adding productive hours to the global workday. Finally, the Literature Prize honored the 'Internet entrepreneurs of Nigeria' for using e-mail to distribute a bold series of short stories introducing millions of readers to a cast of wealthy characters—General Sani Abacha, Mrs. Mariam Sanni Abacha, Barrister Jon A. Mbeki Esq., and others—each requiring just a small advance fee to unlock and share a vast fortune.

2005年第十五届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了跨越世纪的惊人耐心与脑洞大开的奇观。物理学奖授予澳大利亚昆士兰大学的约翰·梅恩斯通与已故的托马斯·帕内尔，表彰他们自1927年起苦苦守候的“沥青滴漏实验”——漏斗中凝固的黑色沥青平均每九年才缓慢滴落一滴。同样考验耐力的还有营养学奖得主、日本东京发明家中松义郎博士，他连续三十四年为自己吃下的每一顿饭拍照并进行回顾性分析。而在新西兰梅西大学，詹姆斯·沃森凭借学术论文《理查德·巴克利先生爆炸的裤子之重要意义》摘得农业史奖，生动还原了二十世纪三十年代新西兰奶农用氯酸钠除草剂喷洒杂草后，药液沾染裤子干燥遇火猛烈爆炸的历史。

The 15th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2005 celebrated monumental scientific patience alongside explosive historical curiosities. The Physics Prize went to John Mainstone and the late Thomas Parnell of the University of Queensland, Australia, who had patiently tended the famous Pitch Drop Experiment since 1927, watching a congealed glob of black tar ooze through a glass funnel at the glacial rate of roughly one drop every nine years. A rival feat of multi-decade dedication earned Dr. Yoshiro Nakamats of Tokyo the Nutrition Prize for photographing and retrospectively analyzing every single meal he had consumed over a period of thirty-four years (and counting). Meanwhile, James Watson of Massey University, New Zealand, captured the Agricultural History Prize for his scholarly paper 'The Significance of Mr. Richard Buckley's Exploding Trousers,' recounting how interwar New Zealand dairy farmers spraying ragwort weeds with sodium chlorate herbicide inadvertently turned their cotton pants into violently combustible garments.

流体与气味的研究更是令人捧腹。德国不来梅国际大学及芬兰奥卢大学的维克托·本诺·迈耶-罗乔与匈牙利罗兰大学的约瑟夫·加尔荣膺流体力学奖，他们运用基础物理学公式严谨计算了企鹅排便时体内积聚的惊人压强，发表了《企鹅排便时产生的压力——鸟类排便计算》。明尼苏达大学的爱德华·卡斯勒与威斯康星大学的布莱恩·格特尔芬格则往泳池里倒入瓜尔胶，通过实验解答“人在糖浆里游泳比在水里更快还是更慢”而拿下化学奖，证实二者速度几乎难分伯仲。生物学奖颁给本杰明·史密斯、克雷格·威廉姆斯、迈克尔·泰勒、布莱恩·威廉姆斯与早坂洋司，他们不辞辛劳地逐一嗅闻并分类记录了131种蛙类在感到压力时分泌的奇特气味。

Fluid mechanics and olfactory endurance took center stage in the middle rounds. Victor Benno Meyer-Rochow of International University Bremen and the University of Oulu, together with Jozsef Gal of Loránd Eötvös University in Hungary, won the Fluid Dynamics Prize for 'Pressures Produced When Penguins Pooh—Calculations on Avian Defaecation,' computing that penguins build up between 10 and 60 kilopascals of rectal pressure to fling guano forty centimeters clear of their nests. Over in Minnesota, chemical engineers Edward Cussler and Brian Gettelfinger thickened a twenty-five-meter swimming pool with guar gum to win the Chemistry Prize, settling a classic debate by proving that humans swim at virtually the same speed in syrup as they do in water. And an intrepid team led by Benjamin Smith, Craig Williams, Michael Tyler, Brian Williams, and Yoji Hayasaka earned the Biology Prize for painstakingly smelling and cataloging the stressed-out skin secretions of 131 different species of frogs—ranging from nutty and floral to rotten fish.

动物福利、昆虫观影与现代科技也各显神通。密苏里州的格雷格·米勒因发明具有三种尺寸和三种软硬度的绝育公狗人造替代睾丸“Neuticles”赢得医学奖；英国纽卡斯尔大学的克莱尔·林德与彼得·西蒙斯在蝗虫观看电影《星球大战》精彩片段时，用电极监测其脑细胞活动，奇妙地捧走和平奖。麻省理工学院的高里·南达发明了会反复逃跑并躲藏起来的闹钟，因理论上能迫使人们准时下床、增加每日有效工作时长而斩获经济学奖；尼日利亚的“互联网创业者们”则因通过电子邮件向全球群发短篇故事，塑造阿巴查将军、阿巴查夫人与姆贝基大律师等急需一小笔手续费以解锁巨额财富的富豪角色，一举夺得文学奖。

Canine dignity, cinephile insects, and digital storytelling rounded out the 2005 honors. Gregg A. Miller of Oak Grove, Missouri, received the Medicine Prize for inventing Neuticles—prosthetic replacement testicles for neutered dogs, offered in three sizes and three degrees of firmness so pets can retain their self-esteem. Newcastle University neurobiologists Claire Rind and Peter Simmons won the Peace Prize for wiring up a locust's brain to monitor its Descending Contralateral Movement Detector neuron while the insect watched action highlights from the movie 'Star Wars.' MIT graduate student Gauri Nanda claimed the Economics Prize for inventing Clocky, a wheeled alarm clock that leaps off the nightstand and hides repeatedly, forcing sleepers out of bed and theoretically adding productive hours to the global workday. Finally, the Literature Prize honored the 'Internet entrepreneurs of Nigeria' for using e-mail to distribute a bold series of short stories introducing millions of readers to a cast of wealthy characters—General Sani Abacha, Mrs. Mariam Sanni Abacha, Barrister Jon A. Mbeki Esq., and others—each requiring just a small advance fee to unlock and share a vast fortune.

#01农业史奖 (Agricultural History)Agricultural History Prize
🏅 获奖者：James Watson🏅 Winners: James Watson
发表学术研究《理查德·巴克利先生爆炸的裤子之重要意义》，探讨两次世界大战之间新西兰奶农因氯酸钠除草剂导致裤子起火爆炸的历史。
For his scholarly study 'The Significance of Mr. Richard Buckley's Exploding Trousers,' examining how sodium chlorate weedkiller caused New Zealand dairy farmers' trousers to detonate between the World Wars.
#02物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Mainstone, Thomas Parnell🏅 Winners: John Mainstone, Thomas Parnell
耐心地主持自1927年启动的“沥青滴漏实验”——漏斗中凝固的黑色沥青以大约每九年一滴的速度缓慢滴落。
For patiently conducting the Pitch Drop Experiment that began in 1927, in which a glob of congealed black tar drips through a funnel at a rate of approximately one drop every nine years.
#03医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gregg A. Miller🏅 Winners: Gregg A. Miller
发明了专供绝育公狗植入的人造替代睾丸“Neuticles”，提供三种尺寸与三种软硬度选择。
For inventing Neuticles—artificial replacement testicles for neutered dogs, available in three sizes and three degrees of firmness.
#04文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：尼日利亚的互联网创业者们 (The Internet entrepreneurs of Nigeria)🏅 Winners: The Internet Entrepreneurs of Nigeria
创作并利用电子邮件分发一系列短篇故事，向数百万读者介绍了阿巴查将军、姆贝基大律师等只需一小笔手续费就能与好心人平分巨额遗产的角色。
For creating and using e-mail to distribute a bold series of short stories introducing millions of readers to rich characters who require just a small advance expense fee to share their vast wealth.
#05和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Claire Rind, Peter Simmons🏅 Winners: Claire Rind, Peter Simmons
在蝗虫观看电影《星球大战》精选片段时，用电极实时监测这只蝗虫脑细胞的电活动反应。
For electrically monitoring the activity of a motion-detecting brain cell in a locust while that locust was watching selected highlights from the movie 'Star Wars.'
#06经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gauri Nanda🏅 Winners: Gauri Nanda
发明了会反复逃跑并躲藏起来的闹钟（Clocky），确保人们必须起床，理论上为工作日增加了许多高效工时。
For inventing Clocky, an alarm clock on wheels that runs away and hides repeatedly, ensuring people get out of bed and theoretically adding productive hours to the workday.
#07化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Edward Cussler, Brian Gettelfinger🏅 Winners: Edward Cussler, Brian Gettelfinger
通过严谨的泳池对比实验解答了困扰科学界已久的问题：人在糖浆里游泳比在水里更快还是更慢？
For conducting a careful experiment in a guar-gum-thickened pool to settle the longstanding scientific question: can people swim faster in syrup or in water?
#08生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Benjamin Smith, Craig Williams, Michael Tyler, Brian Williams, Yoji Hayasaka🏅 Winners: Benjamin Smith, Craig Williams, Michael Tyler, Brian Williams, Yoji Hayasaka
不辞辛劳地嗅闻并分类记录了131种不同蛙类在感到压力时分泌的奇特气味。
For painstakingly smelling and cataloging the peculiar odors produced by 131 different species of frogs when the frogs were feeling stressed.
#09营养学奖 (Nutrition)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：中松义郎博士 (Dr. Yoshiro Nakamats)🏅 Winners: Dr. Yoshiro Nakamats
在长达34年（且仍在继续）的时间里，对自己吃下的每一顿饭进行拍照并展开回顾性分析。
For photographing and retrospectively analyzing every meal he has consumed during a period of 34 years (and counting).
#10流体力学奖 (Fluid Dynamics)Fluid Dynamics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Victor Benno Meyer-Rochow, Jozsef Gal🏅 Winners: Victor Benno Meyer-Rochow, Jozsef Gal
运用基础物理学原理计算企鹅排便时体内积聚的压强，发表报告《企鹅排便时产生的压力——鸟类排便计算》。
For using basic principles of physics to calculate the pressure that builds up inside a defecating penguin in 'Pressures Produced When Penguins Pooh—Calculations on Avian Defaecation.'

📖 2006年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2006 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2006年第十六届搞笑诺贝尔奖在日常声光与生物奥秘中寻找笑点。鸟类学奖颁给加州大学戴维斯分校的伊万·施瓦布与加州大学洛杉矶分校已故的菲利普·梅，他们深入解释了啄木鸟每天狂啄树干上万次却不会得头痛或脑震荡的颅骨防震机制。科威特大学的瓦斯米亚·胡提与科威特环境公共管理局的法滕·穆萨拉姆斩获营养学奖，证明屎壳郎其实是不折不扣的挑食美食家；荷兰瓦赫宁根农业大学等的巴特·克诺尔斯与鲁尔德·德容则夺得生物学奖，他们发现传播疟疾的雌性冈比亚按蚊对林堡干酪气味和人类脚臭味的喜爱程度竟然旗鼓相当，毫无二致。

物理、化学与数学家们在餐桌和相机前大显身手。巴黎第六大学的巴西勒·奥多利与塞巴斯蒂安·诺伊基希荣获物理学奖，他们揭示了弯曲干意大利面条时，首次断裂瞬间释放的弹性波为何总让面条碎成三截或更多截，而非整齐的两截。西班牙瓦伦西亚大学的安东尼奥·穆莱特、何塞·哈维尔·贝内迪托、何塞·邦与巴利阿里群岛大学的卡门·罗塞略凭《温度对切达干酪中超声波传播速度的影响》拿下化学奖。澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织的尼克·斯文森与皮尔斯·巴恩斯则斩获数学奖，精确推算出拍集体照时必须连拍多少张照片，才能几乎保证现场没有任何人闭眼。

感官刺激与语言医学同样令人拍案叫绝。林恩·哈尔彭、伦道夫·布莱克与詹姆斯·希伦布兰德因实验探究人类为何极度讨厌指甲刮黑板的声音而赢得声学奖；威尔士的霍华德·斯塔普尔顿发明了发出高频刺耳噪音驱赶青少年而成年人听不见的装置，后来又用同一技术制成学生听得见但老师听不见的手机隐形铃声，奇妙地捧走和平奖。普林斯顿大学的丹尼尔·奥本海默凭论文《无论必要与否均使用博学语汇之后果：不必要地使用长词的问题》摘得文学奖，证明故意堆砌生僻大词反而会让人显得更蠢；美国田纳西大学医学院的弗朗西斯·费斯迈尔与以色列海法本·锡安医疗中心的马吉德·奥德、哈里·巴桑、阿里·奥利文则因先后发表同名医学病例报告《用手指直肠按摩终止顽固性打嗝》，共同分享了医学奖。

The 16th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2006 found high comedy in everyday acoustics, kitchen physics, and picky creatures. The Ornithology Prize went to Ivan R. Schwab of the University of California, Davis, and the late Philip R.A. May of UCLA for explaining why woodpeckers can hammer tree trunks twelve thousand times a day at decelerations of 1,000 g without getting headaches or concussions—thanks to spongy cranial bones, tightly packed brains, and millisecond-timed third eyelids. Culinary discernment in the insect world earned two prizes: Wasmia Al-Houty of Kuwait University and Faten Al-Mussalam of the Kuwait Environment Public Authority won the Nutrition Prize for proving that Scarabaeus cristatus dung beetles are finicky eaters that strongly prefer horse and sheep dung over camel or fox droppings, while Bart Knols and Ruurd de Jong of Wageningen Agricultural University won the Biology Prize for demonstrating that the female malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae is attracted equally to the odor of Limburger cheese and the smell of unwashed human feet.

Physicists, chemists, and mathematicians tackled puzzles of the dinner table and the family camera. Basile Audoly and Sebastien Neukirch of the Université Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris won the Physics Prize for solving a mystery that had baffled Nobel laureate Richard Feynman: why bending dry spaghetti almost always snaps it into three or more pieces rather than two (the initial break unleashes elastic flexural waves that spike curvature along the remaining rod). In Spain, Antonio Mulet, José Javier Benedito, José Bon, and Carmen Rosselló claimed the Chemistry Prize for 'Ultrasonic Velocity in Cheddar Cheese as Affected by Temperature,' showing ultrasound travels fastest through cheddar between 0 and 17 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, Nic Svenson and Piers Barnes of Australia's CSIRO won the Mathematics Prize for deriving a rule-of-thumb formula calculating how many photos you must snap of a group of N people to almost guarantee that nobody has their eyes closed.

Acoustic torment, pretentious prose, and emergency medicine delivered the evening's final laughs. D. Lynn Halpern, Randolph Blake, and James Hillenbrand won the Acoustics Prize for investigating why the sound of fingernails scraping on a blackboard sends chills down the human spine, pinpointing mid-range frequencies between 2,000 and 4,000 hertz rather than the highest pitches. Welsh inventor Howard Stapleton received the Peace Prize for creating the 'Mosquito' electromechanical teenager repellent—which emits a high-frequency buzz audible to loitering youths but inaudible to adults over thirty—and then reverse-engineering the technology into 'secret' schoolroom cellphone ringtones that students can hear while their teachers remain oblivious. Princeton psychologist Daniel Oppenheimer won the Literature Prize for 'Consequences of Erudite Vernacular Utilized Irrespective of Necessity: Problems with Using Long Words Needlessly,' proving that pompous vocabulary makes authors sound less intelligent. Finally, Francis M. Fesmire of the University of Tennessee and the Israeli team of Majed Odeh, Harry Bassan, and Arie Oliven of Bnai Zion Medical Center shared the Medicine Prize for their identically titled clinical case reports: 'Termination of Intractable Hiccups with Digital Rectal Massage.'

#01鸟类学奖 (Ornithology)Ornithology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Ivan R. Schwab, Philip R.A. May🏅 Winners: Ivan R. Schwab, Philip R.A. May
探索并解释了为什么啄木鸟每天高速撞击树干却不会患上头痛或脑震荡。
For exploring and explaining the anatomical shock-absorption mechanisms that prevent woodpeckers from getting headaches.
#02营养学奖 (Nutrition)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：Wasmia Al-Houty, Faten Al-Mussalam🏅 Winners: Wasmia Al-Houty, Faten Al-Mussalam
通过实验证明蜣螂（屎壳郎）其实是对不同动物粪便十分挑剔的食客。
For showing that Scarabaeus cristatus dung beetles in Kuwait are finicky eaters with distinct dung preferences.
#03和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Howard Stapleton🏅 Winners: Howard Stapleton
发明了发出青少年听得到而成年人听不到的高频噪音“青少年驱逐器”，后又利用该技术制作了学生听得见而老师听不见的手机铃声。
For inventing an electromechanical teenager repellent that makes high-pitched noise audible to teenagers but not to adults, and later using that same technology to make ringtones audible to students but not to their teachers.
#04声学奖 (Acoustics)Acoustics Prize
🏅 获奖者：D. Lynn Halpern, Randolph Blake, James Hillenbrand🏅 Winners: D. Lynn Halpern, Randolph Blake, James Hillenbrand
开展心理声学实验以查明为什么人们如此讨厌指甲刮黑板的声音。
For conducting psychoacoustic experiments to learn why people dislike the chilling sound of fingernails scraping on a blackboard.
#05数学奖 (Mathematics)Mathematics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Nic Svenson, Piers Barnes🏅 Winners: Nic Svenson, Piers Barnes
计算出拍摄集体照时必须连拍多少张照片，才能（几乎）确保没有任何人闭眼。
For calculating the number of photographs you must take to (almost) ensure that nobody in a group photo will have their eyes closed.
#06文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：Daniel Oppenheimer🏅 Winners: Daniel Oppenheimer
发表论文《无论必要与否均使用博学语汇之后果：不必要地使用长词的问题》，证明滥用复杂长词反而会降低作者的智力评价。
For his report 'Consequences of Erudite Vernacular Utilized Irrespective of Necessity: Problems with Using Long Words Needlessly.'
#07医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Francis M. Fesmire, Majed Odeh, Harry Bassan, Arie Oliven🏅 Winners: Francis M. Fesmire, Majed Odeh, Harry Bassan, Arie Oliven
先后发表同名临床医学病例报告《用手指直肠按摩终止顽固性打嗝》。
For their respective medical case reports both titled 'Termination of Intractable Hiccups with Digital Rectal Massage.'
#08物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Basile Audoly, Sebastien Neukirch🏅 Winners: Basile Audoly, Sebastien Neukirch
揭示了为什么弯曲干意大利面条时，它往往会断成两截以上的多段碎块。
For their insights into why, when you bend dry spaghetti, cascading flexural cracks cause it to break into more than two pieces.
#09化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Antonio Mulet, José Javier Benedito, José Bon, Carmen Rosselló🏅 Winners: Antonio Mulet, José Javier Benedito, José Bon, Carmen Rosselló
发表食品声学与化学研究《温度对切达干酪中超声波传播速度的影响》。
For their food science study 'Ultrasonic Velocity in Cheddar Cheese as Affected by Temperature.'
#10生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Bart Knols, Ruurd de Jong🏅 Winners: Bart Knols, Ruurd de Jong
证明传播疟疾的雌性冈比亚按蚊对林堡干酪（Limburger cheese）气味和人类脚臭味的喜爱程度完全相同。
For showing that the female malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae is attracted equally to the smell of Limburger cheese and to the smell of human feet.

牛粪提炼香草精、无底洞汤碗与伟哥帮仓鼠倒时差 Cow-Dung Vanilla, Bottomless Soup Bowls, and Jet-Lagged Hamsters on Viagra

从吞剑副作用与床铺虫子普查到撒网抓劫匪专利 From Sword-Swallowing Side Effects and Bedbug Censuses to Bank-Robber Nets and the 'Gay Bomb'

📖 2007年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2007 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2007年第十七届搞笑诺贝尔奖在卧室、餐桌与蓝天之间展开了奇妙探索。荷兰埃因霍温理工大学的约翰娜·范·布龙斯维克教授凭借对每晚与人类同床共枕的螨虫、昆虫、蜘蛛、伪蝎、甲壳类动物、细菌、藻类、蕨类和真菌进行全面细致的“床铺人口普查”而夺得生物学奖。同在床铺上做文章的还有物理学奖得主、美国哈佛大学的马哈德万与智利圣地亚哥大学的恩里克·塞尔达·维拉布兰卡，他们深入研究了床单等弹性薄片在拉力下起皱的几何与物理规律。而在阿根廷国立基尔梅斯大学，帕特里夏·阿戈斯蒂诺、圣地亚哥·普拉诺与迭戈·戈隆贝克发现抗阳痿药物伟哥（西地那非）能帮助仓鼠更快倒过时差、恢复昼夜节律，一举拿下航空学奖。

吞吐之间尽显硬核科学本色。英国放射科医生布莱恩·威特科姆与美国吞剑协会的丹·迈耶因发表极具穿透力的医学报告《吞剑及其副作用》荣膺医学奖，详尽统计了全球吞剑表演者的喉咙疼痛与食道穿孔等职业伤病。美国康奈尔大学的布莱恩·万辛克设计了通过桌下暗管自动续汤的“无底洞汤碗”，借此探测人类深不可测的食欲与视觉暗示效应，证明人在不知情下会不知不觉多喝七成热汤，从而斩获营养学奖。日本国际医疗福祉大学的山本麻由则因利用亚临界水反应从牛粪中成功提取出香草醛（即香草香精成分）而赢得化学奖，剑桥当地冰激凌名店甚至为此专门推出了纪念款香草冰淇淋。

语言、治安与军事领域的脑洞同样惊人。西班牙巴塞罗那大学的胡安·曼努埃尔·托罗、何塞普·特罗巴隆与努里娅·塞巴斯蒂安-加列斯荣获语言学奖，他们通过实验证明大鼠有时无法区分倒着说的日语和倒着说的荷兰语。澳大利亚索引专家格伦达·布朗深入剖析了英语定冠词“The”给所有试图按字母顺序排列目录的人带来的种种麻烦，幽默摘得文学奖。中国台湾的谢国桢因在2001年为一套从天花板瞬间降下的“撒网抓银行劫匪装置”申请美国专利而拿下经济学奖；美国俄亥俄州代顿市的美国空军赖特实验室则因在1994年提议研发能让敌军士兵彼此产生强烈性吸引力的化学武器“同性恋炸弹”，尴尬地捧走了和平奖。

The 17th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2007 ventured from the microscopic ecosystems of our mattresses to the circadian rhythms of frequent-flying rodents. Dutch biologist Prof. Dr. Johanna E.M.H. van Bronswijk of Eindhoven University of Technology won the Biology Prize for conducting a comprehensive census of all the mites, insects, spiders, pseudoscorpions, crustaceans, bacteria, algae, ferns, and fungi with whom humans share their beds every night—an entire miniature jungle thriving in our mattress dust. Staying in the bedroom, L. Mahadevan of Harvard University and Enrique Cerda Villablanca of the University of Santiago, Chile, captured the Physics Prize for formulating the mathematical geometry and elasticity equations that govern how bedsheets and fabrics become wrinkled and draped under tension. Meanwhile, in Argentina, Patricia V. Agostino, Santiago A. Plano, and Diego A. Golombek of the National University of Quilmes won the Aviation Prize for discovering that small doses of Viagra (sildenafil) help hamsters recover up to fifty percent faster from simulated six-hour eastbound jetlag shifts.

Brave feats of ingestion and aromatic alchemy dominated the medical and food sciences. British radiologist Brian Witcombe and sword-swallower Dan Meyer earned the Medicine Prize for their penetrating British Medical Journal survey 'Sword Swallowing and Its Side Effects,' cataloging 'sword throats,' esophageal perforations, and the hazards of swallowing multiple blades at once—which Meyer memorably demonstrated live on stage at Sanders Theatre. Food psychologist Brian Wansink received the Nutrition Prize for rigging 'bottomless' bowls of tomato soup to secret under-table refill pipes, proving that visual portion cues override stomach fullness as diners unknowingly ate 73 percent more soup without feeling any fuller. And Mayu Yamamoto of the International Medical Center of Japan won the Chemistry Prize for extracting vanillin—real vanilla flavoring and fragrance—from cow dung via subcritical water reactions, inspiring Cambridge's famed Toscanini's Ice Cream shop to serve a special 'Yum-a-Moto Vanilla Twist' flavor in her honor.

Linguistic confusion, indexing headaches, and unconventional crime-and-warfare schemes completed the 2007 lineup. Juan Manuel Toro, Josep B. Trobalon, and Núria Sebastián-Gallés of the University of Barcelona took the Linguistics Prize for showing that while rats can easily distinguish spoken Japanese from spoken Dutch when played forward, the rodents are completely stumped when both languages are played backward. Australian professional indexer Glenda Browne won the Literature Prize for her definitive treatise on the definite article 'The' and the myriad headaches it inflicts on anyone trying to sort titles and entries into alphabetical order. In Taiwan, inventor Kuo Cheng Hsieh earned the Economics Prize for U.S. Patent #6,219,959, an infrared-triggered ceiling trap that catches bank robbers immediately by dropping a heavy net over them. Finally, the Peace Prize went to the U.S. Air Force Wright Laboratory in Dayton, Ohio, for a 1994 proposal to develop the so-called 'Gay Bomb'—a non-lethal aphrodisiac chemical weapon intended to make enemy soldiers become sexually irresistible to one another.

For studying the geometry and physics of how elastic sheets become wrinkled and draped.
#03生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Johanna E.M.H. van Bronswijk🏅 Winners: Prof. Dr. Johanna E.M.H. van Bronswijk
对每晚与人类同床共枕的所有螨虫、昆虫、蜘蛛、伪蝎、甲壳类动物、细菌、藻类、蕨类和真菌进行了一次全面普查。

通过动物实验证明，大鼠有时无法区分一个人倒着说日语和倒着说荷兰语。

专门研究了英语定冠词“The”，以及它给所有试图将词条按字母顺序排列的索引编纂者带来的种种难题。
For her study of the definite article 'the'—and of the many ways it causes problems for anyone who tries to put things into alphabetical order.
#07和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：美国空军赖特实验室 (The Air Force Wright Laboratory)🏅 Winners: The Air Force Wright Laboratory
提议研发一种被称为“同性恋炸弹”（Gay Bomb）的化学武器，试图让敌方士兵彼此产生不可抗拒的性吸引力。
For instigating research and development on a chemical weapon—the so-called 'gay bomb'—designed to make enemy soldiers become sexually irresistible to each other.
#08营养学奖 (Nutrition)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：Brian Wansink🏅 Winners: Brian Wansink
用自动续汤的“无底洞汤碗”喂食受试者，探索人类深不可测的食欲与视觉分量暗示的影响。
For exploring the seemingly boundless appetites of human beings by feeding them with a self-refilling, bottomless bowl of soup.
#09经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：谢国桢 (Kuo Cheng Hsieh)🏅 Winners: Kuo Cheng Hsieh
在2001年为一项通过从天而降的大网迅速罩住并捕捉银行劫匪的装置申请了美国专利（US Patent #6,219,959）。
For patenting a mechanical device in 2001 (U.S. Patent #6,219,959) that catches bank robbers immediately by dropping a net over them.
#10航空学奖 (Aviation)Aviation Prize
🏅 获奖者：Patricia V. Agostino, Santiago A. Plano, Diego A. Golombek🏅 Winners: Patricia V. Agostino, Santiago A. Plano, Diego A. Golombek
发现伟哥（西地那非）能显著加速仓鼠在光照时间表提前后的昼夜节律重整，帮助仓鼠倒时差。
For their discovery that Viagra (sildenafil) accelerates circadian reentrainment and aids jetlag recovery in hamsters.

会走迷宫的黏菌、昂贵假药与自动打结的绳子 Maze-Solving Slime Molds, Pricey Placebos, and Self-Knotting Strings

从电子增脆薯片与植物的尊严到可口可乐杀精大辩论 From Electronically Crisped Potato Chips and Plant Dignity to the Coca-Cola Spermicide Debate

📖 2008年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2008 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2008年第十八届搞笑诺贝尔奖证明，哪怕没有大脑的生物或毫无药效的假药也能创造奇迹。认知科学奖颁给日本北海道大学的中垣俊之、山田裕康、小林亮、手动厚、石黑章夫与匈牙利塞格德大学的阿戈塔·托特，他们发现毫无神经系统的单细胞生物黏菌竟能解开迷宫谜题并找到最短路径。医学奖得主、杜克大学的丹·艾瑞里、麻省理工学院的丽贝卡·瓦贝尔、斯坦福大学的巴巴·希夫与欧洲工商管理学院的齐夫·卡蒙则证实，标价昂贵的假药（安慰剂）比标价低廉的假药止痛效果更好。而在意大利特伦托大学与英国牛津大学，马西米利亚诺·赞皮尼与查尔斯·斯彭斯通过电子手段修饰并调高咀嚼薯片时的咔嚓声，让吃薯片的人相信薯片比实际更酥脆新鲜，从而夺得营养学奖。

动物与植物也在各自的领地改写着规则。法国图卢兹国立兽医学校的玛丽-克里斯蒂娜·卡迪耶格、克里斯代尔·茹贝尔与米歇尔·弗朗拿下生物学奖，他们通过实测发现寄生在狗身上的跳蚤比寄生在猫身上的跳蚤跳得更高。巴西圣保罗大学的阿斯托尔福·梅洛·阿劳若与何塞·卡洛斯·马塞利诺荣获考古学奖，精确测量了一只活犰狳在考古发掘地打洞折腾时如何把历史文物地层搅得天翻地覆。瑞士联邦非人类生物技术伦理委员会与瑞士公民则因正式确立“植物拥有尊严”的法律原则，认为随意把路边野花斩首有悖道德，一举捧走和平奖。

物理、化学与社会学研究更是妙趣横生。美国斯克里普斯海洋研究所的多里安·雷默与加州大学圣迭戈分校的道格拉斯·史密斯斩获物理学奖，他们从数学上证明成堆的绳子或头发只要经过翻滚晃动，就不可避免地会自动打成死结。化学奖由两派针锋相对的学者共享：波多黎各大学的莎莉·乌皮埃尔、约瑟夫·希尔与哈佛医学院的黛博拉·安德森发现可口可乐是有效的杀精剂，而台北医学大学的洪传岳、谢仲思、吴佩与姜必宁则证明可口可乐并无杀精功效。此外，新墨西哥大学的杰弗里·米勒、乔舒亚·泰伯与布伦特·乔丹因发现职业脱衣舞娘在排卵期赚取的小费显著更高而赢得经济学奖；伦敦卡斯商学院的大卫·西姆斯则凭深情撰写的论文《你个混蛋：对组织内部愤怒体验的叙事探索》摘得文学奖。

The 18th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2008 proved that neither a brain nor real medication is strictly necessary to achieve remarkable results. The Cognitive Science Prize went to Toshiyuki Nakagaki, Hiroyasu Yamada, Ryo Kobayashi, Atsushi Tero, Akio Ishiguro, and Ágotá Tóth for demonstrating that Physarum polycephalum—a brainless, single-celled yellow slime mold—can solve a laboratory maze by withdrawing protoplasmic tubes from dead ends to connect two oat flakes along the exact shortest path. Meanwhile, Dan Ariely of Duke University, Rebecca L. Waber of MIT, Baba Shiv of Stanford University, and Ziv Carmon of INSEAD won the Medicine Prize for proving that high-priced fake medicine ($2.50 placebo pills) relieves pain significantly better than discounted low-priced fake medicine ($0.10 placebo pills). Sensory illusion also triumphed in the Nutrition Prize, awarded to Massimiliano Zampini of the University of Trento and Charles Spence of Oxford University for electronically boosting the high-frequency crunch of Pringles potato chips through headphones, tricking tasters into believing stale chips were fifteen percent crisper and fresher than they really were.

Animals and plants rewrote the rules of biology, archaeology, and constitutional ethics. Marie-Christine Cadiergues, Christel Joubert, and Michel Franc of the École Nationale Vétérinaire de Toulouse won the Biology Prize for discovering that fleas living on dogs (Ctenocephalides canis) can jump significantly higher—up to twenty-five centimeters—than fleas living on cats (Ctenocephalides felis). In Brazil, Astolfo G. Mello Araujo and José Carlos Marcelino of the University of São Paulo captured the Archaeology Prize by letting a live nine-banded armadillo burrow through an experimental test pit filled with painted potsherds, measuring just how thoroughly one armored mammal can scramble the chronological strata of human history. And in Europe, the Swiss Federal Ethics Committee on Non-Human Biotechnology (ECNH) and the citizens of Switzerland received the Peace Prize for adopting the legal principle that plants possess intrinsic moral dignity—meaning that arbitrarily decapitating roadside wildflowers without rational justification is ethically wrong.

Physics, chemistry, and workplace indignation delivered a rousing finale. Dorian Raymer of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography and Douglas Smith of the University of California, San Diego, won the Physics Prize for tumbling strings inside a rotating box thousands of times to prove mathematically that heaps of string, cords, or hair inevitably tangle themselves into complex prime knots within seconds. The Chemistry Prize brought together two rival teams on opposite sides of the same fizzy question: Sharee A. Umpierre, Joseph A. Hill, and Deborah J. Anderson won for their 1985 New England Journal of Medicine report showing that Coca-Cola (especially Diet Coke) is an effective spermicide, while Chuang-Ye Hong, C.C. Shieh, P. Wu, and B.N. Chiang of Taipei Medical University shared the prize for their 1987 study proving that it is not. Finally, Geoffrey Miller, Joshua Tybur, and Brent Jordan of the University of New Mexico won the Economics Prize for discovering that professional lap dancers earn substantially higher tips during the fertile ovulatory phase of their menstrual cycles, and David Sims of London's Cass Business School won the Literature Prize for his lovingly written organizational study, 'You Bastard: A Narrative Exploration of the Experience of Indignation within Organizations.'

For electronically modifying the sound of a potato chip being chewed to make the person eating it believe the chip to be crisper and fresher than it really is.
#02和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：瑞士联邦非人类生物技术伦理委员会 (ECNH) 与瑞士公民🏅 Winners: The Swiss Federal Ethics Committee on Non-Human Biotechnology (ECNH) and the Citizens of Switzerland
采纳并确立了“植物拥有尊严”的法律与道德原则。
For adopting the legal and constitutional principle that plants have intrinsic moral dignity.
#03考古学奖 (Archaeology)Archaeology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Astolfo G. Mello Araujo, José Carlos Marcelino🏅 Winners: Astolfo G. Mello Araujo, José Carlos Marcelino
通过实验测量了一只活犰狳在考古遗址活动时能在多大程度上打乱历史地层与文物的顺序。
For measuring how the course of history—or at least the contents of an archaeological dig site—can be scrambled by the burrowing actions of a live armadillo.
#04生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Marie-Christine Cadiergues, Christel Joubert, Michel Franc🏅 Winners: Marie-Christine Cadiergues, Christel Joubert, Michel Franc
发现寄生在狗身上的跳蚤比寄生在猫身上的跳蚤跳得更高。
For discovering that the fleas that live on a dog (Ctenocephalides canis) can jump higher than the fleas that live on a cat (Ctenocephalides felis).
#05医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Dan Ariely, Rebecca L. Waber, Baba Shiv, Ziv Carmon🏅 Winners: Dan Ariely, Rebecca L. Waber, Baba Shiv, Ziv Carmon
通过临床实验证明，标价昂贵的假药（安慰剂）比标价低廉的假药具有更强的疗效。
For demonstrating that high-priced fake medicine (placebo) is clinically more effective at relieving pain than low-priced fake medicine.
#06认知科学奖 (Cognitive Science)Cognitive Science Prize
🏅 获奖者：中垣俊之 (Toshiyuki Nakagaki), 山田裕康 (Hiroyasu Yamada), 小林亮 (Ryo Kobayashi), 手动厚 (Atsushi Tero), 石黑章夫 (Akio Ishiguro), Ágotá Tóth🏅 Winners: Toshiyuki Nakagaki, Hiroyasu Yamada, Ryo Kobayashi, Atsushi Tero, Akio Ishiguro, Ágotá Tóth
发现没有大脑的单细胞变形菌类生物——黏菌（slime molds）能够解开迷宫谜题。
For discovering that brainless amoeboid slime molds (Physarum polycephalum) can solve mazes and find the shortest path.
#07经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Geoffrey Miller, Joshua Tybur, Brent Jordan🏅 Winners: Geoffrey Miller, Joshua Tybur, Brent Jordan
调查发现职业脱衣舞娘（lap dancers）在排卵期赚取的小费明显高于其他生理周期阶段。
For discovering that professional lap dancers earn significantly higher tips when they are ovulating.
#08物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Dorian Raymer, Douglas Smith🏅 Winners: Dorian Raymer, Douglas Smith
从数学与实验上证明，成堆的绳子、头发或几乎任何细长柔韧物都不可避免地会自动缠绕打结。
For proving mathematically and experimentally that heaps of agitated string, hair, or almost anything else will inevitably tangle themselves up in knots.
#09化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Sharee A. Umpierre, Joseph A. Hill, Deborah J. Anderson 以及 洪传岳 (Chuang-Ye Hong), 谢仲思 (C.C. Shieh), 吴佩 (P. Wu), 姜必宁 (B.N. Chiang)🏅 Winners: Sharee A. Umpierre, Joseph A. Hill, Deborah J. Anderson; and Chuang-Ye Hong, C.C. Shieh, P. Wu, B.N. Chiang
前一组学者发现可口可乐是有效的杀精剂，而后一组台湾学者则发现可口可乐并没有杀精作用。
For discovering that Coca-Cola is an effective spermicide (Umpierre et al.), and for discovering that it is not (Hong et al.).
#10文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：David Sims🏅 Winners: David Sims
满怀深情地撰写了管理学叙事研究《你个混蛋：对组织内部愤怒体验的叙事探索》。
For his lovingly written organizational study 'You Bastard: A Narrative Exploration of the Experience of Indignation within Organizations.'
2009 第19届搞笑诺贝尔奖 19th Ig Nobel Prize 2000s 📝 正文 878 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 528 words · 10 Prizes

六十年掰响左手指、龙舌兰造钻石与百亿万亿大钞 Sixty Years of Knuckle-Cracking, Tequila Diamonds, and 100-Trillion-Dollar Bills

从救急防毒胸罩到空酒瓶砸头力学与有名有姓的高产奶牛 From Emergency Gas-Mask Brassieres and Beer-Bottle Skull Physics to Named Dairy Cows

📖 2009年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2009 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2009年第十九届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院热闹颁出，将死磕到底的实验精神推向极致。美国加州的唐纳德·昂格尔医生独揽医学奖：为了验证母亲从小唠叨的“掰手指会得关节炎”究竟是不是真的，他坚持每天掰响左手关节至少两次、却从不碰右手，六十多年后拍片证实双手均无关节炎，在领奖台上仰天高呼“妈，你错了！”同样硬核的还有瑞士伯尔尼大学的斯特凡·博利格、斯特芬·罗斯、拉尔斯·厄斯特黑尔韦格、迈克尔·塔利与贝亚特·克诺伊比尔，五位法医通过砸击实验测定满啤酒瓶还是空啤酒瓶砸头更结实，发现空瓶因无内部气压反而更耐砸，但两者都足以敲碎人类头骨，凭此斩获和平奖。

物理、化学与生物界的发现同样令人拍案叫绝。辛辛那提大学的凯瑟琳·惠特科姆、哈佛大学的丹尼尔·利伯曼与得克萨斯大学的莉萨·夏皮罗从力学和进化角度算出女性腰椎拥有独特的楔形椎骨与前凸曲度，完美解释“为什么孕妇不会向前翻倒”，摘得物理学奖。墨西哥国立自治大学的哈维尔·莫拉莱斯、米格尔·阿帕蒂加与维克托·卡斯塔尼奥将龙舌兰酒加热气化沉积出纳米金刚石薄膜，用液体美酒造出真钻石，捧走化学奖。英国纽卡斯尔大学的凯瑟琳·道格拉斯与彼得·罗林森拿下兽医学奖，证明有名字的奶牛比无名奶牛产奶量更高；日本北里大学的田口文章、宋国富与张光磊则用大熊猫粪便中提取的耐高温细菌将厨余垃圾质量消减九成以上，夺得生物学奖。

公共服务与金融领域的黑色幽默更是入木三分。芝加哥的叶连娜·博德纳尔、拉斐尔·李与桑德拉·马里扬发明了紧急时刻可迅速拆成两个防护面罩的救生胸罩，一个留给自己、一个分给路人，荣膺公共卫生奖。爱尔兰警察局尴尬领走文学奖，因为他们向全国头号违章惯犯“Prawo Jazdy”开出了五十多张罚单，殊不知这词在波兰语里其实是“驾驶执照”。津巴布韦储备银行行长吉迪恩·戈诺因印制面额从一美分到一百万亿的钞票、帮百姓每天练习超大跨度数字而获数学奖；冰岛四大银行Kaupthing、Landsbanki、Glitnir及冰岛央行的高管与审计师则因证明小银行能瞬间变成大银行再瞬间缩水，并顺手把整个国家经济也玩成这样，拿下经济学奖。

The 19th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre celebrated scientific persistence at its most personal and Bruising. California allergist Donald L. Unger claimed the Medicine Prize for a self-experiment spanning more than sixty years: determined to test his mother's stern childhood warning that cracking his fingers would ruin his joints, he diligently cracked the knuckles of his left hand at least twice a day while leaving his right hand untouched. After more than 36,500 cracks, X-rays revealed zero arthritis in either hand, prompting Unger to look skyward and declare, 'Mother, you were wrong!' Equally hard-headed was the Peace Prize team of Stephan Bolliger, Steffen Ross, Lars Oesterhelweg, Michael Thali, and Beat Kneubuehl at the University of Bern, who experimentally smashed full and empty beer bottles onto human skull models. They discovered that empty bottles are actually sturdier because internal beer pressure weakens full ones — though both easily pack enough fracture energy to crack a human cranium.

Physics, chemistry, and biology offered equally dazzling revelations. Katherine K. Whitcome of the University of Cincinnati, Daniel E. Lieberman of Harvard University, and Liza J. Shapiro of the University of Texas won the Physics Prize for analytically determining why pregnant women do not tip over forward: evolution equipped female hominins with three lumbar vertebrae wedged to increase lordosis curvature and shift the center of mass back over the hips. In Mexico, Javier Morales, Miguel Apátiga, and Victor M. Castaño of Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México captured the Chemistry Prize by vaporizing liquid tequila at high temperatures to deposit genuine crystalline diamond films. Meanwhile, Newcastle University's Catherine Douglas and Peter Rowlinson won the Veterinary Medicine Prize for proving that dairy cows given personal names produce significantly more milk than nameless cattle, while Fumiaki Taguchi, Song Guofu, and Zhang Guanglei of Japan's Kitasato University took the Biology Prize for using thermophilic bacteria extracted from giant panda feces to reduce the mass of kitchen refuse by more than 90 percent.

Public institutions and financial wizards rounded out the evening with biting satire. Elena N. Bodnar, Raphael C. Lee, and Sandra Marijan of Chicago won the Public Health Prize for inventing and patenting an emergency brassiere that detaches in seconds into two protective respiratory face masks — one for the wearer and one for a lucky bystander. Ireland's national police service, An Garda Síochána, sheepishly received the Literature Prize after issuing more than fifty traffic tickets to the country's most notorious serial traffic offender, 'Prawo Jazdy' — before realizing that 'Prawo Jazdy' is simply the Polish phrase for 'Driving License' printed at the top of every Polish permit. Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe governor Gideon Gono earned the Mathematics Prize for giving citizens daily arithmetic practice across fourteen orders of magnitude by printing banknotes ranging from one cent ($0.01) to one hundred trillion dollars ($100,000,000,000,000). Finally, the Economics Prize went to the directors, executives, and auditors of four Icelandic banks — Kaupthing Bank, Landsbanki, Glitnir Bank, and the Central Bank of Iceland — for demonstrating that tiny banks can be rapidly transformed into huge banks, and vice versa, and that the exact same trick can be performed on an entire national economy.

2009年第十九届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院热闹颁出，将死磕到底的实验精神推向极致。美国加州的唐纳德·昂格尔医生独揽医学奖：为了验证母亲从小唠叨的“掰手指会得关节炎”究竟是不是真的，他坚持每天掰响左手关节至少两次、却从不碰右手，六十多年后拍片证实双手均无关节炎，在领奖台上仰天高呼“妈，你错了！”同样硬核的还有瑞士伯尔尼大学的斯特凡·博利格、斯特芬·罗斯、拉尔斯·厄斯特黑尔韦格、迈克尔·塔利与贝亚特·克诺伊比尔，五位法医通过砸击实验测定满啤酒瓶还是空啤酒瓶砸头更结实，发现空瓶因无内部气压反而更耐砸，但两者都足以敲碎人类头骨，凭此斩获和平奖。

The 19th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre celebrated scientific persistence at its most personal and Bruising. California allergist Donald L. Unger claimed the Medicine Prize for a self-experiment spanning more than sixty years: determined to test his mother's stern childhood warning that cracking his fingers would ruin his joints, he diligently cracked the knuckles of his left hand at least twice a day while leaving his right hand untouched. After more than 36,500 cracks, X-rays revealed zero arthritis in either hand, prompting Unger to look skyward and declare, 'Mother, you were wrong!' Equally hard-headed was the Peace Prize team of Stephan Bolliger, Steffen Ross, Lars Oesterhelweg, Michael Thali, and Beat Kneubuehl at the University of Bern, who experimentally smashed full and empty beer bottles onto human skull models. They discovered that empty bottles are actually sturdier because internal beer pressure weakens full ones — though both easily pack enough fracture energy to crack a human cranium.

物理、化学与生物界的发现同样令人拍案叫绝。辛辛那提大学的凯瑟琳·惠特科姆、哈佛大学的丹尼尔·利伯曼与得克萨斯大学的莉萨·夏皮罗从力学和进化角度算出女性腰椎拥有独特的楔形椎骨与前凸曲度，完美解释“为什么孕妇不会向前翻倒”，摘得物理学奖。墨西哥国立自治大学的哈维尔·莫拉莱斯、米格尔·阿帕蒂加与维克托·卡斯塔尼奥将龙舌兰酒加热气化沉积出纳米金刚石薄膜，用液体美酒造出真钻石，捧走化学奖。英国纽卡斯尔大学的凯瑟琳·道格拉斯与彼得·罗林森拿下兽医学奖，证明有名字的奶牛比无名奶牛产奶量更高；日本北里大学的田口文章、宋国富与张光磊则用大熊猫粪便中提取的耐高温细菌将厨余垃圾质量消减九成以上，夺得生物学奖。

Physics, chemistry, and biology offered equally dazzling revelations. Katherine K. Whitcome of the University of Cincinnati, Daniel E. Lieberman of Harvard University, and Liza J. Shapiro of the University of Texas won the Physics Prize for analytically determining why pregnant women do not tip over forward: evolution equipped female hominins with three lumbar vertebrae wedged to increase lordosis curvature and shift the center of mass back over the hips. In Mexico, Javier Morales, Miguel Apátiga, and Victor M. Castaño of Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México captured the Chemistry Prize by vaporizing liquid tequila at high temperatures to deposit genuine crystalline diamond films. Meanwhile, Newcastle University's Catherine Douglas and Peter Rowlinson won the Veterinary Medicine Prize for proving that dairy cows given personal names produce significantly more milk than nameless cattle, while Fumiaki Taguchi, Song Guofu, and Zhang Guanglei of Japan's Kitasato University took the Biology Prize for using thermophilic bacteria extracted from giant panda feces to reduce the mass of kitchen refuse by more than 90 percent.

公共服务与金融领域的黑色幽默更是入木三分。芝加哥的叶连娜·博德纳尔、拉斐尔·李与桑德拉·马里扬发明了紧急时刻可迅速拆成两个防护面罩的救生胸罩，一个留给自己、一个分给路人，荣膺公共卫生奖。爱尔兰警察局尴尬领走文学奖，因为他们向全国头号违章惯犯“Prawo Jazdy”开出了五十多张罚单，殊不知这词在波兰语里其实是“驾驶执照”。津巴布韦储备银行行长吉迪恩·戈诺因印制面额从一美分到一百万亿的钞票、帮百姓每天练习超大跨度数字而获数学奖；冰岛四大银行Kaupthing、Landsbanki、Glitnir及冰岛央行的高管与审计师则因证明小银行能瞬间变成大银行再瞬间缩水，并顺手把整个国家经济也玩成这样，拿下经济学奖。

Public institutions and financial wizards rounded out the evening with biting satire. Elena N. Bodnar, Raphael C. Lee, and Sandra Marijan of Chicago won the Public Health Prize for inventing and patenting an emergency brassiere that detaches in seconds into two protective respiratory face masks — one for the wearer and one for a lucky bystander. Ireland's national police service, An Garda Síochána, sheepishly received the Literature Prize after issuing more than fifty traffic tickets to the country's most notorious serial traffic offender, 'Prawo Jazdy' — before realizing that 'Prawo Jazdy' is simply the Polish phrase for 'Driving License' printed at the top of every Polish permit. Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe governor Gideon Gono earned the Mathematics Prize for giving citizens daily arithmetic practice across fourteen orders of magnitude by printing banknotes ranging from one cent ($0.01) to one hundred trillion dollars ($100,000,000,000,000). Finally, the Economics Prize went to the directors, executives, and auditors of four Icelandic banks — Kaupthing Bank, Landsbanki, Glitnir Bank, and the Central Bank of Iceland — for demonstrating that tiny banks can be rapidly transformed into huge banks, and vice versa, and that the exact same trick can be performed on an entire national economy.

连续60多年每天坚持掰响左手手指关节，却从不掰右手关节，以此探究掰手指是否会导致关节炎。
For investigating a possible cause of arthritis of the fingers by diligently cracking the knuckles of his left hand — but never his right hand — every day for more than 60 years.

印制面额从1美分到100万亿（$100,000,000,000,000）的钞票，让民众在日常生活中天天应对极大跨度的数字。
