🏅 获奖者：田口文章 (Fumiaki Taguchi), 宋国富 (Song Guofu), 张光磊 (Zhang Guanglei)🏅 Winners: Fumiaki Taguchi, Song Guofu, Zhang Guanglei
证明利用从大熊猫粪便中提取的细菌，可以将厨余垃圾的质量减少90%以上。
For demonstrating that kitchen refuse can be reduced more than 90% in mass by using bacteria extracted from the feces of giant pandas.
2010 第20届搞笑诺贝尔奖 20th Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 872 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 526 words · 10 Prizes

遥控飞机采鲸鱼鼻涕、黏菌修铁路与随机升职学 Whale-Snot Helicopters, Slime-Mold Railways, and Random Corporate Promotions

从鞋外穿袜防滑、骂脏话止痛到坐过山车治哮喘与油水相溶 From Socks Over Shoes on Ice and Painkilling Profanity to Roller-Coaster Asthma Therapy

📖 2010年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2010 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2010年第二十届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了生物智慧与草根工程学的奇妙碰撞。伦敦动物学会的卡琳娜·阿塞韦多-怀特豪斯、阿涅丝·罗莎-戈瑟兰与墨西哥的黛安娜·让德龙夺得工程学奖：她们在遥控直升机下挂载培养皿，趁鲸鱼浮出水面换气时低空掠过喷气柱，巧妙收集“鲸鱼鼻涕”来监测疾病。而在交通规划奖中，日本学者中垣俊之、手老笃史、高木清二、三枝哲、伊藤贤太郎、弓木健司、小林亮与英国的丹·贝伯、马克·弗里克继2008年让黏菌走迷宫后再度折桂：他们按东京周边城市分布摆放燕麦片，让黏菌自由觅食，长出的菌丝网络竟与现实中的东京铁路网高度吻合，堪称天然的铁路总工程师。

人体奥秘与实验室安全同样笑点密集。荷兰阿姆斯特丹大学的西蒙·里特费尔德与蒂尔堡大学的伊利亚·范比斯特发现坐过山车能显著缓解哮喘症状，摘得医学奖；英国基尔大学的理查德·斯蒂芬斯、约翰·阿特金斯与安德鲁·金斯顿通过冰水耐痛实验，证实骂脏话确实比说文明词更能缓解疼痛，捧走和平奖。新西兰奥塔哥大学的莉安·帕金、希拉·威廉姆斯与帕特里夏·普里斯特通过对照试验，证明冬日结冰路面上“把袜子套在鞋子外面穿”能大幅减少滑倒，荣膺物理学奖。美国德特里克堡的曼努埃尔·巴贝托、查尔斯·马修斯与拉里·泰勒则用实验证实微生物极易顽固附着在留胡子科学家的胡须上，拿下公共卫生奖。

动物行为、职场管理与能源金融领域的讽刺更是辛辣独到。中国学者张礼标、谭敏、朱光剑、叶剑平、洪体玉、周善义、张树义与英国布里斯托大学的加雷思·琼斯科学记录了果蝠的口交行为及其延长交配时间的作用，赢得生物学奖。意大利卡塔尼亚大学的亚历山德罗·普卢基诺、安德烈亚·拉皮萨达与切萨雷·加罗法洛用数学模型修正“彼得原理”，证明机构若随机抽签提拔员工，运作效率反而更高，斩获管理学奖。麻省理工的埃里克·亚当斯、得州农工的斯科特·索科洛夫斯基、夏威夷大学的斯蒂芬·马苏塔尼与英国石油公司因推翻“油水不相溶”的古老信念获颁化学奖；高盛、AIG、雷曼兄弟、贝尔斯登、美林与Magnetar的高管董事们则因创造出使收益最大化、风险最小化的投资新法，共同领走经济学奖。

The 20th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2010 showcased nature's unexpected engineers alongside grassroots mechanical ingenuity. The Engineering Prize went to Karina Acevedo-Whitehouse and Agnes Rocha-Gosselin of the Zoological Society of London and Diane Gendron of Mexico's Instituto Politécnico Nacional, who perfected a non-invasive way to collect whale snot: they strapped sterile Petri dishes to the bottom of a remote-control helicopter and flew it directly through the misty blowhole plumes of surfacing whales to monitor respiratory microbes. Meanwhile, the Transportation Planning Prize honored Japanese and British researchers Toshiyuki Nakagaki, Atsushi Tero, Seiji Takagi, Tetsu Saigusa, Kentaro Ito, Kenji Yumiki, Ryo Kobayashi, Dan Bebber, and Mark Fricker — making Nakagaki, Tero, and Kobayashi two-time laureates after their 2008 puzzle-solving slime mold prize. By arranging oat flakes to match the geography of cities around Tokyo, they let the slime mold Physarum polycephalum grow a foraging network that spontaneously mirrored the actual Tokyo rail system in efficiency and fault tolerance.

Human physiology and laboratory safety inspired equally memorable breakthroughs. Dutch researchers Simon Rietveld of the University of Amsterdam and Ilja van Beest of Tilburg University captured the Medicine Prize for discovering that riding a thrilling roller coaster can alleviate the perceived symptoms of asthma. At Keele University in the UK, Richard Stephens, John Atkins, and Andrew Kingston won the Peace Prize for plunging volunteers' hands into ice water to confirm the age-old belief that swearing aloud genuinely increases pain tolerance and relieves suffering compared with uttering neutral words. In New Zealand, Lianne Parkin, Sheila Williams, and Patricia Priest of the University of Otago conducted a randomized controlled trial on wintry Dunedin sidewalks and won the Physics Prize for proving that pedestrians slip and fall far less often on ice when they wear socks on the outside of their shoes. And the Public Health Prize reached back to a classic Fort Detrick study by Manuel Barbeito, Charles Mathews, and Larry Taylor, who sprayed bacteria onto mannequins and bearded volunteers to prove that dangerous microbes cling tenaciously to bearded scientists even after washing.

Animal behavior, corporate hierarchy, and high-stakes finance completed the 2010 roster. Libiao Zhang, Min Tan, Guangjian Zhu, Jianping Ye, Tiyu Hong, Shanyi Zhou, and Shuyi Zhang of China, together with Gareth Jones of the University of Bristol, won the Biology Prize for scientifically documenting fellatio in short-nosed fruit bats and showing that it prolongs copulation time. Italian physicists Alessandro Pluchino, Andrea Rapisarda, and Cesare Garofalo of the University of Catania claimed the Management Prize by mathematically revisiting the Peter Principle, proving via computational simulations that organizations become significantly more efficient if they promote employees completely at random. MIT's Eric Adams, Texas A&M's Scott Socolofsky, the University of Hawaii's Stephen Masutani, and British Petroleum (BP) shared the Chemistry Prize for deep-sea oil plume research that disproved the old adage that oil and water don't mix. Finally, the Economics Prize saluted the executives and directors of Goldman Sachs, AIG, Lehman Brothers, Bear Stearns, Merrill Lynch, and Magnetar for creating and promoting bold new ways to invest money that maximize financial gain and minimize financial risk for the world economy — or at least for a select portion thereof.

动物行为、职场管理与能源金融领域的讽刺更是辛辣独到。中国学者张礼标、谭敏、朱光剑、叶剑平、洪体玉、周善义、张树义与英国布里斯托大学的加雷思·琼斯科学记录了果蝠的口交行为及其延长交配时间的作用，赢得生物学奖。意大利卡塔尼亚大学的亚历山德罗·普卢基诺、安德烈亚·拉皮萨达与切萨雷·加罗法洛用数学模型修正“彼得原理”，证明机构若随机抽签提拔员工，运作效率反而更高，斩获管理学奖。麻省理工的埃里克·亚当斯、得州农工的斯科特·索科洛夫斯基、夏威夷大学的斯蒂芬·马苏塔尼与英国石油公司因推翻“油水不相溶”的古老信念获颁化学奖；高盛、AIG、雷曼兄弟、贝尔斯登、美林与Magnetar的高管董事们则因创造出使收益最大化、风险最小化的投资新法，共同领走经济学奖。

Animal behavior, corporate hierarchy, and high-stakes finance completed the 2010 roster. Libiao Zhang, Min Tan, Guangjian Zhu, Jianping Ye, Tiyu Hong, Shanyi Zhou, and Shuyi Zhang of China, together with Gareth Jones of the University of Bristol, won the Biology Prize for scientifically documenting fellatio in short-nosed fruit bats and showing that it prolongs copulation time. Italian physicists Alessandro Pluchino, Andrea Rapisarda, and Cesare Garofalo of the University of Catania claimed the Management Prize by mathematically revisiting the Peter Principle, proving via computational simulations that organizations become significantly more efficient if they promote employees completely at random. MIT's Eric Adams, Texas A&M's Scott Socolofsky, the University of Hawaii's Stephen Masutani, and British Petroleum (BP) shared the Chemistry Prize for deep-sea oil plume research that disproved the old adage that oil and water don't mix. Finally, the Economics Prize saluted the executives and directors of Goldman Sachs, AIG, Lehman Brothers, Bear Stearns, Merrill Lynch, and Magnetar for creating and promoting bold new ways to invest money that maximize financial gain and minimize financial risk for the world economy — or at least for a select portion thereof.

利用黏菌（多头绒泡菌）的觅食网络来确定铁路轨道的最优路线规划。
For using slime mold to determine the optimal routes for railroad tracks.

证明在冬日结冰的人行道上，如果人们把袜子套在鞋子外面穿，滑倒摔跤的概率会大大降低。

通过冰水耐痛实验证实了人们普遍相信的观点：骂脏话确实能够缓解疼痛。
For confirming the widely held belief that swearing relieves pain.

通过实验证实微生物会顽固地附着在留胡子科学家的胡须上，即使清洗也难以完全去除。
For determining by experiment that microbes cling to bearded scientists.

创造并推广新的投资方式——使世界经济（或其中一部分人）的财务收益最大化、财务风险最小化。
For creating and promoting new ways to invest money — ways that maximize financial gain and minimize financial risk for the world economy, or for a portion thereof.
#08化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Eric Adams, Scott Socolofsky, Stephen Masutani 与英国石油公司 (BP)🏅 Winners: Eric Adams, Scott Socolofsky, Stephen Masutani, and BP (British Petroleum)
通过深海漏油模拟与实践，推翻了“油和水不相溶”的古老信念。
For disproving the old belief that oil and water don't mix.
#09管理学奖 (Management)Management Prize
🏅 获奖者：Alessandro Pluchino, Andrea Rapisarda, Cesare Garofalo🏅 Winners: Alessandro Pluchino, Andrea Rapisarda, Cesare Garofalo
从数学上证明，如果组织机构采取随机抽签的方式提拔员工，整体效率反而会更高。
For demonstrating mathematically that organizations would become more efficient if they promoted people at random.

科学记录并研究了果蝠中的口交行为及其延长交配时间的功能。
For scientifically documenting fellatio in fruit bats and showing that it prolongs copulation.
2011 第21届搞笑诺贝尔奖 21st Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 845 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 488 words · 10 Prizes

芥末火灾警报器、憋尿决策学与装甲车碾违停豪车 Wasabi Fire Alarms, Full-Bladder Decision-Making, and Tank-Crushed Luxury Cars

从甲虫苦恋澳洲啤酒瓶、结构化拖延症到算错末日的预言家们 From Beer-Bottle-Loving Beetles and Structured Procrastination to Failed Doomsday Prophets

📖 2011年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2011 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2011年第二十一届搞笑诺贝尔奖将生理冲动与感官刺激研究出了花样。日本滋贺医科大学的今井真、漆畑直树、种村秀辉、田岛幸信、后藤秀昭、沟口浩一郎与村上纯一团队荣膺化学奖：为了让听障人士在火灾熟睡中也能及时逃生，他们精确测定了空气中辛辣芥末气味的理想唤醒浓度，发明出一喷就能把人呛醒的“芥末警报器”。医学奖由欧洲的米里亚姆·图克、德布拉·特兰佩、卢克·瓦洛普与美澳的马修·刘易斯、彼得·斯奈德、罗伯特·费尔德曼、罗伯特·皮耶扎克、大卫·达比、保罗·马鲁夫团队共享，他们证实当人类强烈憋尿时，克制冲动的长远决策会变得更英明，但需要快速注意力的认知决策则会变得更糟糕。

动物、运动与人类心理同样妙趣横生。英奥荷匈学者安娜·威尔金森、娜塔莉·塞班茨、伊莎贝拉·曼德尔与路德维希·胡贝尔耗时训练红腿陆龟打哈欠，最终凭《没有证据表明红腿陆龟存在传染性打哈欠》摘得生理学奖。达里尔·格温与大卫·伦茨则因发现澳洲雄性吉丁虫把棕色凹凸纹路的澳洲啤酒瓶误当成性感雌虫、顶着烈日拼命与之交配而夺得生物学奖。法国与荷兰学者菲利普·佩兰、西里尔·佩罗、多米尼克·德维泰尔纳、布鲁诺·拉加吕和赫尔曼·金马查明了为什么铁饼运动员旋转投掷后会头晕而链球运动员却不会，捧走物理学奖；挪威奥斯陆大学的卡尔·哈尔沃·泰根因探究人们日常为何叹气获心理学奖；斯坦福大学的约翰·佩里则凭“结构化拖延理论”——想当高效人士就要靠做重要事情来逃避更重要的事情——斩获文学奖。

街头治理与神学算术更是贡献了年度名场面。立陶宛维尔纽斯市市长阿图拉斯·佐卡斯亲自驾驶装甲运兵车直接碾过违章停放的奔驰豪车，霸气捧走和平奖。多伦多大学的约翰·森德斯获公共安全奖，他在高速公路实验中让遮阳面罩反复落下遮住司机双眼以测试盲开极限。数学奖则颁给先后预言世界末日降临却屡屡落空的多萝西·马丁、帕特·罗伯逊、伊丽莎白·克莱尔·先知、李长林、克雷多尼亚·姆韦林德与哈罗德·坎平六位预言家，感谢他们用一次次算错的末日预言谆谆告诫世人：做数学假设和计算时千万要格外谨慎！

The 21st First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2011 explored urgent bodily impulses and sensory wake-up calls. Japanese researchers Makoto Imai, Naoki Urushihata, Hideki Tanemura, Yukinobu Tajima, Hideaki Goto, Koichiro Mizoguchi, and Junichi Murakami won the Chemistry Prize for determining the ideal airborne density of pungent horseradish (wasabi) needed to rouse sleeping people during a fire emergency, and applying that knowledge to invent the Wasabi Alarm — a lifesaver for deaf and hard-of-hearing sleepers whose trigeminal nerves react instantly to allyl isothiocyanate mist. Meanwhile, the Medicine Prize was shared by two international teams — Mirjam Tuk, Debra Trampe, and Luk Warlop of Europe, and Matthew Lewis, Peter Snyder, Robert Feldman, Robert Pietrzak, David Darby, and Paul Maruff of the USA and Australia — for demonstrating that when people have an acute urge to urinate, 'inhibitory spillover' helps them make better impulse-control decisions on some tasks, while making significantly worse decisions on others.

Animal habits, athletic dizziness, and everyday human quirks filled the middle of the program. Anna Wilkinson, Natalie Sebanz, Isabella Mandl, and Ludwig Huber earned the Physiology Prize for spending months training a red-footed tortoise named Alexandra to yawn on cue, ultimately publishing 'No Evidence of Contagious Yawning in the Red-Footed Tortoise.' Entomologists Darryl Gwynne and David Rentz won the Biology Prize for discovering that male Australian jewel beetles tragically mistake discarded brown 'stubby' beer bottles — whose dimpled glass mimics giant female wing covers — for mates, refusing to leave the bottles even as they bake in the sun. In sports science, Philippe Perrin, Cyril Perrot, Dominique Deviterne, Bruno Ragaru, and Herman Kingma won the Physics Prize for determining why discus throwers become dizzy while spinning whereas hammer throwers do not. University of Oslo psychologist Karl Halvor Teigen claimed the Psychology Prize for investigating why people sigh in everyday life, and Stanford philosopher John Perry took the Literature Prize for his Theory of Structured Procrastination: to be a high achiever, always work on something important as a way to avoid doing something even more important.

Municipal enforcement, highway daring, and apocalyptic arithmetic provided an unforgettable finale. Arturas Zuokas, the mayor of Vilnius, Lithuania, rolled away with the Peace Prize for personally demonstrating that the problem of illegally parked luxury cars blocking bike lanes can be solved by running them over with an armored BTR tank. University of Toronto professor John Senders received the Public Safety Prize for his classic 1967 highway experiments in which he drove an automobile down a major road while a mechanical visor repeatedly flapped down over his eyes to measure driver attentional demand. And the Mathematics Prize honored six doomsday predictors — Dorothy Martin (who predicted the world would end in 1954), Pat Robertson (1982), Elizabeth Clare Prophet (1990), Lee Jang Rim (1992), Credonia Mwerinde (1999), and Harold Camping (September 6, 1994 and October 21, 2011) — for teaching the world to be extra careful when making mathematical assumptions and calculations.

#01生理学奖 (Physiology)Physiology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Anna Wilkinson, Natalie Sebanz, Isabella Mandl, Ludwig Huber🏅 Winners: Anna Wilkinson, Natalie Sebanz, Isabella Mandl, Ludwig Huber
发表实验研究《没有证据表明红腿陆龟之间存在传染性打哈欠》。
For their study 'No Evidence of Contagious Yawning in the Red-Footed Tortoise.'
#02化学奖 (Chemistry)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：今井真 (Makoto Imai), Naoki Urushihata, Hideki Tanemura, Yukinobu Tajima, Hideaki Goto, Koichiro Mizoguchi, Junichi Murakami🏅 Winners: Makoto Imai, Naoki Urushihata, Hideki Tanemura, Yukinobu Tajima, Hideaki Goto, Koichiro Mizoguchi, Junichi Murakami
确定火灾等紧急情况下唤醒熟睡者的空气中芥末理想浓度，并据此发明了芥末警报器。
For determining the ideal density of airborne wasabi to awaken sleeping people in case of an emergency, and for inventing the wasabi alarm.
#03医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Mirjam Tuk, Debra Trampe, Luk Warlop 与 Matthew Lewis, Peter Snyder, Robert Feldman, Robert Pietrzak, David Darby, Paul Maruff🏅 Winners: Mirjam Tuk, Debra Trampe, Luk Warlop; and Matthew Lewis, Peter Snyder, Robert Feldman, Robert Pietrzak, David Darby, Paul Maruff
证明当人们有强烈尿意（憋尿）时，对某些事情能做出更好的决策，而对另一些事情则会做出更糟糕的决定。
For demonstrating that people make better decisions about some kinds of things — but worse decisions about other kinds of things — when they have a strong urge to urinate.
#04心理学奖 (Psychology)Psychology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Karl Halvor Teigen🏅 Winners: Karl Halvor Teigen
试图通过问卷与实验弄明白在日常生活中人们为什么会叹气。
For trying to understand why, in everyday life, people sigh.
#05文学奖 (Literature)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Perry🏅 Winners: John Perry
提出“结构化拖延理论”：要想成为高效成功人士，就要始终去做某些重要的事，以此作为逃避做更重要事情的手段。
For his Theory of Structured Procrastination: To be a high achiever, always work on something important, using it as a way to avoid doing something that's even more important.
#06生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Darryl Gwynne, David Rentz🏅 Winners: Darryl Gwynne, David Rentz
发现某种雄性吉丁虫会把某种特定款式的澳大利亚啤酒瓶误认为雌虫并与之疯狂交配。
For discovering that a certain kind of beetle mates with a certain kind of Australian beer bottle.
#07物理学奖 (Physics)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Philippe Perrin, Cyril Perrot, Dominique Deviterne, Bruno Ragaru, Herman Kingma🏅 Winners: Philippe Perrin, Cyril Perrot, Dominique Deviterne, Bruno Ragaru, Herman Kingma
通过前庭与视觉参考系研究，查明为什么铁饼运动员旋转后会头晕，而链球运动员却不会。
For determining why discus throwers become dizzy, and why hammer throwers don't.
#08数学奖 (Mathematics)Mathematics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Dorothy Martin, Pat Robertson, Elizabeth Clare Prophet, 李长林 (Lee Jang Rim), Credonia Mwerinde, Harold Camping🏅 Winners: Dorothy Martin, Pat Robertson, Elizabeth Clare Prophet, Lee Jang Rim, Credonia Mwerinde, Harold Camping
多位末日预言家因屡次算错世界末日日期，教会世人在进行数学假设和计算时必须保持谨慎。
For predicting various dates for the end of the world, thereby teaching the world to be careful when making mathematical assumptions and calculations.
#09和平奖 (Peace)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Arturas Zuokas（立陶宛维尔纽斯市市长）🏅 Winners: Arturas Zuokas (Mayor of Vilnius, Lithuania)
亲身示范非法停放豪车的城市顽疾可以通过驾驶装甲车直接碾压过去来解决。
For demonstrating that the problem of illegally parked luxury cars can be solved by running them over with an armored tank.
#10公共安全奖 (Public Safety)Public Safety Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Senders🏅 Winners: John Senders
在主要高速公路上开展一系列驾驶安全实验，让遮阳面罩反复落下遮住司机脸部使其暂时失明。
For conducting a series of safety experiments in which a person drives an automobile on a major highway while a visor repeatedly flaps down over his face, blinding him.

死三文鱼的脑电波、闭嘴干扰器与端咖啡走路流体力学 Dead Salmon Brain Scans, the SpeechJammer Gun, and Coffee-Sloshing Dynamics

从马尾辫方程、看臀识黑猩猩到防范结肠镜检查患者爆炸 From Ponytail Physics and Chimpanzee Rear-End Recognition to Non-Exploding Colonoscopies

📖 2012年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2012 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2012年第二十二届搞笑诺贝尔奖给盲目迷信精密仪器与套娃式公文的现代社会敲响了幽默警钟。美国学者克雷格·贝内特、阿比盖尔·贝尔德、迈克尔·米勒与乔治·沃尔福德夺得神经科学奖：他们把一条死大西洋鲑鱼推进核磁共振仪，给死鱼看人类悲喜照片并做常规统计，证明只要忽略多重比较校正，复杂仪器连死鱼脑子里都能扫出“善解人意的脑部活动信号”。日本学者栗原一贵与冢田浩二发明了专治话痨的“话语干扰器”，让说话者以微秒级延迟听到自己的声音，触发听觉延迟反馈干扰令其瞬间舌头打结，摘得声学奖。美国政府问责署更因发布一份《关于报告的报告的报告》，并在文中郑重建议再准备一份《关于这份关于报告的报告的报告的报告》，捧走文学奖。

日常物理与化学谜题同样被拆解得明明白白。美英学者约瑟夫·凯勒、雷蒙德·戈德斯坦、帕特里克·沃伦与罗宾·鲍尔推导出决定人类马尾辫形状与摆动规律的统计物理平衡方程，荣膺物理学奖（组委会现场还特意为凯勒补发了1999年漏署名的茶壶嘴不滴水物理学奖，使其成为双料得主）。加州大学的鲁斯兰·克雷切特尼科夫与汉斯·迈耶因研究人端着咖啡杯走路时步伐频率如何激发液体晃动共振而导致咖啡洒出，拿下流体力学奖。瑞典与卢旺达学者约翰·彼得松则解开了瑞典安德斯勒夫镇部分新房居民洗澡后金发莫名变绿的谜团——源于热水在全新铜管中浸泡过夜溶出的铜离子，凭此获颁化学奖。

生物、心理、医学与军工转型的跨界研究更是脑洞大开。荷兰与秘鲁、俄罗斯学者阿妮塔·埃尔兰、罗尔夫·兹万与图利奥·瓜达卢佩发现《身体向左倾斜会让埃菲尔铁塔看起来更小》，斩获心理学奖（颁奖两天后前两位作者还在荷兰喜结连理）。著名灵长类学家弗朗斯·德瓦尔与珍妮弗·波科尼证实黑猩猩仅凭观看同伴臀部的照片就能准确认出对方是谁，拿下解剖学奖。法国医生埃马纽埃尔·本-苏桑与米歇尔·安东涅蒂获医学奖，他们严肃指导同行在做结肠镜检查时如何排空肠道可燃气体、把“患者在检查中发生体内爆炸”的概率降到最低；俄罗斯SKN公司则因把老旧苏联弹药转化为全新纳米钻石，名副其实地捧走和平奖。

The 22nd First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2012 delivered a masterclass in statistical humility and bureaucratic recursion. American neuroscientists Craig Bennett, Abigail Baird, Michael Miller, and George Wolford won the Neuroscience Prize for placing a dead Atlantic salmon into an fMRI scanner, showing the dead fish photographs of humans in social situations, and demonstrating that without proper multiple-comparisons correction, complex brain-imaging instruments and simple statistics will happily detect 'meaningful brain activity' in a deceased fish. Japanese researchers Kazutaka Kurihara and Koji Tsukada captured the Acoustics Prize for inventing the SpeechJammer — a directional microphone-and-speaker device that disrupts a person's speech by playing back their own spoken words with a fraction-of-a-second delay. And the US Government General Accountability Office (GAO) won the Literature Prize for issuing a report about reports about reports that officially recommends the preparation of a report about the report about reports about reports.

Everyday physics and domestic mysteries received equally rigorous mathematical treatment. Joseph Keller of the USA and Raymond Goldstein, Patrick Warren, and Robin Ball of the UK shared the Physics Prize for calculating the balance of forces and statistical physics equations that shape and move the hair in a human ponytail (in a special ceremony announcement, organizers also corrected a 1999 oversight by awarding Keller a belated share of the 1999 Physics Prize for calculating how to make a teapot spout that does not drip). Fluid Dynamics Prize laureates Rouslan Krechetnikov and Hans Mayer of UC Santa Barbara analyzed the dynamics of liquid sloshing to explain why people walking with a cup of coffee almost inevitably spill it right around their seventh step. Meanwhile, environmental engineer Johan Pettersson of Sweden and Rwanda won the Chemistry Prize for solving the puzzle of why residents in certain newly built houses in Anderslöv, Sweden, found their blonde hair turning green — tracing the culprit to hot water sitting overnight in uncoated new copper pipes.

Psychology, primatology, clinical safety, and disarmament rounded out the night. Dutch and Peruvian researchers Anita Eerland, Rolf Zwaan, and Tulio Guadalupe won the Psychology Prize for their study 'Leaning to the Left Makes the Eiffel Tower Seem Smaller,' showing that subtle body posture biases numerical magnitude estimates (Eerland and Zwaan celebrated by getting married in the Netherlands two days after the ceremony). Primatologists Frans de Waal and Jennifer Pokorny received the Anatomy Prize for discovering that chimpanzees can identify other individual chimpanzees and match their faces simply by looking at photographs of their rear ends. French physicians Emmanuel Ben-Soussan and Michel Antonietti earned the Medicine Prize for advising doctors who perform therapeutic colonoscopies on how to prevent their patients' intestines from exploding during electrocautery. Finally, Russia's SKN Company, represented by Igor Petrov, took home the Peace Prize for converting old Russian military ammunition into shiny new nanodiamonds.

2013 第23届搞笑诺贝尔奖 23rd Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 873 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 516 words · 10 Prizes

仰望银河的屎壳郎、月球水上漂与生吞鼩鼱考古学 Milky Way Dung Beetles, Pond-Running on the Moon, and Swallowing a Boiled Shrew

从听歌剧延寿的换心小鼠、空投劫机犯到被鸭子偷吃的断肢 From Opera-Loving Heart-Transplant Mice and Parachuting Hijackers to Duck-Eaten Amputations

📖 2013年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2013 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2013年第二十三届搞笑诺贝尔奖证明，哪怕脚下推着粪球，心中也能装着浩瀚宇宙。瑞典、澳洲、南非等地学者玛丽·达克、艾米莉·贝尔德、马库斯·伯恩、克拉克·朔尔茨与埃里克·瓦兰特斩获生物学与天文学联合奖：他们给屎壳郎戴上小纸帽并在天象馆实验，首次证实迷路的屎壳郎竟能靠仰望银河系的光带导航回家！物理学奖得主阿尔贝托·米内蒂、尤里·伊万年科、杰尔马娜·卡佩利尼、娜迪亚·多米尼奇与弗朗切斯科·拉夸尼蒂则通过悬吊减重模拟发现，若把人类和池塘搬到月球等低重力环境，人真能施展“水上漂”跑过池塘水面。

医学、化学与考古学家的奉献精神同样令人肃然起敬。日本与中国学者内山雅照、金相元、张祺、平井敏仁、天野笃、判田久与新见正则给做完心脏移植手术的小鼠播放歌剧《茶花女》，发现听歌剧的小鼠免疫排斥更少、术后存活期显著延长，荣膺医学奖。今井真介、柘植信昭、友竹宗昭、长留吉朗、泽田、长田敏行与熊谷英彦因发现催泪因子合成酶、证明洋葱让人流泪的生化过程比原先以为的复杂得多而摘得化学奖。考古学家布赖恩·克兰德尔和彼得·斯塔尔更是狠人中的狠人：为查明人类消化道会溶解哪些小型哺乳动物骨骼，他们把死鼩鼱稍微水煮后不经咀嚼整只生吞下肚，连续数日仔细筛查排泄物，硬核捧走考古学奖。

心理、概率与社会奇闻同样精彩绝伦。洛朗·贝格、布拉德·布什曼、乌尔曼·泽尔胡尼、巴蒂斯特·苏布拉与迈赫迪·乌拉巴通过安慰剂实验证实“自以为喝醉的人也会觉得自己很有魅力”，拿下心理学奖。伯特·托尔坎普、玛丽·哈斯凯尔、弗里莎·兰福德、大卫·罗伯茨与科林·摩根斩获概率学奖，发现奶牛趴着越久越可能很快站起来，但一旦站起来就很难预测它何时再趴下。已故美国发明家古斯塔诺·皮佐因设计用活板门把劫机犯掉入舱底打包封装、再从弹舱门挂降落伞空投给地面警察的防劫机系统获安全工程奖；泰国医生卡西安·班加纳达等七人因发表《暹罗阴茎切除流行病的外科处理》、推荐实施再植术——“除非被鸭子吃掉了一部分”而获公共卫生奖；白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科因立法禁止公共场合鼓掌，与因“鼓掌罪”逮捕独臂男子的白俄罗斯国家警察共同领走和平奖。

The 23rd First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2013 proved that even creatures rolling balls of manure can look to the stars. Marie Dacke, Emily Baird, Marcus Byrne, Clarke Scholtz, and Eric J. Warrant won the Joint Prize in Biology and Astronomy for fitting nocturnal dung beetles with tiny cardboard caps and testing them under the dome of the Johannesburg Planetarium, discovering that lost dung beetles orient themselves and roll straight home by gazing up at the Milky Way. Equally cosmic was the Physics Prize, awarded to Alberto Minetti, Yuri Ivanenko, Germana Cappellini, Nadia Dominici, and Francesco Lacquaniti for strapping harnessed volunteers over a wading pool to prove that humans would be physically capable of running across the surface of a pond — provided those people and that pond were in the low gravity of the Moon.

Medical, chemical, and archaeological dedication reached heroic extremes. Masateru Uchiyama, Xiangyuan Jin, Qi Zhang, Toshihito Hirai, Atsushi Amano, Hisashi Bashuda, and Masanori Niimi won the Medicine Prize for playing Verdi's opera La Traviata to mice that had just received heart transplants, demonstrating that opera-listening mice enjoyed stronger immune regulation and survived significantly longer than mice exposed to single-frequency tones. Shinsuke Imai, Nobuaki Tsuge, Muneaki Tomotake, Yoshiaki Nagatome, H. Sawada, Toshiyuki Nagata, and Hidehiko Kumagai earned the Chemistry Prize for discovering 'lachrymatory factor synthase,' proving that the biochemical process by which onions make people cry is far more complicated than scientists had realized. And archaeologists Brian Crandall and Peter Stahl claimed the Archaeology Prize for parboiling a dead shrew, swallowing it whole without chewing, and painstakingly sifting through everything excreted over subsequent days to see which micro-mammalian bones dissolve inside the human digestive tract.

Psychology, bovine probability, and surreal public policy completed the night. Laurent Bègue, Brad Bushman, Oulmann Zerhouni, Baptiste Subra, and Medhi Ourabah won the Psychology Prize for confirming by experiment that people who merely think they are drunk also think they are remarkably attractive ('beauty is in the eye of the beer holder'). Bert Tolkamp, Marie Haskell, Fritha Langford, David Roberts, and Colin Morgan captured the Probability Prize for two related dairy discoveries: first, the longer a cow has been lying down, the more likely that cow will soon stand up; and second, once a cow stands up, you cannot easily predict how soon it will lie down again. The Safety Engineering Prize honored the late Gustano Pizzo for his 1972 patent on an anti-hijacking system that drops an airplane hijacker through trap doors, seals him into a capsule, and parachutes him through bomb bay doors to waiting police on the ground. Thailand's Kasian Bhanganada, Tu Chayavatana, Chumporn Pongnumkul, Anunt Tonmukayakul, Piyasakol Sakolsatayadorn, Krit Komaratal, and Henry Wilde won the Public Health Prize for their report 'Surgical Management of an Epidemic of Penile Amputations in Siam' — techniques they recommend except in cases where the amputated penis had been partially eaten by a duck. Finally, the Peace Prize went jointly to Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, for making it illegal to applaud in public, and to the Belarus State Police, for arresting a one-armed man for applauding.

2013年第二十三届搞笑诺贝尔奖证明，哪怕脚下推着粪球，心中也能装着浩瀚宇宙。瑞典、澳洲、南非等地学者玛丽·达克、艾米莉·贝尔德、马库斯·伯恩、克拉克·朔尔茨与埃里克·瓦兰特斩获生物学与天文学联合奖：他们给屎壳郎戴上小纸帽并在天象馆实验，首次证实迷路的屎壳郎竟能靠仰望银河系的光带导航回家！物理学奖得主阿尔贝托·米内蒂、尤里·伊万年科、杰尔马娜·卡佩利尼、娜迪亚·多米尼奇与弗朗切斯科·拉夸尼蒂则通过悬吊减重模拟发现，若把人类和池塘搬到月球等低重力环境，人真能施展“水上漂”跑过池塘水面。

The 23rd First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2013 proved that even creatures rolling balls of manure can look to the stars. Marie Dacke, Emily Baird, Marcus Byrne, Clarke Scholtz, and Eric J. Warrant won the Joint Prize in Biology and Astronomy for fitting nocturnal dung beetles with tiny cardboard caps and testing them under the dome of the Johannesburg Planetarium, discovering that lost dung beetles orient themselves and roll straight home by gazing up at the Milky Way. Equally cosmic was the Physics Prize, awarded to Alberto Minetti, Yuri Ivanenko, Germana Cappellini, Nadia Dominici, and Francesco Lacquaniti for strapping harnessed volunteers over a wading pool to prove that humans would be physically capable of running across the surface of a pond — provided those people and that pond were in the low gravity of the Moon.

医学、化学与考古学家的奉献精神同样令人肃然起敬。日本与中国学者内山雅照、金相元、张祺、平井敏仁、天野笃、判田久与新见正则给做完心脏移植手术的小鼠播放歌剧《茶花女》，发现听歌剧的小鼠免疫排斥更少、术后存活期显著延长，荣膺医学奖。今井真介、柘植信昭、友竹宗昭、长留吉朗、泽田、长田敏行与熊谷英彦因发现催泪因子合成酶、证明洋葱让人流泪的生化过程比原先以为的复杂得多而摘得化学奖。考古学家布赖恩·克兰德尔和彼得·斯塔尔更是狠人中的狠人：为查明人类消化道会溶解哪些小型哺乳动物骨骼，他们把死鼩鼱稍微水煮后不经咀嚼整只生吞下肚，连续数日仔细筛查排泄物，硬核捧走考古学奖。

Masateru Uchiyama, Xiangyuan Jin, Qi Zhang, Toshihito Hirai, Atsushi Amano, Hisashi Bashuda, and Masanori Niimi won the Medicine Prize for playing Verdi's opera La Traviata to mice that had just received heart transplants, demonstrating that opera-listening mice enjoyed stronger immune regulation and survived significantly longer than mice exposed to single-frequency tones. Shinsuke Imai, Nobuaki Tsuge, Muneaki Tomotake, Yoshiaki Nagatome, H. Sawada, Toshiyuki Nagata, and Hidehiko Kumagai earned the Chemistry Prize for discovering 'lachrymatory factor synthase,' proving that the biochemical process by which onions make people cry is far more complicated than scientists had realized. And archaeologists Brian Crandall and Peter Stahl claimed the Archaeology Prize for parboiling a dead shrew, swallowing it whole without chewing, and painstakingly sifting through everything excreted over subsequent days to see which micro-mammalian bones dissolve inside the human digestive tract.

心理、概率与社会奇闻同样精彩绝伦。洛朗·贝格、布拉德·布什曼、乌尔曼·泽尔胡尼、巴蒂斯特·苏布拉与迈赫迪·乌拉巴通过安慰剂实验证实“自以为喝醉的人也会觉得自己很有魅力”，拿下心理学奖。伯特·托尔坎普、玛丽·哈斯凯尔、弗里莎·兰福德、大卫·罗伯茨与科林·摩根斩获概率学奖，发现奶牛趴着越久越可能很快站起来，但一旦站起来就很难预测它何时再趴下。已故美国发明家古斯塔诺·皮佐因设计用活板门把劫机犯掉入舱底打包封装、再从弹舱门挂降落伞空投给地面警察的防劫机系统获安全工程奖；泰国医生卡西安·班加纳达等七人因发表《暹罗阴茎切除流行病的外科处理》、推荐实施再植术——“除非被鸭子吃掉了一部分”而获公共卫生奖；白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科因立法禁止公共场合鼓掌，与因“鼓掌罪”逮捕独臂男子的白俄罗斯国家警察共同领走和平奖。

Bert Tolkamp, Marie Haskell, Fritha Langford, David Roberts, and Colin Morgan captured the Probability Prize for two related dairy discoveries: first, the longer a cow has been lying down, the more likely that cow will soon stand up; and second, once a cow stands up, you cannot easily predict how soon it will lie down again. Finally, the Peace Prize went jointly to Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, for making it illegal to applaud in public, and to the Belarus State Police, for arresting a one-armed man for applauding.

在《暹罗阴茎切除流行病的外科处理》中提出断肢再植医疗技术，推荐在除“被鸭子吃掉一部分”之外的情况下使用。

2014 第24届搞笑诺贝尔奖 24th Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 855 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 531 words · 10 Prizes

踩香蕉皮摩擦系数、烤吐司显灵与顺着地磁线便便的狗 Banana-Peel Tribology, Jesus in Toast, and Geomagnetic Pooping Dogs

从咸猪肉塞鼻孔止血、假扮北极熊吓驯鹿到婴儿便便发酵香肠 From Cured-Pork Nosebleed Packing and Polar-Bear Disguises to Infant-Feces Probiotic Sausages

📖 2014年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2014 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2014年第二十四届搞笑诺贝尔奖用严谨数据解答了喜剧片里的百年老梗。日本北里大学的马渕清资、田中健诚、内岛大地与酒井利奈夺得物理学奖：他们用鞋底踩踏测力板上的香蕉皮，测出香蕉皮内侧多糖滤泡凝胶微囊在重压下会破裂化作润滑液膜，使摩擦系数骤降至0.07，比普通地板滑六倍。中国与加拿大学者刘建刚、李军、冯路、李凌、田捷与李康则聚焦“面部空想性错视”，通过脑成像揭示那些在烤吐司面包上看到耶稣面孔的人，大脑面孔区究竟发生了怎样的神经活动，荣膺神经科学奖。

动物磁场、暗黑人格与艺术止痛同样令人大开眼界。捷克、德国与赞比亚的弗拉斯蒂米尔·哈特、佩特拉·诺瓦科娃、海内克·布尔达等十二位学者耗时两年记录70只狗的数千次排泄，证实狗狗在排便和排尿时喜欢将身体轴线与地球南北地磁线对齐，摘得生物学奖。雅罗斯拉夫·弗莱格、扬·哈夫利切克、伊特卡·哈努绍娃-林多娃与大卫·哈瑙尔、纳伦·拉马克里希南、莉萨·赛弗里德因调查养猫（弓形虫感染与猫咬伤）是否会危及人类精神健康而共享公共卫生奖。彼得·乔纳森、艾米·琼斯与明娜·莱昂斯发现习惯熬夜的人比早起者平均更自恋、更具操纵欲且心理变态倾向更高，捧走心理学奖；意大利学者玛丽娜·德托马索、米歇尔·萨尔达罗与保罗·利夫雷亚用强激光束照射受试者手部，证实欣赏优美名画比看丑陋画作更能减轻疼痛，拿下艺术奖。

极地探险、急救偏方与国民经济核算更是妙趣横生。挪威学者艾吉尔·雷默斯与辛德雷·埃夫特斯托尔假扮成北极熊去悄悄接近斯瓦尔巴群岛的驯鹿，测试驯鹿的逃跑反应，夺得北极科学奖。美印医生伊恩·汉弗莱斯、索娜尔·萨赖亚、沃尔特·贝伦基与詹姆斯·德沃金因用腌猪肉条塞进患儿鼻腔、成功止住罕见病引发的致命鼻出血而获医学奖。西班牙学者拉奎尔·鲁维奥、安娜·霍夫雷、贝伦·马丁、特雷莎·艾梅里奇与玛格丽塔·加里加从婴儿粪便中分离出乳酸菌作为益生菌发酵剂来制作发酵香肠，斩获营养学奖；意大利国家统计局（ISTAT）则因率先响应欧盟指令，自豪地将卖淫、毒品交易与走私收入纳入官方国民经济统计规模，领走经济学奖。

The 24th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2014 brought hard numbers to slapstick comedy and pareidolia. Japanese researchers Kiyoshi Mabuchi, Kensei Tanaka, Daichi Uchijima, and Rina Sakai of Kitasato University won the Physics Prize for measuring the exact frictional coefficient between a shoe, a banana skin, and a linoleum floor when a person steps on a banana peel — showing that squished polysaccharide follicular gel globules slash friction down to 0.07, making banana peels six times slipperier than bare floors. Meanwhile, Jiangang Liu, Jun Li, Lu Feng, Ling Li, Jie Tian, and Kang Lee of China and Canada captured the Neuroscience Prize for their fMRI study 'Seeing Jesus in Toast,' mapping the neural activity in the brain's fusiform face area when people perceive illusory faces in random noise or burnt breakfast bread.

Magnetic canines, nocturnal personalities, and laser-zapped art lovers took center stage next. A twelve-member team from the Czech Republic, Germany, and Zambia — Vlastimil Hart, Petra Nováková, Erich Pascal Malkemper, Sabine Begall, Vladimír Hanzal, Miloš Ježek, Tomáš Kušta, Veronika Němcová, Jana Adámková, Kateřina Benediktová, Jaroslav Červený, and Hynek Burda — won the Biology Prize for documenting thousands of canine bathroom breaks over two years to prove that when dogs defecate and urinate under calm geomagnetic conditions, they prefer to align their bodies with Earth's north-south magnetic field lines. The Public Health Prize was shared by Jaroslav Flegr, Jan Havlíček, and Jitka Hanušova-Lindova, along with David Hanauer, Naren Ramakrishnan, and Lisa Seyfried, for investigating whether owning a cat is mentally hazardous to humans due to latent Toxoplasma gondii infection and cat-bite-linked depression. Psychologists Peter K. Jonason, Amy Jones, and Minna Lyons won the Psychology Prize for amassing evidence that night owls who habitually stay up late are, on average, more narcissistic, more manipulative, and more psychopathic ('Dark Triad' traits) than early risers. And Italian researchers Marina de Tommaso, Michele Sardaro, and Paolo Livrea won the Art Prize for shooting volunteers in the hand with a powerful laser beam to prove people suffer less pain while gazing at a beautiful painting by Botticelli than while staring at an ugly painting.

Arctic masquerades, savory emergency medicine, and creative national accounting closed the show. Norwegian researchers Eigil Reimers and Sindre Eftestøl won the Arctic Science Prize for dressing up in white polar-bear disguises on the island of Edgeøya to test how Svalbard reindeer react when approached by humans disguised as polar bears. Ian Humphreys, Sonal Saraiya, Walter Belenky, and James Dworkin of the USA and India received the Medicine Prize for successfully treating 'uncontrollable' life-threatening nosebleeds in a patient with Glanzmann thrombasthenia by packing the nasal cavity with strips of cured salted pork. Spanish food scientists Raquel Rubio, Anna Jofré, Belén Martín, Teresa Aymerich, and Margarita Garriga earned the Nutrition Prize for isolating lactic acid bacteria from infant feces to use as probiotic starter cultures for tasty fermented sausages. Finally, ISTAT — the Italian government's National Institute of Statistics — proudly claimed the Economics Prize for taking the lead in fulfilling a European Union mandate to boost the official size of its national economy by including revenues from prostitution, illegal drug sales, smuggling, and other unlawful financial transactions between willing participants.

Japanese researchers Kiyoshi Mabuchi, Kensei Tanaka, Daichi Uchijima, and Rina Sakai of Kitasato University won the Physics Prize for measuring the exact frictional coefficient between a shoe, a banana skin, and a linoleum floor when a person steps on a banana peel — showing that squished polysaccharide follicular gel globules slash friction down to 0.07, making banana peels six times slipperier than bare floors. Meanwhile, Jiangang Liu, Jun Li, Lu Feng, Ling Li, Jie Tian, and Kang Lee of China and Canada captured the Neuroscience Prize for their fMRI study 'Seeing Jesus in Toast,' mapping the neural activity in the brain's fusiform face area when people perceive illusory faces in random noise or burnt breakfast bread.

动物磁场、暗黑人格与艺术止痛同样令人大开眼界。捷克、德国与赞比亚的弗拉斯蒂米尔·哈特、佩特拉·诺瓦科娃、海内克·布尔达等十二位学者耗时两年记录70只狗的数千次排泄，证实狗狗在排便和排尿时喜欢将身体轴线与地球南北地磁线对齐，摘得生物学奖。雅罗斯拉夫·弗莱格、扬·哈夫利切克、伊特卡·哈努绍娃-林多娃与大卫·哈瑙尔、纳伦·拉马克里希南、莉萨·赛弗里德因调查养猫（弓形虫感染与猫咬伤）是否会危及人类精神健康而共享公共卫生奖。彼得·乔纳森、艾米·琼斯与明娜·莱昂斯发现习惯熬夜的人比早起者平均更自恋、更具操纵欲且心理变态倾向更高，捧走心理学奖；意大利学者玛丽娜·德托马索、米歇尔·萨尔达罗与保罗·利夫雷亚用强激光束照射受试者手部，证实欣赏优美名画比看丑陋画作更能减轻疼痛，拿下艺术奖。

Magnetic canines, nocturnal personalities, and laser-zapped art lovers took center stage next. A twelve-member team from the Czech Republic, Germany, and Zambia — Vlastimil Hart, Petra Nováková, Erich Pascal Malkemper, Sabine Begall, Vladimír Hanzal, Miloš Ježek, Tomáš Kušta, Veronika Němcová, Jana Adámková, Kateřina Benediktová, Jaroslav Červený, and Hynek Burda — won the Biology Prize for documenting thousands of canine bathroom breaks over two years to prove that when dogs defecate and urinate under calm geomagnetic conditions, they prefer to align their bodies with Earth's north-south magnetic field lines. The Public Health Prize was shared by Jaroslav Flegr, Jan Havlíček, and Jitka Hanušova-Lindova, along with David Hanauer, Naren Ramakrishnan, and Lisa Seyfried, for investigating whether owning a cat is mentally hazardous to humans due to latent Toxoplasma gondii infection and cat-bite-linked depression. Psychologists Peter K. Jonason, Amy Jones, and Minna Lyons won the Psychology Prize for amassing evidence that night owls who habitually stay up late are, on average, more narcissistic, more manipulative, and more psychopathic ('Dark Triad' traits) than early risers. And Italian researchers Marina de Tommaso, Michele Sardaro, and Paolo Livrea won the Art Prize for shooting volunteers in the hand with a powerful laser beam to prove people suffer less pain while gazing at a beautiful painting by Botticelli than while staring at an ugly painting.

极地探险、急救偏方与国民经济核算更是妙趣横生。挪威学者艾吉尔·雷默斯与辛德雷·埃夫特斯托尔假扮成北极熊去悄悄接近斯瓦尔巴群岛的驯鹿，测试驯鹿的逃跑反应，夺得北极科学奖。美印医生伊恩·汉弗莱斯、索娜尔·萨赖亚、沃尔特·贝伦基与詹姆斯·德沃金因用腌猪肉条塞进患儿鼻腔、成功止住罕见病引发的致命鼻出血而获医学奖。西班牙学者拉奎尔·鲁维奥、安娜·霍夫雷、贝伦·马丁、特雷莎·艾梅里奇与玛格丽塔·加里加从婴儿粪便中分离出乳酸菌作为益生菌发酵剂来制作发酵香肠，斩获营养学奖；意大利国家统计局（ISTAT）则因率先响应欧盟指令，自豪地将卖淫、毒品交易与走私收入纳入官方国民经济统计规模，领走经济学奖。

Arctic masquerades, savory emergency medicine, and creative national accounting closed the show. Norwegian researchers Eigil Reimers and Sindre Eftestøl won the Arctic Science Prize for dressing up in white polar-bear disguises on the island of Edgeøya to test how Svalbard reindeer react when approached by humans disguised as polar bears. Ian Humphreys, Sonal Saraiya, Walter Belenky, and James Dworkin of the USA and India received the Medicine Prize for successfully treating 'uncontrollable' life-threatening nosebleeds in a patient with Glanzmann thrombasthenia by packing the nasal cavity with strips of cured salted pork. Spanish food scientists Raquel Rubio, Anna Jofré, Belén Martín, Teresa Aymerich, and Margarita Garriga earned the Nutrition Prize for isolating lactic acid bacteria from infant feces to use as probiotic starter cultures for tasty fermented sausages. Finally, ISTAT — the Italian government's National Institute of Statistics — proudly claimed the Economics Prize for taking the lead in fulfilling a European Union mandate to boost the official size of its national economy by including revenues from prostitution, illegal drug sales, smuggling, and other unlawful financial transactions between willing participants.

🏅 获奖者：马渕清资 (Kiyoshi Mabuchi), 田中健诚 (Kensei Tanaka), 内岛大地 (Daichi Uchijima), 酒井利奈 (Rina Sakai)🏅 Winners: Kiyoshi Mabuchi, Kensei Tanaka, Daichi Uchijima, Rina Sakai
精确测量当人踩到地上的香蕉皮时，鞋底与香蕉皮之间以及香蕉皮与地板之间的摩擦系数。
For measuring the amount of friction between a shoe and a banana skin, and between a banana skin and the floor, when a person steps on a banana skin.
#02神经科学奖 (Neuroscience)Neuroscience Prize
🏅 获奖者：刘建刚 (Jiangang Liu), 李军 (Jun Li), 冯路 (Lu Feng), 李凌 (Ling Li), 田捷 (Jie Tian), 李康 (Kang Lee)🏅 Winners: Jiangang Liu, Jun Li, Lu Feng, Ling Li, Jie Tian, Kang Lee
试图弄清楚那些在烤吐司面包上看到耶稣面孔的人，大脑里究竟发生了什么神经活动（面部空想性错视）。
For trying to understand what happens in the brains of people who see the face of Jesus in a piece of toast.
#03心理学奖 (Psychology)Psychology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Peter K. Jonason, Amy Jones, Minna Lyons🏅 Winners: Peter K. Jonason, Amy Jones, Minna Lyons
收集证据表明，习惯熬夜的人平均而言比习惯早起的人更自恋、更具操纵欲且更有心理变态倾向（黑暗三联征）。
For amassing evidence that people who habitually stay up late are, on average, more self-admiring, more manipulative, and more psychopathic than people who habitually arise early.
#04公共卫生奖 (Public Health)Public Health Prize
🏅 获奖者：Jaroslav Flegr, Jan Havlíček, Jitka Hanušova-Lindova 与 David Hanauer, Naren Ramakrishnan, Lisa Seyfried🏅 Winners: Jaroslav Flegr, Jan Havlíček, Jitka Hanušova-Lindova; and David Hanauer, Naren Ramakrishnan, Lisa Seyfried
研究人类养猫（如潜伏感染弓形虫或被猫咬伤）是否会对人类的心理健康与精神状态造成危害。
For investigating whether it is mentally hazardous for a human being to own a cat.
#05生物学奖 (Biology)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Vlastimil Hart, Petra Nováková, Erich Pascal Malkemper, Sabine Begall, Vladimír Hanzal, Miloš Ježek, Tomáš Kušta, Veronika Němcová, Jana Adámková, Kateřina Benediktová, Jaroslav Červený, Hynek Burda🏅 Winners: Vlastimil Hart, Petra Nováková, Erich Pascal Malkemper, Sabine Begall, Vladimír Hanzal, Miloš Ježek, Tomáš Kušta, Veronika Němcová, Jana Adámková, Kateřina Benediktová, Jaroslav Červený, Hynek Burda
仔细记录并证实狗狗在排便和排尿时，在地磁场稳定的情况下喜欢将身体轴线与地球南北地磁线对齐。
For carefully documenting that when dogs defecate and urinate, they prefer to align their body axis with Earth's north-south geomagnetic field lines.
#06艺术奖 (Art)Art Prize
🏅 获奖者：Marina de Tommaso, Michele Sardaro, Paolo Livrea🏅 Winners: Marina de Tommaso, Michele Sardaro, Paolo Livrea
测量当人们的手部被强激光束照射时，看着丑陋画作与欣赏优美名画所承受的相对疼痛感差异。
For measuring the relative pain people suffer while looking at an ugly painting, rather than a pretty painting, while being shot in the hand by a powerful laser beam.
#07经济学奖 (Economics)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：意大利国家统计局 (ISTAT)🏅 Winners: ISTAT (Italian National Institute of Statistics)
自豪地率先履行欧盟指令，将卖淫、非法毒品销售、走私及其他自愿非法金融交易的收入纳入国民经济官方统计规模。
For proudly taking the lead in fulfilling the European Union mandate to increase the official size of its national economy by including revenues from prostitution, illegal drug sales, smuggling, and other unlawful transactions.
#08医学奖 (Medicine)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Ian Humphreys, Sonal Saraiya, Walter Belenky, James Dworkin🏅 Winners: Ian Humphreys, Sonal Saraiya, Walter Belenky, James Dworkin
使用腌制咸猪肉条填塞鼻腔的方法，成功治疗“无法控制的”严重鼻出血。
For treating 'uncontrollable' nosebleeds using the method of nasal packing with strips of cured pork.
#09北极科学奖 (Arctic Science)Arctic Science Prize
🏅 获奖者：Eigil Reimers, Sindre Eftestøl🏅 Winners: Eigil Reimers, Sindre Eftestøl
测试斯瓦尔巴群岛的驯鹿在看到伪装成北极熊的人类时会做出怎样的警戒与逃跑反应。
For testing how reindeer react to seeing humans who are disguised as polar bears.
#10营养学奖 (Nutrition)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：Raquel Rubio, Anna Jofré, Belén Martín, Teresa Aymerich, Margarita Garriga🏅 Winners: Raquel Rubio, Anna Jofré, Belén Martín, Teresa Aymerich, Margarita Garriga
研究从婴儿粪便中分离出的乳酸菌，评估其作为发酵香肠潜在益生菌发酵剂的特性与风味表现。
For their study titled 'Characterization of Lactic Acid Bacteria Isolated from Infant Faeces as Potential Probiotic Starter Cultures for Fermented Sausages.'
2015 第25届搞笑诺贝尔奖 25th Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 826 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 578 words · 10 Prizes

2015：二十一秒排尿定律、绑棍恐龙鸡与生熟逆转的鸡蛋 2015: The 21-Second Law of Urination, Plunger-Tailed Dino-Chickens & Un-Boiled Eggs

第25届盛典：从蜜蜂全身蛰痛地图到嗜血苏丹的数学后宫 The 25th Silver Jubilee Ceremony: From Whole-Body Bee-Sting Maps to a Bloodthirsty Sultan's Mathematical Harem

📖 2015年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2015 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2015年第25届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院迎来银禧盛典，科学家们率先对生物演化与流体物理发起奇袭。智利学者布鲁诺·格罗西团队斩获生物学奖：他们把一根配重木棍绑在活鸡屁股后面改变身体重心，小鸡走路的姿态便瞬间从膝盖弯曲变成髋部驱动，完美复刻出远古霸王龙的威猛步伐。美籍华裔学者胡立德与杨佩良团队则凭动物园排尿录像摘得物理学奖，证实几乎所有体重超过三公斤的哺乳动物，无论猫狗、山羊还是大象，排空膀胱的时间都恒定在二十一秒左右。化学奖颁给了美澳学者奥蒙德、拉斯顿与韦斯等人，他们利用尿素与高速涡流流体装置解开缠结的蛋白质，硬生生把煮熟的鸡蛋“部分变回”生鸡蛋。

在痛觉与医学考场上，研究者们展现了惊人的献身精神。生理学与昆虫学奖由美国学者贾斯汀·施密特与迈克尔·史密斯共享：前者尝遍天下毒虫创立“施密特蛰痛指数”；后者亲自抓蜜蜂在自己全身二十五个部位反复蛰刺，用血泪绘出人体疼痛地图——头皮、中趾尖与上臂最轻，而鼻孔、上唇和阴茎干最痛彻心扉。英国与加拿大等国的阿什当、卡里姆团队获诊断医学奖，证实只需开车载患者经过减速带，凭剧痛反应就能准确诊断急性阑尾炎。医学奖则由日本学者木俣肇与斯洛伐克的塞莱茨、杜尔佳科娃团队共享，前者证实激烈接吻能显著缓解皮肤过敏反应，后者则测出热吻后女性唾液中竟能长久检出男性的遗传物质。

数学与人文社科奖项同样妙趣横生。奥地利学者奥伯扎彻与格拉默获数学奖，通过计算机数学模拟证实摩洛哥历史上的“嗜血苏丹”穆莱·伊斯梅尔在三十年间生育八百八十八个孩子并非神话，每天只需行房约一次即可达成。荷兰丁格曼斯、托雷拉与恩菲尔德凭文学奖发现，“啊（啥）？”这个疑问词几乎存在于人类每一种语言中，尽管他们也不太确定原因。管理学奖得主伯尼尔等人发现，童年历经地震、海啸或火山爆发却毫发无损的企业总裁，成年后在商界更酷爱冒险博弈。最绝的是经济学奖得主泰国曼谷大都会警察局：若警员当场拒绝收受贿赂，警局就直接发给他们额外现金奖金，用魔法打败魔法。

The 25th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony celebrated its silver jubilee at Harvard's Sanders Theatre by turning evolutionary biology and fluid dynamics upside down. Chilean biologist Bruno Grossi and his colleagues captured the Biology Prize by strapping a weighted wooden stick—resembling a miniature toilet plunger—onto the rear ends of growing chickens. The added counterweight shifted the birds' center of mass backward, forcing their femurs into a more horizontal posture and switching their locomotion from knee-driven to hip-driven strides, uncannily recreating the walk of extinct non-avian theropod dinosaurs like Tyrannosaurus rex. Meanwhile, Patricia Yang, David Hu, Jonathan Pham, and Jerome Choo claimed the Physics Prize after filming animals relieving themselves at Zoo Atlanta. Their fluid-dynamics equations proved the 'Law of Urination': nearly all mammals weighing over three kilograms—whether cats, goats, or elephants—empty their bladders in roughly 21 seconds (plus or minus 13 seconds), thanks to longer urethras amplifying gravitational flow in larger beasts.

In the realms of chemistry and extreme human endurance, researchers displayed breathtaking ingenuity and personal sacrifice. Australian and American chemists led by Callum Ormonde, Colin Raston, and Gregory Weiss won the Chemistry Prize for inventing a chemical recipe to partially un-boil a hard-boiled egg, using urea and a high-shear vortex fluidic device to untangle and refold coagulated lysozyme proteins. The Physiology and Entomology Prize went jointly to two legends of self-inflicted agony: Justin Schmidt, who painstakingly cataloged insect venom agony in his poetic 'Schmidt Sting Pain Index,' and Cornell researcher Michael L. Smith, who held live honeybees by the wings and pressed them against 25 locations on his own body three times each. Smith's anatomical pain map revealed that the skull, middle toe tip, and upper arm barely hurt, whereas the nostril, upper lip, and penis shaft deliver electrifying torment.

Medical diagnostics and human intimacy yielded equally unforgettable insights. A British-led team including Helen Ashdown, Diallah Karim, and Anthony Harnden won the Diagnostic Medicine Prize for demonstrating that acute appendicitis can be diagnosed with 97 percent sensitivity simply by asking patients whether they felt excruciating pain when driven over speed bumps on their way to the hospital. The Medicine Prize was shared by Japan's Hajime Kimata—who proved that 30 minutes of intense kissing (or sexual intercourse) significantly reduces allergic skin wheal responses and allergen-specific IgE production—and Slovakian researchers led by Jaroslava Durdiaková and Peter Celec, who quantified how long male DNA persists in female saliva after passionate French kissing. Over in Mathematics, Austria's Elisabeth Oberzaucher and Karl Grammer used computer simulations to verify whether Morocco's Sharifian Emperor Moulay Ismael the Bloodthirsty really fathered 888 children between 1697 and 1727, concluding that he needed a harem of only 65 to 110 women and roughly one copulation per day.

Finally, language, risk-taking, and anti-corruption took center stage in the social sciences. Linguists Mark Dingemanse, Francisco Torreira, and Nick Enfield earned the Literature Prize for discovering that the syllable 'Huh?'—or a nearly identical questioning grunt—exists in every human language they sampled across the globe, and for candidly admitting they were not completely sure why. Management Prize winners Gennaro Bernile, Vineet Bhagwat, and P. Raghavendra Rau showed that corporate CEOs who survived childhood natural disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, or wildfires without dire personal loss grew up with a lifelong fondness for risky financial gambles. Topping off the evening, the Economics Prize went to the Bangkok Metropolitan Police in Thailand, who tackled traffic corruption by offering officers a 10,000-baht cash bonus every time they refused to accept a bribe.

The Medicine Prize was shared by Japan's Hajime Kimata—who proved that 30 minutes of intense kissing (or sexual intercourse) significantly reduces allergic skin wheal responses and allergen-specific IgE production—and Slovakian researchers led by Jaroslava Durdiaková and Peter Celec, who quantified how long male DNA persists in female saliva after passionate French kissing. Over in Mathematics, Austria's Elisabeth Oberzaucher and Karl Grammer used computer simulations to verify whether Morocco's Sharifian Emperor Moulay Ismael the Bloodthirsty really fathered 888 children between 1697 and 1727, concluding that he needed a harem of only 65 to 110 women and roughly one copulation per day.

Finally, language, risk-taking, and anti-corruption took center stage in the social sciences. Linguists Mark Dingemanse, Francisco Torreira, and Nick Enfield earned the Literature Prize for discovering that the syllable 'Huh?'—or a nearly identical questioning grunt—exists in every human language they sampled across the globe, and for candidly admitting they were not completely sure why. Management Prize winners Gennaro Bernile, Vineet Bhagwat, and P. Raghavendra Rau showed that corporate CEOs who survived childhood natural disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, or wildfires without dire personal loss grew up with a lifelong fondness for risky financial gambles. Topping off the evening, the Economics Prize went to the Bangkok Metropolitan Police in Thailand, who tackled traffic corruption by offering officers a 10,000-baht cash bonus every time they refused to accept a bribe.

#01化学奖 (Chemistry Prize)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Callum Ormonde, Colin Raston, Tom Yuan, Gregory Weiss 等（澳大利亚/美国）🏅 Winners: Callum Ormonde, Colin Raston, Tom Yuan, Gregory Weiss, et al. (Australia / USA)
发明了一套利用尿素与高速涡流流体装置解开蛋白质缠结、将煮熟的鸡蛋“部分变回”生鸡蛋的化学配方。
For inventing a chemical recipe using urea and a vortex fluidic device to untangle proteins and partially un-boil a hard-boiled egg.
#02物理学奖 (Physics Prize)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Patricia Yang（杨佩良）, David Hu（胡立德）, Jonathan Pham, Jerome Choo（美国/中国台湾）🏅 Winners: Patricia Yang, David Hu, Jonathan Pham, and Jerome Choo (USA / Taiwan)
检验并证实了一条流体生物学定律：几乎所有体重超过3公斤的哺乳动物排空膀胱的时间都约为21秒（正负13秒）。
For testing the biological principle that nearly all mammals empty their bladders in about 21 seconds (plus or minus 13 seconds), regardless of body size.
#03文学奖 (Literature Prize)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：Mark Dingemanse, Francisco Torreira, Nick J. Enfield（荷兰/美国/西班牙/澳大利亚等）🏅 Winners: Mark Dingemanse, Francisco Torreira, and Nick J. Enfield (The Netherlands / USA / Spain / Australia)
发现“Huh?（啊/啥？）”或其同义疑问词似乎存在于人类每一种语言中，而他们也不完全确定这是为什么。
For discovering that the word 'huh?' (or its equivalent) seems to exist in every human language—and for not being completely sure why.
#04管理学奖 (Management Prize)Management Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gennaro Bernile, Vineet Bhagwat, P. Raghavendra Rau（意大利/新加坡/美国/印度/英国等）🏅 Winners: Gennaro Bernile, Vineet Bhagwat, and P. Raghavendra Rau (Italy / Singapore / USA / India / UK)
发现许多商界领袖之所以酷爱冒险，是因为他们在童年经历过地震、火山爆发或海啸等自然灾害且毫发无损。
For discovering that many business leaders developed a fondness for risk-taking after experiencing childhood natural disasters without dire personal consequences.
#05经济学奖 (Economics Prize)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：泰国曼谷大都会警察局（The Bangkok Metropolitan Police）🏅 Winners: The Bangkok Metropolitan Police (Thailand)
决定如果警察拒绝收受贿赂，警局就向其发放额外的现金奖励。
For offering to pay police officers extra cash bonuses if the policemen refuse to take bribes from motorists.
#06医学奖 (Medicine Prize)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：木俣肇（Hajime Kimata，日本）与 Jaroslava Durdiaková, Peter Celec 等（斯洛伐克）🏅 Winners: Hajime Kimata (Japan) and Jaroslava Durdiaková, Peter Celec, et al. (Slovakia)
通过实验研究激烈接吻及亲密互动的生物医学益处与后果，包括缓解皮肤过敏反应以及热吻后女性唾液中男性DNA的存留。
For experiments studying the biomedical benefits and consequences of intense kissing, including reduced skin allergies and the persistence of male DNA in mixed saliva.
#07数学奖 (Mathematics Prize)Mathematics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Elisabeth Oberzaucher, Karl Grammer（奥地利/德国/英国）🏅 Winners: Elisabeth Oberzaucher and Karl Grammer (Austria / Germany / UK)
运用数学建模与计算机模拟，测算摩洛哥“嗜血苏丹”穆莱·伊斯梅尔如何在1697至1727年间成功生育888个孩子。
For using mathematical modeling to determine whether and how Moulay Ismael the Bloodthirsty, Emperor of Morocco, managed to father 888 children in 30 years.
#08生物学奖 (Biology Prize)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Bruno Grossi, José Iriarte-Díaz, Omar Larach, Mauricio Canals, Rodrigo A. Vásquez（智利/美国）🏅 Winners: Bruno Grossi, José Iriarte-Díaz, Omar Larach, Mauricio Canals, and Rodrigo A. Vásquez (Chile / USA)
观察到在活鸡屁股后面绑上一根配重假尾巴后，鸡走路的姿态会变得像已灭绝的兽脚类恐龙。
For observing that when you attach a weighted stick to the rear end of a chicken, the chicken walks in a manner similar to how dinosaurs are thought to have walked.
#09诊断医学奖 (Diagnostic Medicine Prize)Diagnostic Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Diallah Karim, Anthony Harnden, Nigel D’Souza, Helen Ashdown 等（英国/加拿大/新西兰等）🏅 Winners: Diallah Karim, Anthony Harnden, Nigel D’Souza, Helen Ashdown, et al. (UK / Canada / New Zealand)
证实急性阑尾炎可以通过患者乘车经过减速带时的疼痛剧烈程度来准确诊断。
For determining that acute appendicitis can be accurately diagnosed by the amount of pain a patient feels when driven over speed bumps.
#10生理学与昆虫学奖 (Physiology and Entomology Prize)Physiology and Entomology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Justin Schmidt 与 Michael L. Smith（美国/加拿大等）🏅 Winners: Justin Schmidt and Michael L. Smith (USA / Canada / UK)
施密特创立了评估昆虫蛰伤相对疼痛等级的“施密特蛰痛指数”；史密斯则让蜜蜂在自己全身25个部位反复蛰刺，测出最不痛的是头皮、中趾尖和上臂，最痛的是鼻孔、上唇和阴茎干。
For creating the Schmidt Sting Pain Index of insect venoms, and for arranging for honeybees to sting 25 different body locations to find the least and most painful spots.
2016 第26届搞笑诺贝尔奖 26th Ig Nobel Prize 2010s 📝 正文 840 字 · 10 项大奖 📝 576 words · 10 Prizes

2016：阿尔卑斯山上的假肢山羊人、涤纶内裤与石头的人格 2016: The Prosthetic GoatMan of the Alps, Polyester Underpants for Rats & The Brand Personality of Rocks

第26届盛典：当哲学家钻进獾洞吃蚯蚓，心理学家向一千名骗子打听诚实 The 26th Ceremony: When Oxford Philosophers Eat Earthworms in Badger Burrows and Psychologists Ask a Thousand Liars About Honesty

📖 2016年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2016 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2016年第26届搞笑诺贝尔奖向人类中心主义发起了最荒诞的挑战。英国两位奇人共同摘得生物学奖：牛津学者查尔斯·福斯特为了体察万物，先后在荒野中像獾一样钻进地洞生吞蚯蚓、像水獭捕鱼、像鹿和狐狸一样流浪；设计师托马斯·思韦茨则厌倦了做人的焦虑，专门定制四足行走的假肢与人工瘤胃，装扮成山羊混进阿尔卑斯山羊群同吃同住了三天。同样沉迷自然的瑞典作家弗雷德里克·舍贝里则凭三卷本自传摘得文学奖，深情记述了自己在孤岛上收集死苍蝇与活食蚜蝇的隐秘快乐。

物理与生殖科学的碰撞擦出了意想不到的静电火花。已故埃及学者艾哈迈德·沙菲克荣膺生殖学奖，他耗时多年给大鼠和人类男性穿上涤纶、纯棉与羊毛材质的小裤衩，发现纯涤纶内裤产生的静电势场会导致公鼠性欲骤降、男性精子锐减。匈牙利与瑞典的霍瓦特、奥克松团队荣获物理学奖，揭开了偏振光的生态谜团：白马最不招马蝇叮咬是因为白毛反射非偏振光；而公墓里抛光的黑色墓碑反射出酷似水面的水平偏振光，竟成了诱骗蜻蜓疯狂产卵的致命陷阱。

在感官与大脑的迷宫里，人类的直觉被轻易戏耍。德国吕贝克大学的赫尔姆兴与施普伦格团队斩获医学奖，证实如果身体左侧奇痒难耐，只需对着镜子抓挠身体右侧，就能靠视觉镜像欺骗大脑而瞬间止痒。日本学者东山笃规与足立浩平获知觉奖，他们系统验证了日本传统“股立窥景”效应，证明当人弯下腰从两腿之间倒着往后看世界时，远处景物在视觉上会显得更小更近。心理学奖得主德贝与弗舒尔团队则找来一千名骗子询问撒谎频率，并严肃评估该不该相信骗子给出的答案。

最后三项大奖对现代社会的浮夸祭出了辛辣手术刀。加拿大滑铁卢大学的佩尼库克团队凭论文《论对伪深刻狗屁言论的接收与识别》荣获和平奖，证明容易被空洞玄学词汇拼凑的心灵鸡汤感动的人普遍缺乏分析思维。新西兰阿维斯团队获经济学奖，他们让消费者给几块普通岩石评估“品牌人格”，人们竟纷纷夸石头“自信迷人”或“诚实可靠”，一举戳穿营销学泡沫。化学奖则颁给了德国大众汽车公司，讽刺其发明只在尾气检测时才自动开启减排模式的作弊软件。

The 26th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony launched a frontal assault on human exceptionalism by honoring researchers who literally stepped into the skins—or hooves—of other species. The Biology Prize went jointly to two British adventurers: Oxford polymath Charles Foster, who spent months living in the wild as a badger (sleeping in a hillside burrow and munching earthworms), an urban fox, an otter, a red deer, and a swift; and designer Thomas Thwaites, who built custom prosthetic forelimbs, hindlimbs, and an artificial rumen so he could spend three days grazing on all fours among a herd of Alpine goats to 'take a holiday from being human.' A kindred spirit in the natural world, Swedish entomologist Fredrik Sjöberg, won the Literature Prize for his three-volume autobiographical masterpiece celebrating the quiet, obsessive bliss of collecting dead flies—and flies that are not yet dead—on a remote Baltic island.

Physics and reproductive medicine collided in a crackle of static electricity and polarized light. The Reproduction Prize honored the late Egyptian urologist Ahmed Shafik, who outfitted male rats in tiny trousers stitched from 100 percent polyester, cotton, wool, or a 50/50 polyester-cotton blend. Shafik discovered that rats wearing pure polyester pants suffered a dramatic drop in sexual activity due to electrostatic potentials generated across the scrotum—a contraceptive effect he subsequently verified in human male volunteers. Meanwhile, Gábor Horváth, Susanne Åkesson, and an international team won the Physics Prize for solving two optical riddles of the insect world: why white-haired horses are the most horsefly-proof horses (their coats scatter unpolarized light, whereas dark horses reflect horizontally polarized light that attracts biting tabanids), and why dragonflies are fatally drawn to polished black tombstones, which mimic the polarized glare of water and trick dragonflies into laying eggs on graves.

Inside the labyrinth of human perception and deception, scientists proved just how easily the brain can be fooled. German neurologists led by Christoph Helmchen and Andreas Sprenger earned the Medicine Prize for showing that if you have a maddening itch on your left forearm, you can relieve it by looking into a mirror positioned at your midline while scratching your right forearm, tricking your visual cortex into soothing the un-scratched limb. Japan's Atsuki Higashiyama and Kohei Adachi took the Perception Prize for investigating 'Matanozoki'—the traditional act of bending over and viewing the world upside down between one's own legs—confirming that inverted posture makes distant landscapes appear smaller and closer. And in the Psychology Prize, Evelyne Debey, Bruno Verschuere, and colleagues interviewed 1,005 subjects aged 6 to 77 to ask how often they lie, before grappling with the philosophical paradox of whether to believe self-reported statistics from prolific liars.

The final trio of prizes aimed a scalpel at modern corporate and cultural pretension. Canadian researchers led by Gordon Pennycook won the Peace Prize for their landmark paper 'On the Reception and Detection of Pseudo-Profound Bullshit,' demonstrating that people who rate randomly generated, grammatically correct buzzword sentences ('Wholeness quiets infinite phenomena') as deeply meaningful score lower in analytic thinking and higher in conspiratorial beliefs. New Zealand and UK scholars Mark Avis, Sarah Forbes, and Shelagh Ferguson claimed the Economics Prize for asking consumers to evaluate the 'brand personality' of ordinary rocks—finding that test subjects eagerly described random stones as 'glamorous,' 'sentimental,' or 'sincere,' thereby exposing the absurdity of corporate brand-personality scales. Finally, the Chemistry Prize was awarded to Volkswagen for solving excessive automobile pollution emissions by electromechanically producing fewer emissions only when the car was being tested.

#01生殖学奖 (Reproduction Prize)Reproduction Prize
🏅 获奖者：已故的艾哈迈德·沙菲克（Ahmed Shafik，埃及）🏅 Winners: The late Ahmed Shafik (Egypt)
研究穿聚酯纤维（涤纶）、纯棉或羊毛裤子对大鼠性生活的影响，并在人类男性身上开展了类似实验。
For studying the effects of wearing polyester, cotton, or wool trousers on the sex life of rats, and for conducting similar tests with human males.
#02经济学奖 (Economics Prize)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Mark Avis, Sarah Forbes, Shelagh Ferguson（新西兰/英国）🏅 Winners: Mark Avis, Sarah Forbes, and Shelagh Ferguson (New Zealand / UK)
从销售和市场营销的角度评估普通岩石被消费者感知的“品牌人格”。
For assessing the perceived brand personalities of ordinary rocks from a sales and marketing perspective.
#03物理学奖 (Physics Prize)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gábor Horváth, Susanne Åkesson 等（匈牙利/西班牙/瑞典/瑞士）🏅 Winners: Gábor Horváth, Susanne Åkesson, et al. (Hungary / Spain / Sweden / Switzerland)
发现为什么白马最不容易招马蝇叮咬，以及为什么蜻蜓会被抛光的黑色墓碑致命地吸引。
For discovering why white-haired horses are the most horsefly-proof horses, and why dragonflies are fatally attracted to polished black tombstones.
#04化学奖 (Chemistry Prize)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：德国大众汽车公司（Volkswagen）🏅 Winners: Volkswagen (Germany)
通过在汽车接受尾气检测时自动、机电式地减少污染物排放，从而“解决”了汽车尾气排放超标问题。
For solving the problem of excessive automobile pollution emissions by automatically, electromechanically producing fewer emissions whenever the cars are being tested.
#05医学奖 (Medicine Prize)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Christoph Helmchen, Carina Palzer, Thomas Münte, Silke Anders, Andreas Sprenger（德国）🏅 Winners: Christoph Helmchen, Carina Palzer, Thomas Münte, Silke Anders, and Andreas Sprenger (Germany)
发现如果身体左侧发痒，可以通过看着镜子并抓挠身体右侧来缓解瘙痒（反之亦然）。
For discovering that if you have an itch on the left side of your body, you can relieve it by looking into a mirror and scratching the right side of your body.
#06心理学奖 (Psychology Prize)Psychology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Evelyne Debey, Maarten De Schryver, Gordon Logan, Kristina Suchotzki, Bruno Verschuere（比利时/荷兰/德国/加拿大/美国）🏅 Winners: Evelyne Debey, Maarten De Schryver, Gordon Logan, Kristina Suchotzki, and Bruno Verschuere (Belgium / The Netherlands / Germany / Canada / USA)
询问一千名骗子他们多久撒一次谎，并研究是否应该相信这些答案。
For asking a thousand liars how often they lie, and for deciding whether to believe those answers.
#07和平奖 (Peace Prize)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Gordon Pennycook, James Allan Cheyne, Nathaniel Barr, Derek Koehler, Jonathan Fugelsang（加拿大/美国）🏅 Winners: Gordon Pennycook, James Allan Cheyne, Nathaniel Barr, Derek Koehler, and Jonathan Fugelsang (Canada / USA)
发表了题为《论对伪深刻狗屁言论的接收与识别》的严谨学术研究。
For their scholarly psychological study titled 'On the Reception and Detection of Pseudo-Profound Bullshit.'
#08生物学奖 (Biology Prize)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Charles Foster 与 Thomas Thwaites（英国）🏅 Winners: Charles Foster and Thomas Thwaites (UK)
福斯特先后在野外像獾、水獭、鹿、狐狸和鸟一样生活；思韦茨则打造了四肢假肢延展装置，像山羊一样在山间与羊群共同生活。
For living in the wild at different times as a badger, otter, deer, fox, and bird, and for creating prosthetic limb extensions to roam hills in the company of goats.
#09文学奖 (Literature Prize)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：Fredrik Sjöberg（瑞典）🏅 Winners: Fredrik Sjöberg (Sweden)
撰写了三卷本自传体著作，记述自己收集已经死掉的苍蝇和还没死掉的苍蝇（食蚜蝇）的无穷乐趣。
For his three-volume autobiographical work about the pleasures of collecting flies that are dead, and flies that are not yet dead.
#10知觉奖 (Perception Prize)Perception Prize
🏅 获奖者：东山笃规（Atsuki Higashiyama）, 足立浩平（Kohei Adachi）（日本）🏅 Winners: Atsuki Higashiyama and Kohei Adachi (Japan)
研究当人弯下腰从自己两腿之间往后看时，事物的大小和距离看起来是否会与平时不同。
For investigating whether things look different in size and distance when you bend over and view them between your legs.

2017：猫咪流变学、怀抱鳄鱼的赌徒与雌雄颠倒的洞穴虫 2017: The Rheology of Liquid Cats, Crocodile-Holding Gamblers & Sex-Reversed Cave Insects

第27届盛典：用流体力学证明猫是液体，用吹管乐器拯救打鼾的夜晚 The 27th Ceremony: Proving Felines Are Both Solid and Liquid, and Treating Sleep Apnea with a Didgeridoo

📖 2017年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2017 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2017年第27届搞笑诺贝尔奖从铲屎官的日常困惑中提炼出了硬核物理。法国学者马克-安托万·法尔丁凭论文《论猫的流变学》夺得物理学奖：他引入流体力学的“底波拉数”，严谨证明只要给猫咪充足的松弛时间去适应酒杯、鱼缸或纸箱，成年猫就会像液体一样完美填满容器，从而既是固体又是液体。同样研究液体的韩国高中生韩智元则斩获流体动力学奖，他发现端着咖啡倒着走或从上方抓握杯口，能有效抑制步伐引发的液体晃动共振，终结了边走边洒咖啡的难题。

动物王国的饮食与婚恋内幕彻底颠覆了人类三观。日本与巴西学者吉泽和德、费雷拉等人荣获生物学奖，他们在巴西洞穴昆虫中首次发现雌雄生殖器倒置的奇观——雌虫长着带倒刺的阴茎状器官，交配时会伸入雄虫的阴道状体腔内长达数十小时，强行吸取富含营养的精包。巴西学者伊托团队则因营养学奖拉响警报：原本只吸鸟血的毛腿吸血蝠在森林遭侵占后，已开始夜间偷吸人血。而在澳大利亚，经济学奖得主洛克洛夫与格里尔通过实验证实，嗜赌者在抱过活鳄鱼后，会把恐惧带来的心跳加速误判为“手气正旺的兴奋”，从而在老虎机上疯狂加注。

医学与解剖学的镜头对准了从胎儿到老翁的身体奥秘。英国医生希思科特用尺子测量两百多名患者后获解剖学奖，证实人过三十岁后耳朵仍以每年零点二二毫米的速度持续变长，解开了“为什么老爷爷耳朵那么大”的谜题。西班牙产科学奖得主洛佩斯-特伊洪团队发现，把特制微型音箱塞进孕妇阴道内放音乐，胎儿在超声画面下张嘴吐舌头的反应远比隔着肚皮放音乐强烈。瑞士普汉团队则拿下和平奖，证明每天坚持吹奏澳洲原住民乐器迪吉里杜管能锻炼气道肌肉，有效缓解睡眠呼吸暂停与打鼾。

大脑深处的爱憎与自我认知同样耐人寻味。法国鲁瓦耶与蒋涛团队摘得医学奖，利用功能性磁共振成像测出讨厌奶酪的人闻到奶酪味时，大脑负责奖赏的腹侧苍白球竟反转成了表达生理厌恶的开关。意大利罗马大学的马尔蒂尼团队则捧起认知学奖，证明许多同卵双胞胎在看照片时缺乏自我面孔识别优势，常常分不清照片里究竟是自己还是双胞胎手足。

The 27th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony distilled hard-core rheology out of the internet's favorite feline memes. French physicist Marc-Antoine Fardin won the Physics Prize for his paper 'On the Rheology of Cats,' which deployed the dimensionless Deborah number—the ratio of a material's relaxation time to the observation time—to answer whether a cat can be both a solid and a liquid. Fardin demonstrated that while a cat observed over a split second bounces like an elastic solid, an adult cat given a few minutes to settle into a wine glass, sink basin, or shoebox flows to fill every corner like a true liquid. A fellow pioneer of everyday fluid mechanics, South Korean high-school student Jiwon Han, captured the Fluid Dynamics Prize for proving that walking backward while carrying a cup of coffee—or gripping the rim from above like a claw—dampens the biomechanically induced sloshing resonance that normally spills coffee over your shoes.

Across the animal kingdom, discoveries in diet, anatomy, and risk-taking turned conventional wisdom inside out. Japanese, Brazilian, and Swiss biologists Kazunori Yoshizawa, Rodrigo Ferreira, Yoshitaka Kamimura, and Charles Lienhard won the Biology Prize for discovering a cave-dwelling insect genus (*Neotrogla*) in which the female possesses an elaborate, barbed penis-like organ (*gynosome*) that penetrates the male's vagina-like chamber for up to 70 hours to forcibly extract nutritious seminal gifts. In Brazil, Fernanda Ito, Enrico Bernard, and Rodrigo Torres earned the Nutrition Prize for the first DNA-verified report that hairy-legged vampire bats—previously thought to feed exclusively on birds—have started sneaking human blood meals at night due to deforestation. Meanwhile, in Australia, Matthew Rockloff and Nancy Greer claimed the Economics Prize by having volunteers hold a live one-meter saltwater crocodile just before playing an electronic slot machine, revealing that problem gamblers misattribute terror-induced physiological arousal as 'lucky excitement' and place significantly larger bets.

Clinical medicine and anatomy zoomed in on the human body from womb to old age. British general practitioner James Heathcote received the Anatomy Prize for his classic study 'Why Do Old Men Have Big Ears?', measuring 206 patients to confirm that human ears continue elongating after age 30 at a steady clip of 0.22 millimeters per year—adding a full centimeter over half a century. Spanish obstetricians led by Marisa López-Teijón won the Obstetrics Prize for proving via ultrasound that a developing fetus responds with vigorous mouth-opening and tongue-sticking movements when music is broadcast electromechanically inside the mother's vagina (via their patented 'Babypod' speaker), whereas music played against the mother's abdomen barely registers. And a Swiss-led team headed by Milo Puhan and patient-inventor Alex Suarez won the Peace Prize for a randomized controlled trial proving that practicing the Australian Aboriginal didgeridoo strengthens upper-airway muscles and significantly reduces obstructive sleep apnea and disruptive snoring.

The final two prizes peered directly into the human brain to examine self-recognition and culinary revulsion. French and British neuroscientists Jean-Pierre Royet, Tao Jiang, and colleagues won the Medicine Prize for sliding cheese-haters into an fMRI scanner and discovering that the smell and sight of pungent cheese deactivate and repurpose the ventral pallidum—a core brain reward structure—into an active circuit of disgust. Finally, Italian and Spanish researchers led by Matteo Martini and Salvatore Maria Aglioti took the Cognition Prize for demonstrating that many identical twins lack the normal visual self-face recognition advantage, frequently struggling to tell whether a photograph shows their own face or that of their twin.

#01物理学奖 (Physics Prize)Physics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Marc-Antoine Fardin（法国/新加坡/美国）🏅 Winners: Marc-Antoine Fardin (France / Singapore / USA)
运用流体力学（流变学中的底波拉数）探讨“猫能不能既是固体又是液体”这一科学问题。
For using fluid dynamics and the Deborah number in rheology to probe the question 'Can a Cat Be Both a Solid and a Liquid?'
#02和平奖 (Peace Prize)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Milo Puhan, Alex Suarez, Christian Lo Cascio 等（瑞士/加拿大/荷兰/美国）🏅 Winners: Milo Puhan, Alex Suarez, Christian Lo Cascio, Alfred Zahn, Markus Heitz, and Otto Braendli (Switzerland / Canada / The Netherlands / USA)
证明定期吹奏澳大利亚原住民乐器迪吉里杜管（Didgeridoo）是治疗阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停综合征和打鼾的有效方法。
For demonstrating that regular playing of a didgeridoo is an effective treatment for obstructive sleep apnea and snoring.
#03经济学奖 (Economics Prize)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Matthew Rockloff, Nancy Greer（澳大利亚/美国）🏅 Winners: Matthew Rockloff and Nancy Greer (Australia / USA)
通过实验研究接触一条活生生的咸水鳄鱼会如何影响一个人的赌博下注意愿。
For their experiments investigating how holding a live saltwater crocodile affects a person's willingness to gamble on slot machines.
#04解剖学奖 (Anatomy Prize)Anatomy Prize
🏅 获奖者：James Heathcote（英国）🏅 Winners: James Heathcote (UK)
完成了题为《为什么老年男性的耳朵那么大？》的医学测量研究，证实人过30岁后耳朵每年约增长0.22毫米。
For his medical research study 'Why Do Old Men Have Big Ears?', confirming that human ears grow by roughly 0.22 mm per year after age 30.
#05生物学奖 (Biology Prize)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：吉泽和德（Kazunori Yoshizawa）, Rodrigo Ferreira, 上村佳孝（Yoshitaka Kamimura）, Charles Lienhard（日本/巴西/瑞士）🏅 Winners: Kazunori Yoshizawa, Rodrigo Ferreira, Yoshitaka Kamimura, and Charles Lienhard (Japan / Brazil / Switzerland)
在巴西洞穴昆虫（Neotrogla）中发现了雌性长有阴茎状器官、雄性长有阴道状体腔的生殖器反转现象。
For their discovery of a female penis and a male vagina in a Brazilian cave insect of the genus Neotrogla.
#06流体动力学奖 (Fluid Dynamics Prize)Fluid Dynamics Prize
🏅 获奖者：韩智元（Jiwon Han，韩国/美国）🏅 Winners: Jiwon Han (South Korea / USA)
研究液体晃动动力学，弄清了当一个人端着咖啡倒着走时为何能减少咖啡洒出。
For studying the dynamics of liquid-sloshing to learn what happens when a person walks backward while carrying a cup of coffee.
#07营养学奖 (Nutrition Prize)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：Fernanda Ito, Enrico Bernard, Rodrigo Torres（巴西/加拿大/西班牙）🏅 Winners: Fernanda Ito, Enrico Bernard, and Rodrigo Torres (Brazil / Canada / Spain)
发表了第一份在毛腿吸血蝠（原本只吸鸟血）日常饮食中检出人类血液的科学报告。
For the first scientific report of human blood appearing in the diet of the hairy-legged vampire bat (Diphylla ecaudata).
#08医学奖 (Medicine Prize)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Jean-Pierre Royet, David Meunier, Nicolas Torquet, Anne-Marie Mouly, 蒋涛（Tao Jiang）（法国/英国）🏅 Winners: Jean-Pierre Royet, David Meunier, Nicolas Torquet, Anne-Marie Mouly, and Tao Jiang (France / UK)
利用先进脑部扫描技术（fMRI）测量某些人对奶酪产生生理厌恶的神经机制。
For using advanced fMRI brain-scanning technology to measure the neural extent to which some people are disgusted by cheese.
#09认知学奖 (Cognition Prize)Cognition Prize
🏅 获奖者：Matteo Martini, Ilaria Bufalari, Maria Antonietta Stazi, Salvatore Maria Aglioti（意大利/西班牙/英国）🏅 Winners: Matteo Martini, Ilaria Bufalari, Maria Antonietta Stazi, and Salvatore Maria Aglioti (Italy / Spain / UK)
证明许多同卵双胞胎在视觉上无法准确分辨照片中的人究竟是自己还是双胞胎兄弟姐妹。
For demonstrating experimentally that many identical twins cannot tell themselves apart visually in photographs.
#10产科学奖 (Obstetrics Prize)Obstetrics Prize
🏅 获奖者：Marisa López-Teijón, Álex García-Faura, Alberto Prats-Galino, Luis Pallarés Aniorte（西班牙）🏅 Winners: Marisa López-Teijón, Álex García-Faura, Alberto Prats-Galino, and Luis Pallarés Aniorte (Spain)
证明发育中的人类胎儿对在母亲阴道内机电播放的音乐反应，比在母亲肚皮上播放音乐强烈得多。
For showing that a developing human fetus responds more strongly to music played electromechanically inside the mother's vagina than on the mother's belly.

2018：过山车排肾结石、扎上司巫毒小人与坐姿自我肠镜 2018: Kidney-Stone Roller Coasters, Boss Voodoo Dolls & Self-Administered Colonoscopies

第28届盛典：从邮票监测夜间勃起到坚决不读说明书的现代人 The 28th Ceremony: From Postage-Stamp Erection Tests to Why Nobody Ever Reads the Instruction Manual

📖 2018年度搞笑诺贝尔奖编年史正文 📖 2018 Ig Nobel Prize Chronicle Essay

2018年第28届搞笑诺贝尔奖把医疗诊室搬上了游乐场与自家马桶。美国泌尿科医生米切尔与瓦廷格斩获医学奖：受患者启发，他们用硅胶打印出装有尿液和三颗真结石的仿真肾脏，揣进背包去奥兰多迪士尼乐园连坐二十趟“巨雷山铁路”过山车，证实坐车尾排石率高达六成以上，远胜车头。同样追求极致的日本医生堀内朗则独揽医学教育奖，他坐在椅子上左手握操纵杆、右手把细口径结肠镜塞进自己肛门，连做四次坐姿自我肠镜，写出了令人肃然起敬的无痛自检指南。

在生殖医学与古人类食谱的角落里，科学家们算出了最精明的账目。美国医生巴里、布兰克和布瓦洛凭借1980年的经典研究摘得生殖医学奖：他们发明了廉价的“邮票勃起测试法”，只需睡前在男性阴茎上围一圈连体邮票，次日清晨看邮票齿孔是否被撑断，就能轻松鉴别器质性与心理性阳痿。英国考古学家詹姆斯·科尔则捧走营养学奖，他细致核算人体各器官的热量表后证明，吃人肉所能获取的卡路里远低于猛犸象、野猪甚至马肉，说明旧石器时代古人类同类相食绝非为了充饥，而是出于文化仪式动机。

感官与日常行为实验室里同样好戏连台。瑞典与德国的贝歇尔团队荣获生物学奖，证实哪怕只有一只雌性果蝇掉进葡萄酒杯，它释放的微量性信息素也足以让品酒大师仅凭嗅觉就当场识破。葡萄牙文物修复专家罗芒等人拿下化学奖，通过实验证明人类口水中的淀粉酶确实是清洁十八世纪镀金雕像与古画脏污表面的绝佳去污剂。而在动物园玻璃幕墙两侧，人类学奖得主佩尔松团队观察到，黑猩猩模仿人类游客拍手、敲窗和鬼脸的频率与水准，与人类游客模仿黑猩猩的表现不相上下。

现代职场、交通与消费生活的痛点在最后三项大奖中展露无遗。加拿大与中国的梁瀚予、廉慧文等学者斩获经济学奖，发现受恶毒上司欺凌的员工对着写有老板名字的巫毒娃娃扎针，能显著平复屈辱感、重获心理正义。西班牙阿隆索团队因系统测量司机开车时喊叫与咒骂的路怒症行为而获和平奖；澳大利亚布莱克勒团队则耗时七年拿下文学奖，用铁证道出了全人类的共同习惯——无论复杂电子产品功能多繁多，绝大多数人都绝不看使用说明书。

The 28th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony relocated medical science from the sterile hospital ward to the amusement park and the doctor's own chair. American osteopathic urologists Marc Mitchell and David Wartinger captured the Medicine Prize after patients repeatedly reported passing kidney stones following rides on Disney World's Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. To test the claim rigorously, the duo 3D-printed a transparent silicone renal model modeled on an actual patient's CT scan, filled it with urine and three real kidney stones of varying sizes, tucked it into a backpack, and rode the roller coaster 20 times—proving that sitting in the rear car yielded a whopping 63.89 percent stone-passage rate compared to just 16.67 percent in the front seat. Matching their dedication, Japanese gastroenterologist Akira Horiuchi won the Medical Education Prize for sitting upright in a chair, holding a small-caliber colonoscope controller in his left hand, and inserting the tube into his own rectum with his right hand four separate times to demonstrate the comfort of seated self-colonoscopy.

Ingenious frugal diagnostics and Paleolithic calorie-counting took home two more honors. American urologists John Barry, Bruce Blank, and Michel Boileau won the Reproductive Medicine Prize for their classic 1980 paper 'Nocturnal Penile Tumescence Monitoring With Stamps,' showing that wrapping a ring of joined postage stamps snugly around a sleeping man's penis overnight—and checking in the morning whether the perforations have been snapped—reliably distinguishes organic impotence from psychogenic erectile dysfunction at a fraction of sleep-lab costs. Meanwhile, British archaeologist James Cole earned the Nutrition Prize for calculating a comprehensive nutritional table of the human body, proving that a Paleolithic cannibalism diet provides significantly fewer calories than hunting mammoths, woolly rhinos, wild boars, or horses, and thus prehistoric cannibalism was likely driven by social or ritual motives rather than simple hunger.

Sensory acuity, conservation chemistry, and primate mimicry sparkled in the natural sciences. An international team led by Paul Becher, Sebastien Lebreton, and Peter Witzgall won the Biology Prize for demonstrating that professional wine experts can reliably detect by smell alone whether a single female fruit fly (*Drosophila melanogaster*) has fallen into a glass of wine, thanks to a nanogram-level sex pheromone (*Z4-11Al*) secreted by the female fly that ruins the bouquet. Portuguese conservation scientists Paula Romão, Adília Alarcão, and the late César Viana received the Chemistry Prize for quantifying what mothers and art restorers have long suspected: human saliva—powered by alpha-amylase enzymes—is a remarkably effective cleaning agent for dirty 18th-century gilded sculptures and painted surfaces. And at Furuvik Zoo, Anthropology Prize winners Tomas Persson, Gabriela-Alina Sauciuc, and Elainie Madsen documented that chimpanzees imitate human visitors' claps, window knocks, and grimaces just as frequently and skillfully as humans imitate the apes.

Finally, the frustrations of modern work, traffic, and consumer electronics received overdue scientific validation. Researchers Lindie Hanyu Liang, Douglas Brown, Huiwen Lian, and colleagues won the Economics Prize for proving that employees mistreated by an abusive supervisor feel a restored sense of psychological justice after sticking pins, pliers, and fire into a virtual Voodoo doll labeled with their boss's initials. Spanish traffic researchers led by Francisco Alonso earned the Peace Prize for systematically measuring how often—and why—motorists shout and curse behind the wheel. Rounding out the ceremony, Australian and UK ergonomists Thea Blackler, Rafael Gomez, Vesna Popovic, and M. Helen Thompson won the Literature Prize for their seven-year study 'Life Is Too Short to RTFM,' confirming experimentally that most people never read the instruction manual no matter how complicated a product is.

#01医学奖 (Medicine Prize)Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：Marc Mitchell, David Wartinger（美国）🏅 Winners: Marc Mitchell and David Wartinger (USA)
利用3D打印肾脏模型乘坐迪士尼过山车，检验并证实乘坐过山车（尤其是后排座位）能加速肾结石排出。
For using roller coaster rides with a 3D-printed renal model to test and hasten the passage of kidney stones.
#02人类学奖 (Anthropology Prize)Anthropology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Tomas Persson, Gabriela-Alina Sauciuc, Elainie Madsen（瑞典/罗马尼亚/丹麦/英国等）🏅 Winners: Tomas Persson, Gabriela-Alina Sauciuc, and Elainie Madsen (Sweden / Romania / Denmark / UK)
在动物园收集证据表明，黑猩猩模仿人类游客的频率和水平，与人类游客模仿黑猩猩的频率和水平旗鼓相当。
For collecting evidence in a zoo that chimpanzees imitate humans about as often, and about as well, as humans imitate chimpanzees.
#03生物学奖 (Biology Prize)Biology Prize
🏅 获奖者：Paul Becher, Sebastien Lebreton, Peter Witzgall 等（瑞典/哥伦比亚/德国/法国/瑞士）🏅 Winners: Paul Becher, Sebastien Lebreton, Peter Witzgall, et al. (Sweden / Colombia / Germany / France / Switzerland)
证明葡萄酒专家仅凭嗅觉就能可靠地鉴别出一杯葡萄酒里是否掉进过一只雌性果蝇。
For demonstrating that wine experts can reliably identify, by smell alone, the presence of a single female fruit fly in a glass of wine.
#04化学奖 (Chemistry Prize)Chemistry Prize
🏅 获奖者：Paula Romão, Adília Alarcão, 已故的 César Viana（葡萄牙）🏅 Winners: Paula Romão, Adília Alarcão, and the late César Viana (Portugal)
测量并证实人类唾液作为脏污表面（如古董镀金雕塑与油画）清洁剂的出色去污能力。
For measuring the degree to which human saliva is an effective cleaning agent for dirty surfaces and gilded sculptures.
#05医学教育奖 (Medical Education Prize)Medical Education Prize
🏅 获奖者：堀内朗（Akira Horiuchi，日本）🏅 Winners: Akira Horiuchi (Japan)
发表了题为《坐姿结肠镜检查：从自我结肠镜检查中学到的经验》的医学报告。
For his medical report 'Colonoscopy in the Sitting Position: Lessons Learned From Self-Colonoscopy.'
#06文学奖 (Literature Prize)Literature Prize
🏅 获奖者：Thea Blackler, Rafael Gomez, Vesna Popovic, M. Helen Thompson（澳大利亚/萨尔瓦多/英国）🏅 Winners: Thea Blackler, Rafael Gomez, Vesna Popovic, and M. Helen Thompson (Australia / El Salvador / UK)
记录并证实大多数使用复杂电子产品的人根本不阅读产品使用说明书。
For documenting over seven years that most people who use complicated products do not read the instruction manual ('Life Is Too Short to RTFM').
#07营养学奖 (Nutrition Prize)Nutrition Prize
🏅 获奖者：James Cole（英国/津巴布韦/坦桑尼亚）🏅 Winners: James Cole (UK / Zimbabwe / Tanzania)
计算出人类食人族饮食（吃人肉）所提供的卡路里热量显著低于大多数其他传统肉类饮食。
For calculating that the caloric intake from a human-cannibalism diet is significantly lower than the caloric intake from most other traditional meat diets.
#08和平奖 (Peace Prize)Peace Prize
🏅 获奖者：Francisco Alonso, Cristina Esteban 等（西班牙/哥伦比亚）🏅 Winners: Francisco Alonso, Cristina Esteban, et al. (Spain / Colombia)
测量人们在驾驶汽车时大喊大叫和咒骂（路怒症）的频率、动机及影响。
For measuring the frequency, motivation, and effects of shouting and cursing while driving an automobile.
#09生殖医学奖 (Reproductive Medicine Prize)Reproductive Medicine Prize
🏅 获奖者：John Barry, Bruce Blank, Michel Boileau（美国等）🏅 Winners: John Barry, Bruce Blank, and Michel Boileau (USA)
使用一圈连体邮票在睡前围住男性生殖器，以此监测夜间阴茎勃起功能是否正常。
For using a ring of postage stamps to test whether the male sexual organ is functioning properly overnight ('Nocturnal Penile Tumescence Monitoring With Stamps').
#10经济学奖 (Economics Prize)Economics Prize
🏅 获奖者：梁瀚予（Lindie Hanyu Liang）, Douglas Brown, 廉慧文（Huiwen Lian）等（加拿大/中国/新加坡/美国）🏅 Winners: Lindie Hanyu Liang, Douglas Brown, Huiwen Lian, Samuel Hanig, D. Lance Ferris, and Lisa Keeping (Canada / China / Singapore / USA)
研究员工使用巫毒娃娃（扎小人）来报复刻薄上司是否有助于恢复心理正义感。
For investigating whether it is effective for employees to use Voodoo dolls to retaliate against abusive bosses and restore a sense of justice.
